choices.text: An inference-time latency issue

title: Missing Values in Demand Time Series

choices.explanation: This helps distinguish a true zero from an unobserved value and choose an appropriate imputation policy.

title: A Primary Role of Generative AI
prompt: A communications team wants to create several draft product descriptions from a list of product features. Which AI role is the best fit?

choices.text: Delete existing records

title: Characteristics of foundation models
prompt: The team has not yet prepared training data for its specific business tasks, but wants a starting point for trying a broad range of natural language tasks. Which description of a foundation model is appropriate?

choices.text: A fixed set of rules trained only for one company
choices.explanation: A foundation model is not made up solely of fixed rules.

choices.text: A model pretrained on large amounts of broad data that serves as a foundation for various tasks
choices.explanation: Correct. Foundation models are pretrained on broad data and provide a starting point for diverse generative AI tasks.

choices.text: A model that can handle only one type of tabular data
choices.explanation: Some foundation models can handle different modalities, such as text and images.

choices.text: A model that cannot be used until training is completed at inference time
choices.explanation: An existing foundation model can be used for inference; additional training is not required.

source.label: What is Amazon Bedrock

title: Prompting for the desired response
prompt: You want a summarization assistant to produce three sentences in Japanese for executives, add a brief explanation for technical terms, and avoid speculation. What is the most appropriate first improvement?

choices.text: Explicitly state the intended audience, format, and constraints in the prompt
choices.explanation: Correct. Specifying the task, audience, format, and constraints helps elicit the desired response.

choices.text: Add random words without reading the input document
choices.explanation: Adding unrelated words does not clarify the requirements.

choices.text: Do not save the model's outputs, and repeat the same failure each time
choices.explanation: You cannot make useful comparisons to guide improvement.

choices.text: Leave the request blank and let the model infer the objective
choices.explanation: The constraints become unclear, making it harder to consistently get an output that meets the objective.

source.label: Amazon Bedrock prompt engineering concepts

learning.reason: A prompt gives instructions to the model; clarifying the objective, format, and constraints is a basic way to improve quality.
learning.concept: Improving a prompt does not change the model weights.

title: Recognizing plausible misinformation
prompt: An internal assistant gave the name of a nonexistent company policy and an article number in a confident tone. Which term best describes this phenomenon?

choices.text: Data compression
choices.explanation: This is a technique for reducing data size, not for generating plausible misinformation.

choices.text: Hallucination
choices.explanation: Correct. This is when a model plausibly generates content that is not factual.

choices.text: Horizontal scaling
choices.explanation: This is an infrastructure concept for increasing processing resources.

choices.text: Encryption
choices.explanation: This is a technique for protecting data, not a term for the accuracy of generated content.

source.label: AWS Prescriptive Guidance: Model hallucinations and output integrity

learning.reason: A hallucination is a phenomenon in which generative AI may produce inaccurate or fabricated content in a confident-sounding manner.
learning.concept: Fluency does not guarantee factual accuracy.

title: Why wording can vary for the same input
prompt: Even with the same summarization instruction and source text, a response may use slightly different wording or word order. Which explanation best describes this as a basic property of generative AI?

choices.text: Generation is probabilistic, so the output may not be unique for the same input
choices.explanation: Correct. Generative models produce probabilistic outputs, so wording may vary even for identical inputs.

choices.text: The model does not refer to the input at all
choices.explanation: Variation in output does not mean the model is ignoring the input.

choices.text: Generative AI cannot process text
choices.explanation: Text generation is a common use case.

choices.text: A malfunction in the user's device is always the cause
choices.explanation: Probabilistic generation is a property separate from device malfunctions.

source.label: Amazon Bedrock prompt engineering concepts

learning.reason: Because LLM generation is probabilistic, identical inputs do not necessarily produce exactly the same wording.
learning.concept: Output variation is not the same as failing to understand the input.

prompt: An insurance company wants to generate a review memo for its adjusters using both damage photos and a written accident description as input. Which model capability should it check first?

choices.explanation: The name of the storage destination does not determine the model's modality capabilities.

choices.text: The creation date of the IAM user
choices.explanation: This is an access management attribute, not a model input capability.

source.label: Amazon Bedrock models at a glance

learning.reason: When selecting a generative AI model, check that it supports the input and output modalities the task requires, such as text, images, or audio.
learning.concept: Multimodal support means the ability to handle data in multiple formats.

sourceLabel: Amazon Bedrock models at a glance

title: The Unit Generative AI Uses to Process Text
prompt: A team is considering whether a long input will fit within the range a model can process. What is the most appropriate basic unit for splitting and processing text in generative AI?

choices.text: Availability Zone
choices.explanation: This is an AWS infrastructure placement unit, not a text processing unit.

choices.text: Token

choices.text: Subnet

choices.text: Tag

source.label: Amazon Bedrock prompt design

title: What to Consider in a Long Conversation

choices.text: The amount of input and output that fits in the context window
choices.explanation: Correct. A model has limits on the input it can reference and the output it can generate in a single generation.

choices.text: The number of digits in the AWS account number

choices.explanation: This is a display property, not a model's context processing capacity.

title: A Task for Condensing a Long Document
prompt: An auditor wants to understand the key findings, risks, and next steps from a 50-page report in a short passage. Which generative AI task is the most direct fit?

choices.text: Image classification

title: Drafting Code from a Specification
prompt: A developer wants to describe input validation rules in prose and create an initial draft of a function that follows those conditions. Which is the most appropriate example of using generative AI?

choices.text: Drafting code
choices.explanation: Correct. Instructions to an LLM can generate a code draft from natural-language requirements.

choices.text: Automatically deleting a production database
choices.explanation: Generating a code draft is a different task from performing a destructive operational action.

choices.text: Eliminating the need for encryption

title: Separating Reference Text from Instructions
prompt: A query, reference text, and instructions about the response format were combined in one long passage, so the assistant treated part of the reference text as an instruction. What is a basic improvement to the prompt?

choices.text: Separate the instructions, input, and reference information with clear headings or delimiters
choices.explanation: Correct. Structuring content by its role makes it easier to clarify what the model should treat as an instruction.

choices.text: Delete the reference text and have the model guess its contents
choices.explanation: Removing necessary context makes it harder to get an accurate response.

choices.text: Omit all requirements for the response format
choices.explanation: The expected format would be unclear.

choices.text: Paste the same text repeatedly in an unrelated order
choices.explanation: Redundant repetition does not clarify the roles of the content.

source.label: Amazon Bedrock prompt engineering concepts

learning.reason: Structure prompts so the model can distinguish instructions, input, and context.
learning.concept: Prompt structuring improves the input; it is not additional model training.

title: Compare generation quality using representative inputs
prompt: You are choosing between two text-generation models. Both look natural in a general demo, but in practice you need to write polite replies to short complaint emails. Which comparison method is most appropriate?

choices.text: Prepare representative emails similar to the intended use and compare the outputs using the same evaluation criteria
choices.explanation: Correct. Evaluating with inputs and criteria close to the actual use makes it easier to justify the choice.

choices.text: Choose the model with the longer name
choices.explanation: A model's name length does not indicate its suitability for the task.

choices.explanation: That is not a quality comparison.

title: Search by both part number and description
prompt: Parts inquiries may include a sentence with an exact part number or a sentence describing the intended use in natural language. Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases uses a vector store in OpenSearch Serverless with a text field configured. Which setting lets search results reflect both exact part-number matches and semantic similarity to the description?

choices.text: Set the search type to HYBRID to search both text and embeddings.
choices.explanation: HYBRID combines text search with vector search. The store and field also meet the stated requirements.

choices.text: Set the search type to SEMANTIC and increase the number of results.
choices.explanation: SEMANTIC uses embeddings. Increasing the number of results does not make it a search type that also performs exact string matching on part numbers.

choices.text: Set an exact-match filter on part-number metadata and use the entire inquiry as the value.
choices.explanation: This would require the entire inquiry to match the part-number value, so it would not handle natural-language searches without a part number.

choices.text: Switch the model that generates responses and leave the search type unchanged.
choices.explanation: Changing the generation model does not change how search selects candidates.

source.label: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases の検索方式

learning.reason: To use both string matching and semantic similarity in the same search, specify hybrid search on a supported store.
learning.concept: Changing the search type affects candidate selection before an answer is generated.

sourceLabel: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases search types

title: Select the most relevant evidence from search candidates
prompt: In a RAG system for repair technicians, the 20 retrieved candidates include the correct procedure, but procedures for different equipment models rank higher. You must limit the evidence passed to the generation model to five items, and you cannot rebuild the search target or index. Which measure should you try next?

choices.text: Keep all 20 items and lower the output token limit.
choices.explanation: The output limit affects answer length. It does not change the ranking or number of evidence items passed to generation.

choices.text: Reduce the number of items retrieved in the initial search to five and pass them directly to generation.
choices.explanation: This would preserve the incorrect ranking, removing the correct procedure from sixth place or lower.

choices.text: Rerank the candidates by relevance to the inquiry and pass the top five to generation.
choices.explanation: Reranking reassesses the candidates already retrieved. It can increase the chance that the correct procedure in the candidate set moves up.

choices.text: Fine-tune the foundation model using only the latest repair documents.
choices.explanation: Model training is different from changing the ranking of retrieved candidates. It also does not meet the requirement to limit the evidence to five items.

source.label: Amazon Bedrock の再ランキング

learning.reason: Because the initial search includes the correct evidence, reassess relevance to the query before discarding candidates.
learning.concept: A reranker cannot add documents that are not in the candidate set.

title: Use only the explicitly selected version as evidence
prompt: Older and current versions of an equipment manual are stored in the same knowledge base. The version is recorded in each document's metadata, and users select a version on the screen. How can you limit the candidates used for an answer to only the selected version?

choices.text: Write “Use only the selected version” in the answer prompt.
choices.explanation: This gives an instruction at generation time but cannot exclude other versions at the retrieval-candidate stage.

choices.text: Apply an equality filter at retrieval time to the version in the document metadata.
choices.explanation: Search can be limited to documents whose metadata matches the version entered by the user.

choices.text: Set the number of retrieved items to one and keep only the document with the highest similarity.
choices.explanation: High similarity does not guarantee a version match. If the old and new versions have similar content, a nonselected version could still rank highest.

choices.text: Set the generation temperature to its minimum.
choices.explanation: This is a generation-time sampling setting and does not change the document retrieval conditions.

source.label: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases のメタデータフィルター

learning.reason: Because the input determines which version is correct, filter candidate documents by an equality condition on their metadata.
learning.concept: Known attributes that must match exactly, such as version or language, can constrain retrieval.

title: Reflecting Revised Documents in Search
prompt: A revised internal procedure has been uploaded to a Bedrock Knowledge Base that uses Amazon S3 as its data source. Even after restarting the application, searches still return the previous procedure, and the data source was last synchronized before the upload. What should you do first?

choices.explanation: This configures inference capacity; it does not ingest S3 documents into the search index.

choices.text: Increase the maximum response length so subsequent chunks can be displayed.
choices.explanation: Response length sets a generation limit; it does not replace the outdated search data.

choices.text: Point the search application to a foundation model in another Region.

choices.text: Synchronize the Knowledge Base's S3 data source and check the ingestion job results.
choices.explanation: Synchronizing the data source ingests updated data and reflects it in the search index.

source.label: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases のデータソース同期

learning.reason: Uploading a file to S3 and ingesting it into a Knowledge Base are separate steps. An ingestion job reflects changes made since the last synchronization.
learning.concept: When checking whether the latest documents can be retrieved, first check the index update time and ingestion results before changing the foundation model.

sourceLabel: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases data source synchronization

title: Measuring Unsupported Statements
prompt: You are evaluating a product FAQ before publication. You want to distinguish answers that include information not supported by the supplied materials, even when that product information happens to be correct. Which Bedrock LLM evaluation metric directly measures faithfulness to the materials?

choices.text: Correctness
choices.explanation: This measures whether an answer is correct. Correctness alone does not show whether the answer is grounded in the supplied materials.

choices.text: Faithfulness
choices.explanation: This measures whether an answer adds information that is not in the supplied context, matching the property you want to assess.

choices.text: Helpfulness
choices.explanation: This measures an answer's clarity, completeness, and usefulness. An answer can seem useful even when it includes detailed information absent from the materials.

choices.text: Logical coherence
choices.explanation: This evaluates consistency within an answer. An internally consistent answer can still add information absent from the materials.

source.label: Amazon Bedrock のモデル評価指標

learning.reason: Whether content is correct and whether it is supported by the supplied context are distinct things to measure.
learning.concept: Use faithfulness as the primary metric, and track correctness separately if needed.

title: Balancing Two Types of Errors
prompt: In equipment failure prediction, both missed failures and unnecessary maintenance recommendations are costly. You want to compare candidate models using a single value that balances positive-class precision and recall. Which metric is most appropriate?

title: Changing the Classification Threshold

title: Numeric Features with Different Scales
prompt: A distance-based model classifies warehouse candidates using delivery distance in meters and operational priority on a scale of 1 to 5. title: Reliable Comparison with Limited Data
prompt: There is little labeled data for a rare disease, and a single validation split is highly susceptible to chance imbalance. You want to compare candidate models across multiple splits and use every observation for evaluation. Which evaluation method is appropriate?

choices.text: Use Amazon SageMaker Canvas to build a tabular model.

choices.text: Sentiment analysis in Amazon Comprehend

title: A Quick Trial Starting with a Pretrained Model
prompt: A small team wants to assess the potential of image classification in a few days. Before training a model from scratch with a large dataset, it wants to use a pretrained model as a starting point. Which SageMaker AI feature is the best fit?

title: Feature Mismatch Between Training and Production
prompt: A purchase prediction model achieved high accuracy during development using a “date of last purchase” column, but the production API does not provide that column. Which two actions should be taken before deployment?

choices.text: Skip evaluation and deploy directly to all users.
choices.explanation: This would not detect a performance drop caused by the mismatch.

choices.text: Provide the ground-truth label as an input in production.
choices.explanation: Ground-truth labels are generally unavailable at prediction time.

choices.text: Train and evaluate using only features available in production.
choices.explanation: This removes dependence on information that cannot be reproduced from production inputs.

choices.explanation: This does not reproduce the meaning of the training data or guarantee performance.

choices.explanation: This can reveal missing inputs or differences in how features are calculated before deployment.

source.label: SageMaker AI のMLワークフロー

learning.reason: Train and evaluate using features that can be reproduced in production and the same rules for generating them.
learning.concept: A mismatch between training and inference inputs can reduce performance after release.

title: Signs That Retraining Should Be Considered
prompt: For a price prediction model, a change in the input data distribution and a sustained increase in errors against ground-truth labels obtained later have both been observed. What is the most appropriate next action?

choices.text: Keep the model and disable quality metric alarms because the live data format is correct.
choices.explanation: Performance against labels can deteriorate even when the schema is correct.

choices.text: Reevaluate the model on recent representative examples, and retrain a candidate if needed, then validate it under current conditions.
choices.explanation: Because both input distribution and performance against ground-truth labels have degraded, testing with post-change data can show whether the model improves.

choices.text: Rescore the current model on the validation set used during training and keep it if its error matches the earlier result.
choices.explanation: This measures performance only under old conditions and cannot determine whether performance on current inputs has deteriorated.

choices.text: Train a candidate on a subset of recent inputs and replace the production model without comparison.
choices.explanation: This might fit the recent distribution, but there is no way to confirm that performance improved after the change.

source.label: Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor

learning.reason: Use evidence of drift and declining quality to consider reevaluation and retraining.
learning.concept: Retraining is not automatically the right choice. Decide whether to update based on new data and independent validation.

title: Reduce Handling Time with Draft Assistance
prompt: An insurance company wants to reduce the time representatives spend reading customer emails and drafting replies. Representatives will continue to decide whether to send each reply. What is the most appropriate generative AI use case?

choices.text: Automatically send only approved templates and continue handling free-form inquiries as before.
choices.explanation: This automates some cases but does not draft replies to free-form inquiries while preserving the representative’s decision to send them.

choices.text: Have generative AI write and send replies, then let representatives sample sent emails for review.
choices.explanation: This reduces drafting time, but representatives no longer make the decision before a message reaches the customer.

choices.text: Use generative AI to draft replies, then have representatives review the content and recipient before sending.
choices.explanation: This shortens drafting time while leaving the send decision with the representative.

title: Reduce Operational Overhead for a Generative AI Platform

choices.explanation: This can manage compute resources, but it still requires a container and differs from calling a foundation model directly through an interactive experimentation interface.

title: Choosing an Inference Option for Unpredictable Trial Usage
prompt: A new internal assistant processes requests during conversations, but its daily usage is not yet predictable. The candidate model supports both on-demand inference and a capacity-reservation option. Which option should you choose during the trial to avoid committing to fixed capacity?

choices.text: Use Amazon Bedrock on-demand inference and do not reserve fixed capacity until actual usage has been measured.
choices.explanation: It can handle requests as usage occurs, without requiring you to keep model units reserved at this stage.

choices.text: Batch users' questions and submit them for batch inference at the end of each day.
choices.explanation: This can work when immediate responses are unnecessary, but it does not meet the requirement to process requests during a conversation.

choices.text: Keep model inference running on a dedicated GPU instance, reserving it even when no requests arrive.
choices.explanation: It can handle interactive requests, but it keeps fixed compute resources allocated during periods of no usage.

learning.reason: When demand is still unpredictable, on-demand usage may be a better fit than reserving fixed capacity.

title: Reserving Capacity for Steady, High Demand

title: Choosing Inference for Nonurgent, High-Volume Work

title: Selecting a Model That Meets Language Requirements

title: Search precisely, return broader context

title: Switch prompts safely

choices.explanation: This continues training the model on unlabeled documents to adapt it to the industry's language and style.

source.label: Amazon Bedrockの基盤モデルのカスタマイズ

learning.reason: Continued pretraining fits the requirement to adapt the model itself using unlabeled text.
learning.concept: Supervised fine-tuning teaches specific responses using answer pairs, so it requires different training data.

sourceLabel: Customizing Foundation Models in Amazon Bedrock

title: Transfer a Larger Model's Output Behavior to a Smaller Model
prompt: For a product-attribute organization task, an existing large model produces sufficiently good output, but processing every product takes too much time and costs too much. You can generate response examples from the large model for the target task, and a compatible smaller model is available. How can you use the smaller model while preserving the output behavior?

choices.text: Use the large model as the teacher and distill the smaller model on response examples for the target task.
choices.explanation: This lets the smaller model learn the teacher model's task-specific behavior.

choices.text: Lower the temperature of the large model and continue using that same large model.
choices.explanation: This changes the output distribution but does not transfer processing to a smaller model.

choices.text: Use the smaller model without referring to the large model's outputs, and add only a knowledge base.
choices.explanation: Reference documents can be provided, but this does not teach the smaller model the teacher's output behavior.

choices.text: Pretrain a foundation model from scratch at the same computational scale as the large model.
choices.explanation: This does not move the task to a smaller model or make use of the existing teacher, and it requires substantial compute resources.

source.label: Amazon Bedrockのモデル蒸留

learning.reason: The large model's outputs serve as training examples that teach the smaller student model the target task.
learning.concept: Evaluate the distilled model on an independent evaluation set to confirm that it meets the required quality and processing-efficiency targets.

title: Measure Retrieval Improvements Separately from Generation Quality
prompt: You are comparing two indexes in Bedrock Knowledge Bases. The foundation model and the total number of results are the same, but you want to measure only whether retrieval finds the evidence needed. The quality of the generated text is outside the scope of this evaluation. Which setting is appropriate?

choices.text: Generate answers from both indexes and compare only the usefulness of the final answers.
choices.explanation: This includes the effects of both retrieval and generation, so it cannot compare evidence retrieval alone.

choices.text: Run a retrieve-only RAG evaluation using the same representative query set.
choices.explanation: This measures whether both indexes retrieve the relevant information needed, separately from answer generation.

choices.text: Compare the number of output tokens from the same foundation model.
choices.explanation: Output length does not show whether the retrieved results contain the necessary evidence.

choices.text: Run only the model without retrieving information and compare its answers with the correct answers.
choices.explanation: The indexes are not used, so retrieval differences are not included in the evaluation.

source.label: Bedrockの取得専用RAG評価

learning.reason: A retrieve-only evaluation targets evidence retrieval and leaves generation effects out of scope.
learning.concept: Investigate separately whether evidence could not be found and whether an answer failed to use evidence that was found.

title: Track Wording Overlap with Reference Summaries
prompt: Each week, evaluate automated summaries for routine reports using the same data as approved reference summaries. First, you want a metric based on overlap in words or phrases; the impact on review time and factuality will be evaluated separately. Which metric and interpretation are appropriate?

choices.text: Use cost-effectiveness amounts to determine how much terminology overlaps with the reference summaries.
choices.explanation: Cost-effectiveness measures business outcomes, not wording.

choices.text: Use the number of generation requests to measure the recall of phrases from the reference summaries.
choices.explanation: The number of requests reflects usage frequency, not content overlap.

choices.text: Use ROUGE to measure wording overlap with the reference summaries.
choices.explanation: ROUGE makes it straightforward to evaluate wording overlap automatically. Factuality and work efficiency require separate evaluation.

choices.text: Measure whether the full answers have the same character count and treat that as wording overlap.
choices.explanation: The same character count does not mean that the content or wording is the same.

source.label: AIF-C01公式ガイドの基盤モデル評価

learning.reason: ROUGE can compare wording overlap with a reference summary, but it does not measure business efficiency or all aspects of factuality.
learning.concept: Keep text metrics separate from business outcomes, and do not interpret a metric beyond what it measures.

sourceLabel: Foundation Model Evaluation in the Official AIF-C01 Guide

title: When an Evaluator Consistently Prefers the First Candidate
prompt: An LLM-as-a-judge frequently reverses its verdict when responses A and B are presented in the opposite order, even though their content is unchanged. Select two ways to check for and reduce the effect of order bias while keeping the evaluation criteria consistent.

choices.text: Always place the longer response first.
choices.explanation: This ties order to response length, making it hard to tell which affected the verdict.

choices.text: Change the evaluation rubric every time you reverse the order of the same pair.
choices.explanation: Changing both position and criteria prevents you from comparing the effect of order alone.

choices.text: Have a person review representative cases whose verdict changes with presentation order, using the same criteria.
choices.explanation: This allows results that may be affected by order to be checked independently instead of accepted without question.

choices.text: Extend the evaluation timeout and keep only verdicts that select the first response.
choices.explanation: More processing time does not reduce a bias toward the response presented first.

choices.text: Evaluate the same pair in both A→B and B→A order, then aggregate the results using the same criteria.
choices.explanation: This measures differences caused by position without changing the content or always putting the same model first.

source.label: LLM-as-a-judgeの位置バイアスの実証研究

learning.reason: Keep the content fixed, vary only presentation order, and hold other conditions constant to identify position bias. A person can review cases whose verdicts are unstable.
learning.concept: Even when the same model performs automated evaluations, check their validity using controlled comparisons and human review.

sourceLabel: Empirical Study of Position Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge

title: Do Response Quality Scores Translate into Business Outcomes?
prompt: The goal of introducing an internal support AI is to let employees resolve inquiries without handing them off to a person. Its written answers receive high ratings, but many users ask again immediately after receiving an answer. Which metric evaluates the goal of the deployment?

choices.text: Average number of tokens per output
choices.explanation: This measures answer length but does not show whether an inquiry was resolved.

choices.text: Average wording similarity to approved answers
choices.explanation: This can score model outputs but does not track repeat inquiries or handoffs.

choices.text: Number of chat sessions started per user
choices.explanation: This measures usage, but the value can increase when users start sessions repeatedly for the same issue.

choices.text: The proportion of inquiries resolved within a defined period without a repeat inquiry about the same case or a handoff to a support agent
choices.explanation: This directly measures whether the inquiry was resolved without human assistance, as intended.

source.label: AIF-C01公式ガイドのビジネス目標と基盤モデル評価

learning.reason: Define resolution in terms of no repeat inquiry about the same case and no handoff to a support agent within a defined period.
learning.concept: High answer-quality ratings do not guarantee that users' issues are resolved; measure the proportion of cases that are resolved.

sourceLabel: Business Goals and Foundation Model Evaluation in the AIF-C01 Official Guide

title: Validate JSON Structure Before Passing It to a Downstream Process
prompt: Generated product information will be used as input to another API. Evaluation shows that even text that looks like the requested JSON can be missing required keys or contain values of disallowed types. The current model, which does not support structured output, must remain in use. What should be done before submitting the output?

choices.text: Specify the desired structure in the prompt, then parse the output and pass it on only if it conforms to the schema.
choices.explanation: Combining format instructions during generation with mechanical validation prevents nonconforming output from reaching the downstream process.

choices.text: Submit the output to the API only if it starts with an opening brace.
choices.explanation: Checking only the first character cannot establish that the output is valid JSON or has the required keys and types.

choices.text: Lower the temperature and pass every generated output on without checking it.
choices.explanation: This can reduce variation, but it does not guarantee that every response conforms to the schema.

choices.text: Let the downstream API handle type mismatches and check only for required keys before submission.
choices.explanation: This does not verify that the input meets the required types before it is submitted.

source.label: Amazon BedrockのJSONスキーマによる出力制約

learning.reason: Specify the format in the prompt, then parse the actual response and validate required fields and types against the schema.
learning.concept: Parsable JSON may still fail the constraints of its intended use. Format instructions and runtime validation serve different purposes.

sourceLabel: Constrained Output with JSON Schemas in Amazon Bedrock

title: Link Citations in an Answer to Their Source Material
prompt: An internal FAQ answer must show the document passages used as supporting evidence. You are using RetrieveAndGenerate in Bedrock Knowledge Bases and must not list every retrieved candidate as a source. Which information should you use?

choices.text: The model API request ID as the source link
choices.explanation: This helps track a request but does not show where the supporting material is located.

choices.text: Use the `retrievedReferences` associated with citations in the response and each reference’s `location`.
choices.explanation: This lets you retrieve the references associated with citations in the answer.

choices.text: Ask the generation model to append plausible reference URLs without showing it the documents.
choices.explanation: Generated links may have no connection to the materials actually referenced.

choices.text: List the URLs of every file included in the index.
choices.explanation: This lists the indexed materials but does not identify which ones were used in the answer.

source.label: Bedrockの取得・生成結果と引用情報

learning.reason: Link citations in the answer to the corresponding retrieved references.
learning.concept: Sources can help users verify an answer, but displaying links alone does not guarantee that generated text aligns with the cited material.

sourceLabel: Bedrock Retrieval and Generation Results and Citation Information

title: Make the search index available for a new portal
prompt: Using an empty vector store and an embedding model, you are preparing to start semantic search across product records. Unprocessed documents are in S3, and the internal portal will return excerpts from source text that are relevant to a question. Order the batch steps according to their data dependencies.

choices.text: Register the chunk vectors in the vector store together with references to their source documents.
choices.explanation: After converting the documents to vectors, save them in the index so they can be searched.

choices.text: Split the product documents into chunks of a searchable size.
choices.explanation: First, divide the documents into units that can be returned as search results.

choices.text: Embed a question and return similar chunks from the prepared index.
choices.explanation: Once the document-side preparation is complete, similarity search can be performed for a question.

choices.text: Convert the chunks into vectors with the embedding model.
choices.explanation: Convert each chunk into a numerical representation before adding it to the index.

source.label: Bedrockナレッジベースのデータ処理

learning.reason: Once chunks are created, they can be embedded; once the vectors are stored, a question vector can be used to search them.
learning.concept: Ingestion-time data processing and query-time search are separate stages.

title: Differences in counts and label rates before training
prompt: There are 800 vocational training recommendation records from Region A and 200 from Region B. Only historical data is in scope, and the model has not been trained. You want to distinguish the difference in record counts from the difference in the proportion recorded as recommended. Choose two appropriate measures.

choices.text: Use the regional false positive rate for the difference in the proportion recorded as recommended.
choices.explanation: A false positive rate requires model outputs and ground-truth labels; it is different from the label rate before training.

choices.text: Use Class Imbalance for the difference in record counts by region.
choices.explanation: It can measure the imbalance in the number of data records belonging to each region.

choices.text: Use the difference in positive prediction rates for the difference in record counts by region.
choices.explanation: Because the model is untrained, predictions are not available; the positive prediction rate also differs from the number of records in each region.

choices.text: Use Class Imbalance for the difference in the proportion recorded as recommended.
choices.explanation: This measure compares the number of records in each region; it does not distinguish the share carrying the recommended label.

choices.text: Use Difference in Proportions of Labels for the difference in the proportion recorded as recommended.
choices.explanation: For training data, this can compare the share of the same target label across regions.

source.label: SageMaker Clarifyの学習前バイアス指標

learning.reason: The difference in record counts between regions and the label proportion within each region are different quantities and cannot substitute for each other.
learning.concept: Class Imbalance compares group counts, while Difference in Proportions of Labels compares the proportions carrying the target label.

title: Human review only for uncertain readings of a critical field
prompt: A company that already uses Amazon A2I processes contracts with Amazon Textract. It wants human review only when the confidence in the contract number text is below a threshold. The reading accuracy of other form fields is not part of the review condition for this task. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Target the contract number in A2I and start a review based on the confidence range for the text.
choices.explanation: This combines targeting a specific key with evaluating confidence in the text contained in the key or value.

choices.text: Have the application find the lowest word confidence on the page and use that value to review all fields.
choices.explanation: Review would also start for a page with hard-to-read text in another field, so it would not be limited to the contract number.

choices.text: In A2I, start a review whenever the contract number key is found, regardless of text confidence.
choices.explanation: A key-detection condition can be configured, but this would also send readings above the threshold for human review.

choices.text: Target the contract number in A2I and start a review based only on confidence in identifying the key-value pair.
choices.explanation: Even if the key-value pair is identified, the text in the value may still have been recognized inaccurately.

source.label: Amazon A2IとAmazon Textractの連携

learning.reason: Limit A2I activation conditions to the contract number field, then trigger human review based on confidence in reading its value.
learning.concept: Confidence that a key-value pair was detected in a form can be evaluated separately from confidence in the characters within the key or value.

sourceLabel: Amazon A2I and Amazon Textract integration

title: Sampling high-confidence readings for quality checks
prompt: An existing Amazon A2I review workflow routes only low-confidence documents for review. Reviewers want to detect misreadings that slip through at high confidence while keeping the confidence-based routing condition and limiting routine review volume. What should they add?

choices.text: Lower the existing threshold for routing low-confidence documents.
choices.explanation: The documents sent for human review would be limited to those with confidence lower than before.

choices.text: Add a small random sample alongside the existing condition and aggregate the review results by confidence level.
choices.explanation: This makes high-confidence results more likely to be sampled while preserving the existing low-confidence review condition.

choices.text: Send every high-confidence document for human review.
choices.explanation: This could detect the desired misreadings, but would not meet the requirement to limit routine review volume.

choices.text: Randomly select documents already routed because of low confidence and ask another person to judge them again.
choices.explanation: This can assess the consistency of low-confidence results, but high-confidence misses will not be included in the sample.

source.label: Amazon A2IのTextract向け条件とランダムサンプリング

learning.reason: Adding a sample selected independently of confidence lets reviewers inspect documents that do not meet the low-confidence condition.
learning.concept: When the goal is to detect high-confidence misses, do not determine audit samples based on confidence alone.

sourceLabel: Amazon A2I conditions for Textract and random sampling

title: Explaining an individual prediction
prompt: The weekly report for a delivery-delay model includes feature importance aggregated across all predictions. When a specific package is predicted to be delayed, a support representative wants to see how that package’s input fields contributed to the prediction. Which information should they use?

choices.text: Use only the top aggregated SHAP features across all predictions to explain one case.
choices.explanation: Aggregated results do not show how this package’s features moved the prediction.

choices.text: Use the label frequencies of training samples similar to this package.
choices.explanation: This shows outcomes for similar samples but does not calculate each input field’s contribution to the current model prediction.

choices.text: Use local SHAP values for this package’s input.
choices.explanation: Local explanation values can show each feature’s contribution to the prediction for the specified input.

choices.text: Use the model’s accuracy for that week.
choices.explanation: This is an aggregate measure of prediction quality and cannot explain each field’s contribution.

source.label: SageMaker Clarifyの説明可能性分析結果

learning.reason: For a single case, refer to local feature contributions for that input.
learning.concept: Aggregated importance describes overall trends, which differ from feature contributions for one case.

title: Aligning the reference for explanations
prompt: Two representatives produce different SHAP explanations for the same application and prediction model. Representative A uses representative values from the training data as the background, while representative B uses a background made from values close to empty. What should they standardize so that they can compare their explanations?

choices.text: Use the same classification threshold while keeping each representative’s background.
choices.explanation: The model’s decision threshold does not resolve differences in the SHAP reference background.

choices.text: Remove the signs of the SHAP values and compare only their absolute values.
choices.explanation: Differences in contribution magnitude caused by the background would remain, and the direction of each contribution would be lost.

choices.text: Divide each representative’s SHAP values by the prediction probability and compare them.
choices.explanation: Normalizing by prediction probability does not eliminate differences in the background used to replace features.

choices.text: Define a shared SHAP baseline suited to the use case, then recalculate both explanations under the same conditions.
choices.explanation: Aligning the reference and calculation conditions removes differences caused by using different backgrounds.

source.label: SageMaker ClarifyのSHAPベースライン

learning.reason: SHAP compares features with reference values, so changing the background can change how contributions are interpreted.
learning.concept: Even when the prediction being compared is the same, use the same background and method to compare feature contributions.

title: Deciding whether to reuse a model outside its evaluated scope
prompt: A company proposes using its internal invoice classification model at a new site. The language and formats will differ, but the current model card records evaluation results only for documents from the original site. Which material is appropriate to inform the decision before reuse?

choices.text: Evaluate representative data from the new site and record the use case, limitations, and results in the model card.
choices.explanation: This makes measured results for the target site and the applicable scope clear to reviewers.

choices.text: Add the name of the new site to the model card and display only the current evaluation results.
choices.explanation: The evaluated languages and formats may not be the same, and adding a site name alone does not show quality at the new site.

choices.text: Treat the inference endpoint’s uptime at the new site as its accuracy there.
choices.explanation: Endpoint availability does not measure whether documents in another language and format are classified correctly.

choices.text: Reuse only aggregate results from the original site for the risk assessment, without distinguishing sites.
choices.explanation: This does not reveal whether quality declines under the new conditions.

source.label: SageMaker Model Cardsの用途・評価記録

learning.reason: Use the current documentation to identify what has not been evaluated, then record an evaluation representative of the new site together with the use case and limitations.
learning.concept: A model card communicates known evaluation results and their applicable scope; it does not certify an unevaluated use.

sourceLabel: SageMaker Model Cards use cases and evaluation records

title: Monitoring fairness during production
prompt: A company already uses SageMaker Model Monitor. At launch, the difference in positive offer-prediction rates across membership groups was within the acceptable range. The team wants to be notified if that difference widens during operation. Which monitoring should they use?

choices.text: Use Model Monitor to monitor schema violations across all inputs.
choices.explanation: Even when the schema is valid, the difference in positive prediction rates by membership group can change.

choices.text: Configure Clarify bias drift monitoring in the existing environment and calculate the target metric regularly.
choices.explanation: CloudWatch can send a notification when the metric for production predictions falls outside the acceptable range.

choices.text: Distribute only the pre-training bias report created at launch each week.
choices.explanation: Reading a report based on the same training data cannot detect new prediction bias arising in production.

choices.text: Monitor the average positive prediction rate across all model users.
choices.explanation: The average may change very little even when differences between groups grow.

source.label: SageMaker Clarifyの本番バイアス監視

learning.reason: Continuously calculate the target metric for the model’s production predictions and notify the team when it falls outside the acceptable range.
learning.concept: Fairness in production is not fixed at launch; measure the target metric using production inputs and predictions.

title: An answer that is grounded in the source but does not answer the question
prompt: A policy RAG application receives a question and supporting source excerpts, then generates the full answer before displaying it to the user. Because it may extract a correct sentence from an irrelevant paragraph, it must not display an answer that is supported by the source but unrelated to the question. What should it use?

choices.text: Raise only the grounding threshold.
choices.explanation: This checks whether the answer is supported by the source, but whether it is relevant to the question is a separate measure.

choices.text: Add words commonly found in irrelevant paragraphs to a word filter.
choices.explanation: This could also block relevant answers containing the same words. It cannot measure the semantic relationship between the question and the answer.

choices.text: Pass the supporting source and the question to a contextual grounding check, and configure a relevance threshold.
choices.explanation: It evaluates relevance to the question separately from grounding and can exclude answers that do not meet the threshold.

choices.text: Add dangerous subjects to denied topics.
choices.explanation: This can block subjects that must not be discussed, but cannot distinguish an unrelated answer about an allowed subject.

source.label: Amazon Bedrockのコンテキストグラウンディングチェック

learning.reason: Assess support from the source and relevance to the user's question with separate scores, then apply a relevance threshold.
learning.concept: Stating something found in a source and answering the question are separate quality requirements.

title: Validate an English policy response with formal rules
prompt: An English-language benefits explanation determines an amount according to several conditions in an internal policy. The application can assemble the full response before sending it. You want to formalize the policy, identify which rules a response violates, and route it for regeneration or human review. What should you use?

choices.text: Add the amounts in the policy to Denied topics and automatically correct any displayed amount.
choices.explanation: Denied topics detect subjects; they do not validate the formulas for benefit conditions or correct amounts.

choices.text: Measure accuracy on test data, then skip checking individual responses before sending them.
choices.explanation: This can measure average quality in advance, but it cannot determine which rule a particular response violates.

choices.text: Retrieve the policy sentence with the highest embedding similarity and use that similarity as proof that the amount is valid.
choices.explanation: This finds a relevant policy passage but does not perform an exact check against a value derived from multiple conditions.

choices.text: Represent the policy as an Automated Reasoning policy, then have the application process the results of checking the full response before displaying it.
choices.explanation: Formal logic evaluates consistency with the policy, and the application can use the structured results to hold or correct the response.

source.label: Amazon Bedrock GuardrailsのAutomated Reasoningチェック

learning.reason: Automated Reasoning checks the logical consistency of a response against an explicit policy, and the application can handle the result.
learning.concept: The check is effective within the scope of the defined policy, and the application needs to interpret its results before sending the response.

sourceLabel: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails Automated Reasoning checks

title: Mask email addresses in a conversation summary for sharing
prompt: A generated summary for a support agent will also be shared with another department. You want to keep the body of the summary and replace only detected email addresses in the response using an evaluated masking feature. Which setting is appropriate?

choices.text: In the sensitive information filter for generated output, specify the email address type and configure the Mask action.
choices.explanation: Only detected portions of the specified type are anonymized in the result, leaving the rest of the text available for use.

choices.text: Set the sensitive information filter to Block for email addresses.
choices.explanation: This blocks the output when the target is detected, so the rest of the generated body cannot be shared as is.

choices.text: Shorten the output length to leave less room for an email address.
choices.explanation: A short response can still contain an email address. This does not meet the detection and replacement requirements.

choices.text: Specify “email” in Denied topics, then share the original summary from the filter result.
choices.explanation: The subject of a conversation and the presence of an email address are different. Sharing the original response leaves the address in it.

source.label: Amazon Bedrock Guardrailsの機密情報フィルター

learning.reason: The requirement is to hide only the specified type of detected information, not to block the entire summary.
learning.concept: You can choose the personal information type to detect and whether to block or anonymize it when detected.

sourceLabel: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails sensitive information filters

title: Distinguish general information from personalized investment advice
prompt: A public relations chatbot may provide general information about financial products, but it must not recommend a portfolio allocation tailored to an individual user. The same product names can appear in both types of response, and personalized advice can be phrased in many ways. How should you configure this boundary in Guardrails?

choices.text: Add all relevant financial product names to a word filter.
choices.explanation: This would also block permitted general information that uses those product names and cannot distinguish it from a personalized recommendation involving the same names.

choices.text: Define the topic of individually recommending portfolio allocations as a denied topic, and evaluate it using boundary examples.
choices.explanation: This defines the meaning of the prohibited recommendation and supports evaluation without relying only on matching words.

choices.text: Lower the temperature for financial responses.
choices.explanation: This changes sampling behavior but does not define the boundary between allowed and denied topics.

choices.text: Refuse only when the user includes an amount in the inquiry.
choices.explanation: Personalized advice may omit an amount, while permitted general examples may include one.

source.label: Amazon Bedrock Guardrailsの拒否トピック

learning.reason: The prohibited content is a personalized recommendation as a matter of meaning, not the appearance of a particular word.
learning.concept: Denied topics can be defined with a description and examples, allowing general information to be treated as a separate topic.

title: Checks Before Using a Public Model for Business
prompt: A publicly available image-generation model with open weights will be used to create advertising materials. Its performance tests meet the requirements, but the terms for secondary use and redistribution have not yet been checked. What should be verified before production begins?

choices.text: Treat the fact that the model was obtained at no cost from a public site as authorization for commercial use and redistribution.
choices.explanation: Availability and permission for each intended use must be checked separately.

choices.text: If the model passes the quality tests specified for the advertising, no license review is needed.
choices.explanation: Quality tests do not assess obligations such as usage terms or attribution.

choices.text: Review the rights information and submit the planned production, sharing, and redistribution uses for organizational review to confirm that they comply with the terms.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes the planned uses from the terms of provision before the model is actually used.

choices.text: Decide that usage restrictions no longer matter as long as the model name is added to the generated materials.
choices.explanation: Even when attribution is required, it does not establish compliance with usage or distribution terms.

source.label: AIF-C01公式ガイドの透明性・ライセンス

learning.reason: The fact that the weights are accessible or the model performs well does not establish permission for a particular use or distribution.
learning.concept: Transparency about a provider's model, data, and license helps explain the conditions of use and the associated risks.

sourceLabel: AIF-C01 official guide: transparency and licensing

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Tag-Based Access to AI Data
prompt: You want an approved training role to read only those S3 training data objects under the same prefix whose Classification tag is Confidential. The bucket is configured to use S3 object tags. Which design is appropriate?

choices.text: Allow reads based only on the training role's PrincipalTag, without including object tags as a condition.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes approved roles but does not prevent a role from reading objects with a different classification.

choices.text: For the training role, add a condition on the existing object's Classification tag to the s3:GetObject permission.
choices.explanation: Both the target role and the tag value of the existing object are reflected in the read permission.

choices.text: Require a request tag from when the object was created in the condition for GetObject.
choices.explanation: A read request does not include the tag from the object's creation, so this cannot determine the classification of an existing object.

choices.text: Generate S3 Inventory reports based on classification tags and allow the entire prefix in the IAM policy.
choices.explanation: The tags can be audited, but the classification restriction is not enforced at read time.

source.label: Amazon S3のオブジェクトタグとポリシー

learning.reason: To distinguish objects under the same prefix, scope the GetObject permission using the tag value on each existing object.
learning.concept: A condition that checks an existing object's tags differs from one that checks tags included in a creation request.

sourceLabel: Amazon S3 object tags and policies

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Controlling the Retention Period for AI Data
prompt: An S3 bucket with versioning disabled and no retention obligation stores intermediate files that do not need to be reproduced. You want temporary files to expire automatically after 30 days from creation while retaining the training files in the same bucket. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Transition the temporary files to an infrequent-access storage class after 30 days.
choices.explanation: This changes the storage class, but the temporary data remains.

choices.text: Configure only NoncurrentVersionExpiration to manage delete markers that are not visible.
choices.explanation: There are no noncurrent versions in this bucket, so this cannot target the current temporary files.

choices.text: Configure an S3 Lifecycle Expiration rule limited to the temporary-file prefix.
choices.explanation: This can expire only the targeted files based on the time elapsed since creation.

choices.text: Set a 30-day Object Lock retention period on the temporary files.
choices.explanation: A retention period restricts deletion; it does not automatically delete data when the period ends.

source.label: Amazon S3 Lifecycleの有効期限

learning.reason: Lifecycle expiration automatically enforces a data-retention deadline.
learning.concept: Design deletion rules according to data classifications and retention requirements.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Promoting Only Approved Models to Production
prompt: In SageMaker AI, you evaluate a new model version each month and want only versions approved by the responsible reviewer to be registered as deployment candidates. A different person performs the approval after evaluation and registration, and build artifacts must be retained for auditing. Which control is appropriate?

choices.text: Always deploy the most recently registered model version and use its approval status in Model Registry for reporting only.
choices.explanation: The latest unapproved version could become a production candidate.

choices.text: Have the approver run the training job and deploy completed jobs without a separate approval record.
choices.explanation: This does not verify evaluation and approval by different people, and it confuses completion status with approval status.

choices.text: Record only approved versions in Model Registry and delete artifacts for failed models each time.
choices.explanation: Approved versions can be selected, but this does not meet the requirement to retain build artifacts for auditing, including those for failed models.

choices.text: Version model packages in Model Registry and make the deployment process select only versions with approved status.
choices.explanation: This applies approval status as an explicit deployment condition while tracking the evaluated artifacts.

source.label: Amazon SageMaker Model Registry

learning.reason: Making approval status a deployment condition prevents unapproved models from being used in production.
learning.concept: Approval controls for the model lifecycle.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Discovering sensitive information in training data
prompt: You want to continuously identify sensitive data, such as personal information, in an S3 training dataset. Which service is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use Amazon Macie to detect sensitive data in S3
choices.explanation: Macie detects sensitive data in S3 buckets and provides findings.

choices.text: Classify S3 data with Amazon Inspector
choices.explanation: Inspector helps manage workload vulnerabilities; it is not intended to classify sensitive data in S3.

choices.text: Scan S3 objects with AWS WAF
choices.explanation: WAF protects web requests; it does not classify stored data.

choices.text: Enable Amazon GuardDuty alone
choices.explanation: GuardDuty detects threats; it is not a substitute for discovering sensitive items in a dataset.

source.label: Amazon Macie User Guide

learning.reason: Understand the contents of training data before deciding how to handle it and control access to it.
learning.concept: Sensitive data discovery and classification.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Retaining tamper-resistant training data
prompt: Store the approved, finalized version of training data in S3. For a specified period, prevent even operators with administrator privileges from deleting that object version or shortening its retention period. Which method is appropriate?

choices.text: Use Object Lock in governance mode and allow operators to bypass the retention settings.
choices.explanation: This does not prevent operators with the required permissions from changing the retention settings.

choices.text: Use Object Lock in compliance mode and configure a retention period for the target version.
choices.explanation: During the retention period, even administrators cannot delete the target version or shorten its retention period.

choices.text: Enable versioning only and use delete markers for ordinary delete operations.
choices.explanation: This helps with recovery, but it does not prevent authorized users from permanently deleting a specific version.

choices.text: Record S3 data deletions with CloudTrail and send notifications.
choices.explanation: This can reveal deletions, but it does not prevent deletion during the retention period.

source.label: Amazon S3 Object Lockの保持モード

learning.reason: Design immutable storage for data subject to audit in accordance with its retention requirements.
learning.concept: Immutable storage and retention controls.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Validate IAM policies before deployment
prompt: Before applying IAM policies for an AI workload in production, you want to check them for syntax errors and security warnings. Which feature should you use?

choices.text: Wait only for external access findings

choices.text: Send the policy document to CloudWatch Logs
