choices.text: Use IAM Access Analyzer policy validation
choices.explanation: Policy validation checks policy syntax, security, and common warnings.

choices.text: Grant administrator permissions
choices.explanation: This is not a substitute for validation and violates least privilege.

source.label: IAM Access Analyzer policy validation

learning.reason: Validate authorization settings before use so you can catch errors early.
learning.concept: Preventive IAM policy controls.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Logically isolating test data from production
prompt: You want to prevent the development team from freely accessing production personal data for AI experiments, even when the experiments and production environment are in the same organization. Which AWS boundary is most appropriate?

choices.text: Share the same administrator role across all environments
choices.explanation: This undermines environment isolation and least privilege.

choices.text: Keep the production bucket name private
choices.explanation: Hiding a name does not create an authorization boundary.

choices.text: Give developers uniform read-only access to production
choices.explanation: This creates ongoing access rather than sharing only the minimum data required.

choices.text: Put development and production in separate AWS accounts and share only what is needed
choices.explanation: AWS accounts provide a strong isolation boundary and allow access controls to be separated by environment.

source.label: Organizing Your AWS Environment

learning.reason: Separating environments by account clarifies the authorization boundary between AI experiments and production data.
learning.concept: Data boundaries through a multi-account architecture.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Minimize data access in SageMaker
prompt: You want the SageMaker environment used by data scientists to access only authorized data. Which authorization design is the most direct?

choices.text: Allow only the required S3 resources in each user's execution role
choices.explanation: An IAM policy on the SageMaker execution role can restrict which AWS resources the role can access.

choices.text: Grant all users full access to S3
choices.explanation: This does not limit the scope of accessible data.

choices.text: Change the SageMaker domain name
choices.explanation: Changing a name does not control authorization.

choices.text: Configure only automatic notebook shutdown
choices.explanation: This helps prevent idle usage; it does not control data access.

source.label: SageMaker Roles

learning.reason: Apply least privilege to roles in AI development environments as well.
learning.concept: Controlling data access with execution roles.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Prevent public S3 settings with preventive controls
prompt: You want to prevent anonymous public access to an S3 bucket used for AI training. Internal users access the bucket through IAM roles, but you also want to ensure that operators cannot make it public even if they try to configure a public ACL or public bucket policy by mistake. Which preventive control is appropriate?

choices.text: Disable ACLs with S3 Object Ownership and allow public bucket policies.
choices.explanation: Public ACLs can no longer be used, but a public bucket policy remains a way to expose the bucket.

choices.text: Enable all S3 Block Public Access settings at the account or bucket level.
choices.explanation: This can prevent public ACLs and public policies independently of existing IAM access.

choices.text: Require encryption but do not restrict creation of public policies.
choices.explanation: Encryption at rest is not a substitute for access controls that reject public settings.

choices.text: Use an Organization audit to detect public settings and remediate them daily.
choices.explanation: This cannot prevent exposure before remediation and does not meet the requirement to preventively reject attempts to configure public access.

source.label: Blocking public access to your Amazon S3 storage

learning.reason: A dataset needs public access paths blocked in advance, not merely detected.
learning.concept: Preventive controls against public access to S3.

sourceLabel: Blocking public access to your Amazon S3 storage

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Continuously collect compliance evidence
prompt: For controls over an AI service, you want to continuously collect and evaluate evidence required for audits from your AWS environment. Which service is most appropriate?

choices.text: Collect evidence with AWS Budgets
choices.explanation: Budgets handles cost notifications and budget management, not audit evidence collection.

choices.text: Collect evidence with Amazon Route 53
choices.explanation: A DNS service is not designed to manage control evidence.

choices.text: Use AWS Audit Manager to help collect and evaluate evidence
choices.explanation: Audit Manager automatically collects evidence from AWS usage and supports audit assessments.

choices.text: Collect evidence with Amazon CloudFront
choices.explanation: A CDN is not intended to collect evidence for audit assessments.

source.label: AWS Audit Manager User Guide

learning.reason: Audit evidence should be collected continuously, not just once.
learning.concept: Automated collection of compliance evidence.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Minimize training data sharing
prompt: You want to provide AI teams in multiple accounts with least-privilege access to a central data lake. Which data authorization service is most appropriate?

choices.text: Manage access permissions with AWS Budgets
choices.explanation: Budgets manages costs; it does not manage data authorization.

choices.text: Manage access permissions with Amazon Route 53
choices.explanation: DNS management is not authorization for a data lake.

choices.text: Manage access permissions with Amazon CloudFront
choices.explanation: A CDN does not manage table- and column-level access in a data lake.

choices.text: Manage fine-grained data lake permissions with AWS Lake Formation
choices.explanation: Lake Formation provides fine-grained access control for data in a data lake.

source.label: AWS Lake Formation

learning.reason: When sharing data across accounts, authorize access to the minimum necessary data.
learning.concept: Fine-grained access control for data lakes.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Keep API credentials out of application code
prompt: An AI application needs credentials to call an external API. The credentials must be managed so they can be rotated without storing them in source code. Which service is most appropriate?

choices.text: Store the secret in AWS Secrets Manager
choices.explanation: Secrets Manager supports storing, retrieving, and rotating secrets.

choices.text: Store it in Amazon S3 object metadata
choices.explanation: This is not a dedicated credential store with rotation capabilities.

choices.text: Store it in a CloudWatch dashboard
choices.explanation: A dashboard is not a place to store sensitive values.

choices.text: Store it unencrypted in a Git repository
choices.explanation: Storing credentials in source control increases the risk of exposure.

source.label: AWS Secrets Manager

learning.reason: Separate credentials from application code so access can be controlled and credentials can be rotated.
learning.concept: Secrets management.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Enforce organization-wide permission ceilings
prompt: You want to set permission ceilings across an organization so that AI development accounts cannot use unapproved AWS services. Which feature is most appropriate?

choices.text: Change each developer's IAM user name
choices.explanation: Changing a name does not enforce a permission ceiling.

choices.text: Use service control policies in AWS Organizations
choices.explanation: SCPs define permission ceilings for IAM permissions in accounts within an organization.

choices.text: Set up CloudWatch alarms only
choices.explanation: Alarms do not proactively restrict permissions.

choices.text: Require billing tags only
choices.explanation: Cost allocation does not set limits on which services can be used.

source.label: Service control policies

learning.reason: Organization-wide permission ceilings can be applied, including to account administrators.
learning.concept: Preventive guardrails with SCPs.

title: Completion notification for large inputs
prompt: A user submits a high-resolution image analysis that takes 2 minutes. The result can be retrieved from S3 later. You do not want to keep a waiting connection open, and you want to reduce capacity when there is no load. Which inference mode is suitable?

choices.text: Synchronous real-time inference
choices.explanation: This is intended for returning results to the screen immediately and does not fit a long-running asynchronous task.

choices.text: Asynchronous inference
choices.explanation: It accepts long-running tasks and suits the requirement to retrieve the S3 output later.

choices.text: Nightly batch inference
choices.explanation: It does not handle completion notifications for individual requests.

choices.text: Image clustering
choices.explanation: It does not determine how inference requests are accepted or answered.

source.label: SageMaker 非同期推論

learning.reason: Process long-running individual requests asynchronously and place the results in S3.
learning.concept: Choose an inference mode based on input size, response-wait requirements, and unit of processing.

title: Sporadic small predictions
prompt: You need to make an immediate prediction on inputs of a few KB only a few dozen times per day. The design cannot be changed to poll for a response, but an initial cold start is acceptable. You want SageMaker to respond synchronously without keeping inference capacity running when there are no requests. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Nightly batch inference
choices.explanation: It does not provide an immediate response.

choices.text: Asynchronous inference for long-running inputs
choices.explanation: This mode is intended primarily for large payloads or long-running tasks.

choices.text: Serverless Inference
choices.explanation: It suits sporadic, small, immediate requests when you do not want to manage always-on capacity.

choices.text: Cross-validation
choices.explanation: This is a model evaluation method.

source.label: SageMaker サーバーレス推論

learning.reason: Choose serverless inference for sporadic, immediate requests.
learning.concept: Distinguish serverless, asynchronous, and batch modes by request timing and input characteristics.

title: Ranking Candidates
prompt: A search service displays 20 candidate products to each user and wants to order them from most to least likely to be purchased. It needs their relative order, not assignment to a new category. Which problem type is the closest match?

choices.text: Regression
choices.explanation: It can predict continuous values, but the question is about optimizing the order itself.

choices.text: Clustering
choices.explanation: It discovers groups of similar items; it does not return an ordering of candidates.

choices.text: Object detection
choices.explanation: It deals with locations within images.

choices.text: Ranking
choices.explanation: It fits the goal of optimizing the relative positions of candidates.

source.label: AIF-C01 Domain 1 試験ガイド

learning.reason: Choose ranking to determine the display order.
learning.concept: Classification deals with classes, while ranking deals with the order of candidates.

title: A Sequential Action Policy
prompt: A warehouse robot chooses its next move from its current position. It receives a negative reward for a collision and a positive reward for reaching its destination quickly. It should improve its policy by trying actions, rather than by predicting correct labels from a fixed history. Which learning approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Reinforcement learning
choices.explanation: It improves a policy through actions and rewards in an environment.

choices.text: Supervised classification
choices.explanation: It classifies against existing labels; it does not learn a sequential policy that maximizes rewards.

choices.text: Clustering
choices.explanation: Grouping states does not teach the robot a policy.

choices.text: Time-series forecasting
choices.explanation: It predicts future values rather than handling action selection.

source.label: AIF-C01 Domain 1 試験ガイド

learning.reason: Choose reinforcement learning to optimize rewards from sequential actions.
learning.concept: Reinforcement learning uses rewards from the environment rather than labels.

title: Multiple Tags for One Image
prompt: A photo contains the sea, a person, and a boat at the same time. The goal is to assign every applicable tag to each photo, rather than one exclusive category. What type of output is needed?

choices.text: Single-label classification
choices.explanation: It assumes that only one class is selected.

choices.text: Multilabel classification
choices.explanation: It allows multiple independent labels to be assigned to one observation.

choices.text: Regression
choices.explanation: It returns a continuous numeric value.

choices.text: Ranking
choices.explanation: It returns an ordering of candidates.

source.label: SageMaker Canvas モデル種別

learning.reason: Choose multilabel classification to return several tags at once.
learning.concept: Multiclass and multilabel classification differ in whether labels are mutually exclusive.

title: Forecast Granularity for Ordering
prompt: A convenience store decides every day at 6 a.m. how many boxed meals to order for sale the next day. Daily sales vary by weekday at each store. At what granularity should historical data be prepared to make it easier to forecast next-day demand by store and product at ordering time?

choices.text: Company-wide annual totals
choices.explanation: This is too coarse for a store-specific, next-day decision.

choices.text: A transaction list in random order
choices.explanation: This loses the time sequence.

choices.text: A daily time series for each store and product
choices.explanation: This matches the ordering unit and next-day forecast horizon.

choices.text: Image pixels of the products
choices.explanation: This does not represent a time series of sales quantities.

source.label: SageMaker Canvas 時系列予測

learning.reason: Choose daily granularity for each store and product to match the decision.
learning.concept: Time-series granularity should match the frequency of the business decision that uses the forecast.

title: When to Start Forecasting for a New Product
prompt: A new product has only two days of sales history since launch, while the overall category has three years of history that includes seasonality. What is the most important concern before forecasting demand for the new product for the following week?

choices.text: The lack of image bounding boxes
choices.explanation: This is not a primary limitation for demand time-series forecasting.

choices.text: The lack of speech transcriptions
choices.explanation: Speech transcriptions are not needed to forecast from sales history.

choices.text: The lack of multilingual answers
choices.explanation: This is unrelated to the amount of time-series observations.

choices.text: The short product-specific history provides a weak basis for the forecast
choices.explanation: There are too few product-specific observations to learn sufficient time-series patterns.

source.label: SageMaker Canvas 時系列予測

learning.reason: A short history specific to the new product increases forecast uncertainty.
learning.concept: Before using time-series forecasting, check the amount and granularity of history and which features will be available in the future.

title: Unknown Failure Patterns
prompt: Equipment logs have very few failure labels, and you want to quickly investigate behavior that differs substantially from normal behavior, including unknown failures. Which initial approach is the most suitable?

choices.text: Anomaly detection that looks for deviations from normal patterns
choices.explanation: With too few failure labels, deviations from normal behavior can be flagged for investigation.

choices.text: Supervised classification using only known failures
choices.explanation: Unknown patterns cannot be included as training labels.

choices.text: Sales regression forecasting
choices.explanation: This does not target anomalies in equipment logs.

choices.text: Multilabel image classification
choices.explanation: This does not address behavior in logs.

source.label: SageMaker Canvas 異常検知

learning.reason: Because failures are unknown and labels are scarce, look for deviations from normal behavior.
learning.concept: Anomaly detection and supervised classification of known classes differ in the labels available and the objective.

title: Routing Messages by Language
prompt: You want to automatically route overseas customer inquiry emails to teams responsible for each language, without translating their content. Which natural language processing task is needed first?

choices.text: Image object detection
choices.explanation: This does not process the language of text.

choices.text: Language identification
choices.explanation: It determines the language of the input text so the message can be routed to the appropriate team.

choices.text: Demand forecasting
choices.explanation: This predicts future numerical values.

choices.text: Speech synthesis
choices.explanation: This reads text aloud.

source.label: Amazon Comprehend 言語識別

learning.reason: Determine the input language before translating it.
learning.concept: Language identification, translation, sentiment analysis, and classification are distinct NLP tasks.

title: Taking Natural-Language Questions About Internal Information
prompt: Employees on the same internal portal ask natural-language questions about company benefits and expense policies. You want to provide an assistant connected to existing enterprise information while minimizing the custom search and generation work and operational effort. Which approach is a good fit?

choices.text: Call a Bedrock foundation model with only a generic prompt and do not connect it to internal information.
choices.explanation: The model can respond, but this does not meet the requirement to answer questions about benefits and expenses using existing enterprise information.

choices.text: Use Amazon Kendra to provide a search interface that returns only a list of relevant documents.
choices.explanation: This can point users to search results, but the requirement to compose answers to their questions from the retrieved information remains.

choices.text: Connect Amazon Q Business to existing information sources.
choices.explanation: This service provides question answering based on enterprise data, so there is no need to build the search and generation components from scratch.

choices.text: Register each question category and response individually in Amazon Lex.
choices.explanation: This can create structured conversations, but additional implementation is needed to quickly provide open-ended question answering grounded in existing materials.

source.label: What is Amazon Q Business

learning.reason: Amazon Q Business is an option for quickly providing a generative AI assistant for enterprise use.
learning.concept: Document extraction or speech recognition alone does not directly provide natural-language question answering over enterprise information.

title: Separate record updates from text generation
prompt: An order system must accurately decrement inventory and retain auditable transaction records. It also needs to create shipping messages for customers. Which use of generative AI is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use generative AI to determine inventory quantities and save transaction records as free-form text.
choices.explanation: Inventory updates and transaction records require deterministic, auditable processing.

choices.text: Stop inventory management in order to create shipping messages.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the order-processing requirements.

choices.text: Update inventory without creating customer messages.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the goal of improving customer communications.

choices.text: Update inventory and transactions in the business system, and use generative AI to draft shipping messages.
choices.explanation: This is correct. It separates accurate record processing from generating natural customer communications.

source.label: Amazon Bedrock prompt engineering concepts

learning.reason: Generative AI can assist with writing, but it is not a substitute for updating accurate core business records.
learning.concept: Separate unstructured writing tasks suited to generation from deterministic business records.

title: Improve accessibility with image descriptions
prompt: Product photos on a product page have no alt text, making it difficult for screen reader users to understand the products. The descriptions must briefly explain features that are actually visible, and a staff member must verify that they match the images before publication. Which approach meets these requirements?

choices.text: Generate alt-text suggestions from each image and its associated product information, then have a staff member compare them with the original image before publication.
choices.explanation: This puts image content into words, while allowing a staff member to remove invisible features or correct inaccurate descriptions.

choices.text: Use a compatible image classifier and use the returned category name as the alt text for every image.
choices.explanation: The category is identified, but specific features conveyed by the image, such as color and shape, are not described.

choices.text: Generate one general product description and use it for every image in the same category.
choices.explanation: This keeps the descriptions consistent but cannot describe differences between individual images.

choices.text: Extract only printed text from each image and publish it automatically as the alt text.
choices.explanation: This extracts text in the image, but does not describe visual features or include a human review before publication.

source.label: Amazon Bedrock models at a glance

learning.reason: The ability to understand images and generate descriptions can improve user experience and accessibility.
learning.concept: For image-related use cases, connect the required input and output modalities to the business value.

sourceLabel: Amazon Bedrock models at a glance

title: Test multiple variants quickly
prompt: A marketing team wants to create several headline options from the same campaign requirements and compare responses in a small A/B test. What is the most direct value of using generative AI?

choices.text: Generate one headline, show it to everyone, and compare monthly responses from before publication.
choices.explanation: It can be published quickly, but changes in timing or audience are mixed in, so multiple options cannot be compared.

choices.text: Create multiple headlines with different wording under the same product and channel conditions, then compare candidates in a small experiment under the same conditions.
choices.explanation: This reduces the time needed to create options and lets the team measure user responses while controlling for differences in the displayed wording.

choices.text: Choose the model that generates the most outputs and set the criteria for selecting a headline after publication.
choices.explanation: This increases the number of drafts but does not define in advance which options contribute to the business goal.

choices.text: Generate a batch of options and ask the generative model to predict responses using only the option it ranks highest.
choices.explanation: This can help narrow the candidates, but it does not verify how the target audience actually responds.

source.label: AWS CAF: Accelerating business outcomes

learning.reason: Generative AI speeds up the creation of multiple options and supports experimentation and improvement based on customer responses.
learning.concept: Validate the value of generated content using actual user responses.

title: Break down a comparison question to find supporting evidence
prompt: In an application that searches policy documents, a single similarity search for “Compare the cancellation fees and refund deadlines for the old and new plans” mostly returns policies for the new plan. Which approach lets the application find each item separately and then assemble an answer, without asking the user to rewrite the question?

choices.text: Pass the current single query unchanged to a reranker after retrieval.
choices.explanation: This can change the ranking of candidates, but it does not run new searches for separate aspects of the question.

choices.text: Convert the policies into long, fixed-length chunks and always pass only the first one.
choices.explanation: This can include more information from a section, but it cannot distinguish comparison targets spread across different documents.

choices.text: Keep the current single search and increase the token limit for the generated answer.
choices.explanation: This can increase the length of the answer, but it does not add policies for comparison targets that were not retrieved.

choices.text: Use query decomposition with a supported retrieval and generation configuration.
choices.explanation: This splits a compound question into subquestions and allows multiple search results to inform the answer.

source.label: 質問の分解

learning.reason: When multiple aspects are obscured by a single search, split the question into subquestions before searching and then combine the supporting evidence.
learning.concept: Reranking reorders the retrieved set; it does not split the question before retrieval.

title: Bring Values Found Only in Tables and Figures into Search
prompt: A performance table in maintenance documentation appears in a PDF with its values embedded as an image. The content ingested with the current text extraction contains none of those values, and the table relevant to the question does not appear in the search results. What should be reviewed first?

choices.text: Configure a parsing method in the data source that can handle tables and figures, then ingest the documents again.
choices.explanation: This can address information that could not be searched for at the parsing and ingestion stage, before retrieval.

choices.text: Increase the number of chunks returned by search without changing ingestion.
choices.explanation: This may return more candidates, but it will not include table values that were never ingested as text.

choices.text: Add the document's update date as metadata and restrict results to the latest date.
choices.explanation: This can narrow the search to a document version, but it will not extract the contents of figures.

choices.text: Instruct the model to prioritize values from the documents during generation and use the current retrieval results.
choices.explanation: The instruction itself cannot supply figure values that are absent from the retrieved results.

source.label: ナレッジベースの文書解析

learning.reason: Choose a parsing method during ingestion that can handle information in tables and images, then include the parsed results in the index.
learning.concept: Even a highly capable generative model cannot retrieve a value that is not present in the index.

title: An Agent That Continues Processing in an Existing Application
prompt: An internal assistant gathers an equipment reservation date, time, and equipment number through a conversation. An existing application performs the reservation and auditing, and the agent cannot call the reservation API directly. How can the agent pass the collected arguments to the application and then answer the user using the execution result?

choices.text: Specify a Lambda function that directly executes the reservation API in the action group.
choices.explanation: This configuration lets the agent initiate the reservation, which conflicts with the requirement that execution remain in the existing application.

choices.text: Configure the action group to return control to the caller, and have the application associate its processing result with the same invocation and return it.
choices.explanation: The AI can handle the conversation and explain the result while reservation execution and auditing remain in the application.

choices.text: Add a description of the reservation API to a knowledge base so that a reservation is created in response to the answer.
choices.explanation: Reference material can support an explanation, but it does not structure the arguments and associate them with a reservation execution result.

choices.text: Record the date and time in agent memory, then have the application read them in the next session and infer the result.
choices.explanation: This is intended to retain conversational context, not to link the current action arguments with the execution result.

source.label: Bedrock Agentsの制御返却

learning.reason: The agent returns the action arguments, and the application processes them and returns a result associated with that invocation.
learning.concept: This separates collecting information in a conversation from executing a business operation.

title: Carry a Selected Warehouse Forward Only Within a Conversation
prompt: In an internal inventory assistant, an employee selects a warehouse at the start of a conversation. The application must be able to pass that warehouse to the agent on the next turn in the same conversation, but it must not carry over the selection after the conversation changes. Which approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Set the warehouse only on the first turn in a prompt session attribute that persists for a single turn.
choices.explanation: It is limited to that turn, so the next turn cannot refer to it as configured.

choices.text: Use cross-session memory for each user to store the warehouse.
choices.explanation: This design carries context into the next session, which exceeds the required lifetime.

choices.text: Treat the selected warehouse as a session attribute for the same session ID.
choices.explanation: The value can be retained within the same session without needing to carry it into a new conversation by default.

choices.text: Write the last selected warehouse into shared agent instructions used by all users.
choices.explanation: This would mix values specific to a user and conversation into shared configuration.

source.label: Bedrock Agentsのセッション属性

learning.reason: Keep a value used within the same session at the session level, and distinguish it from memory shared across sessions.
learning.concept: Choose the attribute's lifetime based on whether it is needed for one invocation or multiple turns in the same conversation.

title: Reduce Input Costs for Questions Using the Same Long Document
prompt: Different users ask different questions, but the same lengthy business policy is repeatedly sent to a foundation model. For a supported model, you want to optimize a series of requests made close together without changing the policy. Where should you place the cache boundary?

choices.text: Put the question first and cache the entire question and policy.
choices.explanation: Whenever the question changes, the input stops matching from the beginning, so the condition for reuse is no longer met.

choices.text: Embed the question partway through the policy and place the boundary at the end of the entire policy.
choices.explanation: Because the question inserted partway through the policy changes, the entire input, including everything after it, cannot be reused as the same prefix.

choices.text: Keep the policy after the question and shorten the model's output.
choices.explanation: Shortening the output does not change which input prefix can be reused.

choices.text: Place the fixed instructions and document at the beginning, put the cache point at their end, and then add the question.
choices.explanation: This caches the fixed portion while allowing only the question to change from request to request.

source.label: Amazon Bedrockのプロンプトキャッシュ

learning.reason: Put the unchanged instructions and policy first, make their end the end of the cached portion, and put the question after them.
learning.concept: Because this mechanism reuses content that matches from the beginning, putting a changing question first shortens the reusable portion. Actual reuse also requires conditions such as the model-specific minimum token count and validity period; placement alone does not guarantee a cache hit.

title: Adding a business-specific criterion to human evaluation
prompt: For internal contract summaries, a team wants to evaluate whether exceptions to disclaimer clauses are retained, in addition to clarity. Evaluators can make judgments by following a rubric, and there is no single reference answer for each summary. Which approach should they use?

choices.text: Define retention of exceptions as a custom metric and give human evaluators criteria for deciding whether each summary meets it.
choices.explanation: Even when there is no single reference answer, evaluators can apply the same criteria to determine whether the required information was retained.

choices.text: Rank candidates using only a general fluency score.
choices.explanation: A readable summary may still omit an exception to a disclaimer clause.

choices.text: Ask each evaluator to produce a different output and rank the results using their own criteria.
choices.explanation: Without shared criteria, it is difficult to compare what the candidates satisfy.

choices.text: Use summary length as the exception-retention rate.
choices.explanation: A longer summary does not necessarily include the important exceptions.

source.label: Bedrockの人によるモデル評価

learning.reason: Define criteria that people can apply and compare candidate outputs using the same evaluation data.
learning.concept: General metrics such as fluency cannot independently verify important conditions specific to an internal policy.

sourceLabel: Human evaluation of models in Bedrock

title: Comparing evaluation results from an existing system under the same conditions
prompt: A custom internal RAG system has saved the policies, answers, and retrieved results from a specific point in time. Running inference again with the system updated to the current policies would not reproduce the evidence used at that time. How can the saved outputs be evaluated with Bedrock RAG evaluation?

choices.text: Run a new RetrieveAndGenerate using the current policies and treat the result as the result from that point in time.
choices.explanation: The evidence version would differ, so this would not evaluate the answer from the target point in time.

choices.text: Include the saved questions and answers, along with their corresponding sources, in the evaluation dataset using the bring-your-own-inference input format.
choices.explanation: This evaluates both the saved generation and retrieval results without generating new responses.

choices.text: Use answers from the external RAG system as training data to tune a model, then infer the earlier responses from its new outputs.
choices.explanation: This does not directly evaluate the actual responses and retrieved evidence from that point in time.

choices.text: Evaluate the historical data with a retrieval-only job and omit the generated answers.
choices.explanation: This can evaluate the evidence, but it cannot measure the quality of the saved answers.

source.label: BedrockのRAG評価用データセット

learning.reason: Bringing past inference results and retrieved information into the evaluation dataset makes it possible to evaluate outputs from the same point in time.
learning.concept: Generating the outputs used in an evaluation can be separated from scoring saved outputs against predefined criteria.

title: Investigating why a search was not reached
prompt: An equipment-search agent responded to an inventory question with contact information for the responsible team without using search. Search-side metrics alone do not show whether the agent never decided to search or whether it returned that response after receiving a search result. What should you inspect first using safe test data?

choices.text: Use only the number of characters in the generated output as a substitute for a trace.
choices.explanation: Output length cannot show whether a particular operation was selected.

choices.text: Leave the configuration unchanged and aggregate only overall processing time on the search side.
choices.explanation: This does not answer whether an individual agent invocation selected search.

choices.text: Enable tracing for a test invocation and compare the operations that ran with the results of each step.
choices.explanation: This lets you check step by step whether the agent reached knowledge retrieval and used its results.

choices.text: Add an instruction to the final answer to list the tools used at the end.
choices.explanation: Generated text is not an execution record proving that an operation actually ran.

source.label: Bedrock Agentsの処理の流れとトレース

learning.reason: Inspect a trace containing the actions selected by the agent and the results returned at each step.
learning.concept: Checking the final answer is different from checking which internal operations were selected.

title: Using a custom-tuned model as is
prompt: A model tuned in-house must retain the weights used during evaluation. Its architecture and data format are supported by Bedrock Custom Model Import, and its model artifacts can be stored in S3. How should you serve inference with Bedrock?

choices.text: Choose a Bedrock foundation model for the same use case and give it the same name as the in-house model.
choices.explanation: Matching the name does not make the evaluated model's weights available.

choices.text: Use output examples from the in-house model to distill a separate, smaller model.
choices.explanation: This can teach similar output behavior, but it does not retain and run the original weights as an artifact.

choices.text: Register the model artifacts in S3 in a knowledge base and retrieve them as documents.
choices.explanation: A knowledge base handles data for retrieval; it does not load model weights as an executable model.

choices.text: Import the compatible artifacts from S3 using Custom Model Import, then specify the imported model for inference.
choices.explanation: This lets you use the original tuned model for inference through Bedrock.

source.label: Bedrockのカスタムモデルのインポート

learning.reason: Importing compatible model artifacts makes the tuned weights available for use.
learning.concept: Importing a tuned model differs from fine-tuning another model provided by Bedrock.

title: Tuning a task without a single expected output
prompt: A model helps organize logistics data, and you want it to learn outputs that allow multiple valid orderings. An existing verifier can check all required fields and aggregate values and return a numeric score. Which method tunes the compatible model itself without continuing to write a single reference response?

choices.text: Use verifier-based rewards to reinforcement fine-tune a compatible model.
choices.explanation: This lets the verifier assess quality without forcing multiple valid formats into a single correct response.

choices.text: Fix a single output format as correct for each input and continue supervised fine-tuning on those reference responses.
choices.explanation: This can train the model, but it does not meet the requirement to stop writing a single reference response.

choices.text: Add longer logistics documents and perform unlabeled continued pretraining.
choices.explanation: This may adapt terminology and style, but it does not train aggregation correctness using verifier-based rewards.

choices.text: Only score production outputs with the same verifier, without changing the model.
choices.explanation: This can detect invalid outputs, but it does not tune the model itself.

source.label: Amazon Novaモデルの強化ファインチューニング

learning.reason: When several outputs are valid, training can use a reward that quantifies the desired properties.
learning.concept: A reward should evaluate whether required values and constraints are actually satisfied, not just how the output looks.

sourceLabel: Reinforcement fine-tuning for Amazon Nova models

title: Assigning node roles in an application workflow
prompt: In Bedrock Flows, check whether an application has been submitted and create supplementary text only when needed. Match each task to the node that performs it.

choices.text: Prompt node
choices.explanation: Generates supplementary text using the configured prompt and foundation model.

choices.text: Flow output node
choices.explanation: Returns the result determined in the flow to the caller.

choices.text: Condition node
choices.explanation: Routes execution based on the specified flag value.

source.label: Amazon Bedrock Flowsのノード種別

learning.reason: Assign condition checks, natural-language generation, and returning the result to their respective nodes.
learning.concept: There is no need to delegate explicit rules such as branching to a model’s natural-language judgment.

prompts.text: Route execution based on the submitted flag.
Create supplementary text with a foundation model.
Return the final result produced by the flow to the caller.

title: Correcting historical training labels
prompt: A company already uses SageMaker Ground Truth, and some previously labeled equipment photos contain labels assigned by workers using outdated criteria. Counting correct and incorrect labels is not enough; the company wants corrected labels to use in the next training run. Which workflow should it use?

choices.text: Send the relevant images and existing labels to an adjustment job and correct them according to the new criteria.
choices.explanation: This reuses the existing annotations and prepares corrected results for the next training run.

choices.text: Use a verification job to record only whether the labels are correct, then train on the original labels unchanged.
choices.explanation: This can identify the problem, but incorrect labels remain in the next training run.

choices.text: Retrain a classification model on the current labels and unconditionally delete only the low-confidence images.
choices.explanation: This does not correct mislabeled data and could remove important low-confidence images.

choices.text: Relabel every image using the old labels and accept only cases that match the old labels.
choices.explanation: This checks agreement with the outdated criteria, so it cannot resolve problems caused by the change in criteria.

source.label: Ground Truthのラベル検証・調整

learning.reason: Choose a job that corrects annotations when needed, rather than only checking existing labels.
learning.concept: Verification evaluates existing annotations; adjustment corrects annotations for later use.

sourceLabel: Ground Truth label verification and adjustment

title: Improving guidelines from annotator disagreements
prompt: A quality audit found that multiple workers assigned different labels to the same product images. Many misclassifications involve images where it is difficult to distinguish a minor scratch from a normal surface pattern. Which action would make judgments at this ambiguous boundary more consistent before the next training run?

choices.text: Train on the label provided by the first worker to respond for each image.
choices.explanation: This is easy to measure, but it does not resolve the reasons for the differing judgments.

choices.text: Have experts review the disagreements, add boundary cases to the guidelines, then relabel the affected examples and check agreement rates.
choices.explanation: This reduces differences in judgment at their source and measures whether the revised criteria are applied consistently.

choices.text: Apply a mechanical majority vote to every image and leave the labeling guidelines unchanged, even for close cases.
choices.explanation: This produces an aggregate label, but leaves the ambiguous boundary criteria unresolved.

choices.text: Rank workers only by how often their labels agree with the model’s predictions.
choices.explanation: The model was also trained on ambiguous labels, so its predictions do not provide a reliable standard for the correct boundary.

source.label: Ground Truthのアノテーション統合

learning.reason: Identify cases with disagreement, clarify the decision boundary, and verify label consistency.
learning.concept: Consolidating annotations from multiple people does not resolve the cause if everyone is applying different criteria.

title: Keep People in Control of High-Impact Decisions, Even at High Confidence
prompt: An internal AI system provides reasons and recommendations for transaction reviews before orders are accepted. Business rules require a reviewer to read the reasons before finalizing any decision to reject a contract, regardless of prediction confidence. Which operating design fits?

choices.text: Send only low-confidence recommendations to a person, and automatically finalize high-confidence rejections.
choices.explanation: This may reduce workload, but it violates the requirement for review before any rejection is finalized, regardless of confidence.

choices.text: Automatically finalize rejections, then have reviewers sample cases weekly.
choices.explanation: This is a post-decision audit and does not allow an individual decision to be reviewed in advance.

choices.text: Keep rejections pending until a reviewer reads the reasons and approves or changes the decision before finalizing it.
choices.explanation: A person can make the decision before it takes effect and retains the authority to change the AI recommendation.

choices.text: Show users the AI's reasons for rejecting a contract and treat that display as a substitute for reviewer approval.
choices.explanation: Explaining a decision to users does not mean a reviewer approved it.

source.label: 責任あるAIの人による監督

learning.reason: Before a consequential action, a person should be able to review the rationale and choose a decision different from the recommendation.
learning.concept: Reviewing only low-confidence predictions is different from requiring approval based on the impact of a decision.

title: Measure Stereotypes in Polite-Sounding Responses
prompt: Customer service responses generated by a model rarely contain insults, but they tend to assign the same social attribute to people from a particular place of origin without support from the text. Which Bedrock evaluation metric directly measures this issue?

choices.text: Logical coherence
choices.explanation: It measures the logical consistency of a response, but does not directly measure unsupported generalizations about a group.

choices.text: Following instructions
choices.explanation: It measures adherence to instructions. Outputs that follow instructions while adding stereotypes need to be evaluated separately.

choices.text: Helpfulness
choices.explanation: It measures whether a response is useful, which does not directly identify polite text that contains stereotypes.

choices.text: Stereotyping
choices.explanation: This metric can be used to evaluate generated content for stereotypes about a particular group.

source.label: Bedrockの組み込み評価指標

learning.reason: The issue to measure is the tendency to generate stereotypes about a group, not the use of offensive language.
learning.concept: Harmfulness, stereotyping, grounding in retrieved sources, and answer relevance measure different things.

title: Measure the Rate of Normal Responses Blocked by a New Policy First
prompt: You want to add a new content filter to a support chat. Do not stop responses to users until you have measured how often normal responses would be blocked using traffic equivalent to production. Then enable blocking. Which method should you use for this validation stage?

choices.text: Evaluate the filter in detection-only mode and separately measure which of its findings were normal responses.
choices.explanation: This lets you test the impact of blocking without actually blocking responses.

choices.text: Immediately block all users' inputs and use complaints as the false-block rate.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement not to stop normal responses during measurement, and complaints alone do not capture the full impact.

choices.text: Disable the filter and record only the number of responses without it.
choices.explanation: This avoids affecting users but does not show which responses the candidate policy would detect.

choices.text: Estimate the false-positive rate after blocking using only a set of inappropriate outputs that contains no normal responses.
choices.explanation: This can show how inappropriate outputs are detected, but cannot measure false positives on normal responses.

source.label: Bedrock Guardrailsの遮断・検出時の動作

learning.reason: Detection-only mode lets you collect potential interventions and evaluate false positives without changing the responses users receive.
learning.concept: Before enabling blocking, explicitly measure how much it would affect normal inputs.

sourceLabel: How Bedrock Guardrails handle blocking and detection

title: Tell Users How to Interpret AI Responses
prompt: A local public service office uses generative AI to summarize application procedures. Only staff can verify the latest exception rules. What should be displayed when users begin using the service so they do not mistake a response for an official decision and can reach staff when needed?

choices.text: Label the response page “Official determination” and list the internal model ID at the end of the user guide.
choices.explanation: The model identifier does not tell users the scope of the response or where to go for help.

choices.text: Clearly label the response as AI-generated guidance and show which exceptions cannot be verified, along with how to contact staff.
choices.explanation: Users can see the nature of the information and what to do next at the point where they read the response.

choices.text: Record the contact for exception-related questions only in operating instructions for staff.
choices.explanation: Staff may share the information internally, but it does not help users understand the limits of AI responses.

choices.text: Display only the response confidence score and leave users to decide how to handle exceptions and where to seek confirmation.
choices.explanation: Even a high confidence score does not mean exception rules have been verified, and users are given no path to reach staff.

source.label: 責任あるAIの人による監督

learning.reason: Tell users, where they can read it, that the response is AI-generated, what the system can verify, and how to contact staff.
learning.concept: Separate internal system records from the information users need to understand the system's limits and reach a person when necessary.

title: Check whether harmless input changes affect results
prompt: An AI system reads the same invoice content, but mistakes the amount when the scan is tilted or image compression differs. These changes do not alter the correct value. Which test most directly measures this problem before release?

choices.text: Repeatedly score only the existing, unaltered images and calculate a confidence interval.
choices.explanation: This measures results under the same conditions, but does not show whether tilt or compression has an effect.

choices.text: Create images edited to show different invoice amounts, but continue using the original amounts as the expected values.
choices.explanation: Because the correct content has changed, this cannot test robustness to changes in representation alone.

choices.text: Create multiple images from the same invoice, changing only tilt or compression while preserving the content, and compare whether the same amount is extracted.
choices.explanation: This tests only input variations for a single piece of content.

choices.text: Calculate accuracy by invoice issuer without recording each issuer's scan conditions.
choices.explanation: This may reveal variation by issuer, but cannot directly isolate the effects of tilt or compression.

source.label: AIF-C01公式ガイドの堅牢性

learning.reason: Vary only the input while preserving its content, then compare the outputs with the same expected answer.
learning.concept: Measuring performance degradation under meaning-preserving input variations tests robustness to ordinary real-world changes.

sourceLabel: Robustness in the official AIF-C01 guide

title: Separate application-side model calls from input checks
prompt: A business application needs to receive a judgment on an input first, then send it to its existing inference platform only if it is allowed. The inference platform cannot be migrated to Bedrock inference APIs. Where can Bedrock Guardrails be used?

choices.text: Because a Guardrail setting is required on an inference request, the existing platform must be migrated to Bedrock.
choices.explanation: Guardrails can also be applied alongside Bedrock inference, but there is a way to use them independently for evaluation.

choices.text: Check the input after a response is returned from the existing inference platform.
choices.explanation: This can be used for a decision at output time, but the input has already been sent for inference.

choices.text: Create a guardrail and assume it is active without calling it from the existing inference platform.
choices.explanation: Creating a guardrail does not apply it to requests or make its result available as an application branching condition.

choices.text: Evaluate the input with ApplyGuardrail first, then call the existing inference platform based on the result.
choices.explanation: Independent evaluation allows the inference destination to remain unchanged and only permitted inputs to proceed downstream.

source.label: Amazon Bedrockの独立したGuardrail評価

learning.reason: Passing an input to an evaluation API that operates independently of model invocation enables checking it without changing the inference destination.
learning.concept: Calling a guardrail does not stop the business process by itself, so the application must branch based on the evaluation result.

sourceLabel: Independent Guardrail evaluation in Amazon Bedrock

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Define what must be approved for AI use
prompt: An internal generative AI use policy requires that only uses approved in advance may be used for results sent to customers. Internal validation experiments may follow a separate review process. Which control design is most appropriate?

choices.text: Unconditionally prohibit all generative AI use.
choices.explanation: This also applies to validation experiments and cannot express the distinction the policy requires.

choices.text: Record the purpose, target data, and approver for each customer-facing use case, and allow only approved cases in production.
choices.explanation: Linking each use case to its purpose and approval scope consistently controls only the uses covered by the policy.

choices.text: Require users to read the policy once.
choices.explanation: Acknowledgment alone does not track the approval status of individual use cases.

choices.text: Always fix generated results to the same wording.
choices.explanation: Fixing output content is not a control for use-case approval.

source.label: AWS Responsible AI Lensの人による監督

learning.reason: AI use rules should define approvable units based on the context of the use and data.
learning.concept: Use-case-specific AI governance approval.

sourceLabel: Human oversight in the AWS Responsible AI Lens

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Trace the origins of training data
prompt: If a problem is found in a model's output, you want to determine later which version of which dataset was used for training. Which operational practice is most appropriate?

choices.text: Record only the final model's file name.
choices.explanation: A file name alone cannot trace the training data or its transformations.

choices.text: Unconditionally delete the source data after training is complete.
choices.explanation: This ignores retention requirements and also loses lineage needed for investigation.

choices.text: Record the relationships among dataset versions, sources, preprocessing, and model training jobs.
choices.explanation: Recording data lineage makes it possible to trace the inputs and transformations that led to the model.

choices.text: Monitor only dataset size.
choices.explanation: Size does not indicate a dataset's source, version, or transformations.

source.label: Amazon SageMaker ML Lineage Tracking

learning.reason: Reproducibility and accountability require lineage from data to model.
learning.concept: Data lineage and model reproducibility.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Require an approved guardrail version for every inference
prompt: Several business applications can invoke the same Bedrock model. Even if an application is not updated, inference must not be possible without the approved numbered guardrail version. Which IAM control should be used?

choices.text: Restrict the available foundation models to approved model IDs.
choices.explanation: This can restrict the models, but it does not distinguish calls to the same model that omit a guardrail.

choices.text: Grant permission to evaluate only the approved guardrail, while leaving inference permissions unchanged.
choices.explanation: This allows the guardrail to be used, but does not require it to be specified during inference.

choices.text: Use CloudWatch to notify administrators when a guardrail is updated, without changing how applications use it.
choices.explanation: Administrators receive change notifications, but inference with an outdated configuration is not blocked before execution.

choices.text: Use the IAM policy to condition access on the approved guardrail ID and numbered version, and deny inference when they do not match.
choices.explanation: This can reject the inference request itself when the guardrail is omitted or an unapproved version is used.

source.label: Bedrock推論におけるガードレールの強制

learning.reason: Make the required guardrail and version conditions for inference, and deny calls that do not meet them.
learning.concept: An operational rule that applications should follow instructions differs from a control enforced through permissions.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Enforce inference data-retention settings by Region
prompt: The applications use the Bedrock Responses API. Organizational policy requires that inference inputs and outputs not be kept in service-side persistent storage for the target accounts in permitted Regions. Use only candidate models that support this setting. What should be configured?

choices.text: Set the retention mode to none in the accounts in the target Regions, and select models that support that setting.
choices.explanation: This can disable persistent service-side retention, and you can also check that the models support operating without retention.

choices.text: Only set the save flag to false on each request, leaving the data-retention mode at its default.
choices.explanation: This controls whether the response can be retrieved, but some models may retain data for other purposes.

choices.text: Only disable the setting that saves model outputs to your own S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Changing a customer-managed storage destination does not configure data retention by the inference service.

choices.text: Configure data retention only in a separate Region used for administration, and leave the permitted Regions at their defaults.
choices.explanation: The retention mode does not propagate to other Regions; it must be configured in the Region where inference runs.

source.label: Amazon Bedrockのデータ保持モード

learning.reason: Distinguish a setting that prevents retrieving a response later from one that prohibits retention by the service itself.
learning.concept: The setting applies by Region, and requests to models that require retention are rejected if they do not meet the condition.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Monitor intervention counts without collecting content
prompt: You want to track the number of items processed and the number of interventions made by Bedrock Guardrails each day. During normal operations, inquiry text and generated outputs must not be stored in monitoring storage. Which data should you use?

choices.text: Save inputs and outputs in model invocation logs, then convert them into daily counts.
choices.explanation: Although you could aggregate counts, the content that must not be stored would first be written to the logs.

choices.text: Aggregate invocation and intervention counts from Guardrails CloudWatch metrics.
choices.explanation: These metrics provide the counts needed for monitoring without storing content.

choices.text: Treat the number of CloudTrail management events for configuration changes as the number of guardrail interventions.
choices.explanation: The number of management actions is not the number of actual evaluations or interventions.

choices.text: Aggregate vector-store writes as the number of guardrail evaluations.
choices.explanation: These count a different process, such as ingestion, and do not correspond to evaluations or interventions.

source.label: Bedrock GuardrailsのCloudWatchメトリクス

learning.reason: Use metrics needed to aggregate counts rather than logs that collect individual inputs and outputs.
learning.concept: If monitoring requires only totals, detailed logs that collect content do not need to be enabled.

title: Use prefecture names as features
prompt: The input to a price-prediction model includes a string column called “region.” You want the model to handle differences between region categories, not the number of characters in each region name. Which preprocessing step is appropriate?

choices.text: Delete all region names
choices.explanation: This may discard useful regional differences.

choices.text: Encode the categories and convert them into features
choices.explanation: This represents the discrete region categories as model inputs.

choices.text: Use region names as the labels for sales volume
choices.explanation: This confuses the target variable with a feature.

choices.text: Convert the strings into images
choices.explanation: This is not a direct way to handle categories.

source.label: SageMaker Canvas データ分析

learning.reason: Convert the categorical column into features the model can handle.
learning.concept: Preprocessing serves different purposes for numerical, categorical, text, and image data.

title: Using Probabilities for Decisions
prompt: A sales representative prioritizes customers based on a “70% probability of purchase.” They want to confirm that the actual purchase rate is also about 70% among customers assigned a 70% probability. What property describes this?

choices.text: Object detection in images
choices.explanation: This concerns locating objects in images.

choices.text: Inference latency
choices.explanation: This is response time; it does not describe what a probability means.

choices.text: Probability calibration
choices.explanation: This describes whether predicted probabilities align with observed event frequencies.

choices.text: Data encryption
choices.explanation: This protects data; it does not describe the validity of predicted probabilities.

source.label: AIF-C01 Domain 1 試験ガイド

learning.reason: When probabilities are used for business decisions, their calibration should be checked.
learning.concept: Even if a model ranks cases correctly, its probability values do not necessarily reflect actual frequencies.

title: Gradually Releasing a New Model
prompt: A new credit model performed better in offline evaluation, but you want to avoid switching all production traffic to it immediately. What is the best way to monitor it with a small portion of live traffic and be able to return to the previous version if problems arise?

choices.text: Switch all traffic to the new model without evaluation
choices.explanation: This can expose all traffic to unexpected effects.

choices.text: Delete the new model and discard the evaluation results
choices.explanation: This prevents you from validating a promising candidate.

choices.text: Only change the order of rows in the training data
choices.explanation: This is not a safe production rollout method.

choices.text: Gradually route a small portion of traffic to it, monitor metrics, and keep rollback possible
choices.explanation: This lets you compare the new and old versions while limiting production risk.

source.label: SageMaker Model Monitor

learning.reason: A gradual rollout with monitoring limits the impact on production.
learning.concept: Offline evaluation and quality checks in production complement each other.

title: Increasing the Variety of a Small Image Dataset
prompt: There are few inspection images, and left-right flips or changes in brightness may occur in production. Which technique can help generalization by increasing the variety of training examples while preserving their meaning?

choices.text: Data augmentation
choices.explanation: Plausible transformations such as rotation or brightness changes can increase the diversity of training examples.

choices.text: Provide the correct production labels as input
choices.explanation: The correct labels are not available at inference time.

choices.text: Delete all images unconditionally
choices.explanation: This discards useful training information.

choices.text: Cache inference results
choices.explanation: This does not increase the variety of training examples.

source.label: AIF-C01 Domain 1 試験ガイド

learning.reason: Use meaning-preserving transformations to increase diversity during training.
learning.concept: Limit augmentation to changes that could occur in the business setting, and preserve the meaning of the labels.

title: Measuring a Model’s Business Impact
prompt: A new recommendation model has stronger offline metrics. You want to compare whether it actually improves purchase or return rates. Which method compares the old and new models over the same period by splitting users into two groups?

choices.text: Only deduplicate the training data
choices.explanation: This does not compare business impact in production.

choices.text: A/B testing
choices.explanation: This compares the effects of different models on real users during the same period.

choices.text: Report a single successful example
choices.explanation: This cannot rule out chance or selection bias.

choices.text: Change the model name
choices.explanation: This does not measure outcomes.

source.label: AIF-C01 Domain 1 試験ガイド

learning.reason: Use A/B testing to compare business metrics in production.
