title: Speeding Up Post-Meeting Follow-Up
prompt: You want to create a list of decisions and owners from a meeting. However, the recording also contains proposals that are still under consideration. Distributing an item with no assigned owner as if the assignment were confirmed could lead to rework. Which role is appropriate for generative AI using the transcript?

choices.text: Treat every proposal in the discussion as a confirmed decision, fill in the name of the most likely owner, and distribute the list.
choices.explanation: This produces a list quickly, but it confuses decisions with unresolved items and may assign work to the wrong person.

choices.text: Create only a single paragraph summarizing the meeting in chronological order, without listing owners or decision status in a table.
choices.explanation: This gives readers a summary, but does not meet the goal of clearly identifying decisions and unresolved items.

choices.text: Draft separate sections for decisions and items under consideration. Mark items with no stated owner as unassigned and send them for confirmation.
choices.explanation: This supports post-meeting organization without making up details where information is missing.

choices.text: Use only the transcript headings to identify the relevant departments and assign tasks without checking whether the meeting reached a decision.
choices.explanation: A department may be relevant, but that does not mean it was agreed upon as the owner or that a decision was made.

source.label: Amazon Bedrock prompt engineering concepts

learning.reason: Generative AI can use existing information, such as a transcript, to draft action items for review.
learning.concept: Speech recognition and organizing or generating content from recognized text are separate tasks.

title: Measuring the Value of Reducing Rework on Support Inquiries
prompt: The goal of a trial in which support agents use suggested replies is to speed up first responses without increasing low-quality answers. The trial group and the control group receive inquiries of similar difficulty. Which metrics are best suited to deciding whether to adopt the trial?

choices.text: Measure only the inference time of the generative model and the number of model errors.
choices.explanation: These metrics show whether the model is operating, but not the final response time after human edits or the quality of replies that agents can use.

choices.text: Measure only the trial group's total number of replies and how many times the generative feature was displayed.
choices.explanation: These metrics show usage, but not whether first responses became faster or whether the suggested replies were high quality.

choices.text: Measure only the cost of generating suggested replies, without evaluating the time until customers receive a reply.
choices.explanation: This shows inference costs, but does not address the trial's main goals of improving response time and quality.

choices.text: Measure both the time to first response and the share of suggested replies used without substantial revision.
choices.explanation: Together, these metrics assess speed and the quality of replies that agents can use.

source.label: AWS CAF: Accelerating business outcomes

learning.reason: Assess generative AI by business outcomes such as rework, response time, and usable quality, rather than by the number of generations.
learning.concept: Business KPIs measure the change experienced by users or customers, rather than the volume of technical usage.

title: Prototyping a Generative AI Interface Without Business Data
prompt: In a product-development workshop, participants need to prototype and share the interface and features of a generative AI app without writing code. They will use only fictional sample data, and do not need a production environment or connections to external systems. Which option is a good fit?

choices.text: Use PartyRock’s no-code environment to prototype an app with sample data and share it with the participants.
choices.explanation: This lets participants prototype a generative AI app with an interface without first setting up a production environment.

choices.text: Build a custom web interface that calls a model through the Amazon Bedrock API, with each participant setting up a backend.
choices.explanation: This allows a flexible design, but does not meet the requirement that participants write no code.

choices.text: Use only the console’s chat playground, without creating a shareable app that accepts input and produces output.
choices.explanation: Participants can try model responses, but this leaves the requirement to prototype and share a user-facing app interface unmet.

choices.text: Have each team train a custom model in SageMaker AI before starting to build the interface.
choices.explanation: Training a custom model is unnecessary here and adds preparation to a short prototyping exercise.

source.label: PartyRockのノーコード生成AI試作

learning.reason: A no-code playground is suitable when the goal is to learn with samples and prototype an app with an interface.
learning.concept: Sharing a prototype is different from running a production system that requires business-data controls or availability.

title: Changing One Part of an Image Without Redrawing the Whole Image
prompt: A photo for promotional use has an approved product appearance and logo. Only an unwanted object in the background needs to be replaced. If the existing image and the area to change can be provided as input, which generative feature fits the request?

choices.text: Generate an entirely new photo from a text description of the image.
choices.explanation: This may produce a similar composition, but does not let you keep the existing product and logo while changing only the object.

choices.text: Specify the original image and a mask for the object, then edit that area with inpainting.
choices.explanation: This limits the edit to the object and helps preserve the approved content around it.

choices.text: Expand the area outside the image using outpainting.
choices.explanation: This can extend the frame, but does not replace a specified area within the image.

choices.text: Create an image embedding and search for similar existing photos.
choices.explanation: This may find similar images, but it does not edit the object in the photo you intend to use.

source.label: Amazon BedrockのStability AI画像機能

learning.reason: For a partial edit with a specified replacement area, generation can preserve the approved content around it.
learning.concept: After generation, check that the final image has not changed unintended areas.

sourceLabel: Amazon Bedrock Stability AI image capabilities

title: Create a Short Video from a Still Image
prompt: You are prototyping a short video to introduce a new product. You want to use an approved product photo as the first frame and generate the camera movement that follows from a text prompt. Which capability should you look for when comparing video generation services?

choices.text: Generate video from text without using the approved photo as input.
choices.explanation: You can specify movement, but this does not meet the requirement to use the approved photo as the first frame.

choices.text: Use an image editing model to make targeted edits to the source image and create several still images.
choices.explanation: This can adjust still images, but it does not generate a video with camera movement.

choices.text: Image-to-video generation that uses a reference image as the first frame and also accepts text describing the movement.
choices.explanation: This meets both requirements: starting from the approved image and specifying the subsequent movement in text.

choices.text: Give the product photo to a video understanding model and have it output only a description of the movement.
choices.explanation: It can describe the content, but it does not output moving footage.

source.label: 画像からの動画生成方式の例（提供終了モデルの技術資料）

learning.reason: Specify the initial appearance with an image, then add text describing the movement that follows.
learning.concept: First check whether the model outputs a video, a still image, or a description of an image.

sourceLabel: Example of an image-to-video generation method (technical material for a discontinued model)

title: Handle Interruptions During Voice Guidance
prompt: In a simulated reception desk that users can interact with by voice, users must be able to start speaking midway through a long response and change their question. Processing the recording afterward is not an option; both the user's speech and generated audio must be handled in real time. Which capability is the best fit?

choices.text: Transcribe a recording with Amazon Transcribe after the call ends, then generate an answer from its contents.
choices.explanation: Transcription is possible, but processing after the call ends cannot respond in the middle of the conversation.

choices.text: Synthesize a fixed guidance script with Amazon Polly and play it to the end regardless of what the user says.
choices.explanation: This produces audio output but does not handle user input or interruptions.

choices.text: Generate dialogue in advance and play the same recording for each question.
choices.explanation: Playback may be immediate, but it cannot generate an answer based on a question that changes mid-response.

choices.text: Use Nova 2 Sonic audio streams and discard queued audio when an interruption notification arrives.
choices.explanation: It handles audio in both directions, and the client can stop queued, outdated audio and switch to the user's new utterance.

source.label: Amazon Nova 2 Sonicの発話割り込み

learning.reason: An audio model that handles bidirectional streams can support interactions that accept input while responding.
learning.concept: Transcribing a recording and synthesizing speech from text are not the same as real-time, two-way interaction.

title: Route to a More Capable Model Only When Needed for the Same Use Case
prompt: A single reception API handles short, routine requests as well as requests involving several interacting conditions. Requests of varying difficulty come from the same user, and their attributes alone cannot distinguish them. You want to route each request among supported models in the same family based on predicted answer quality and cost. What should you use?

choices.text: Use intelligent prompt routing with a supported model family.
choices.explanation: Because it can choose a model for each input, it is an option for controlling cost based on the quality required.

choices.text: Route every response to the largest model and distribute requests only across processing Regions.
choices.explanation: This may increase available capacity, but it does not select a smaller model for different inputs.

choices.text: Choose a model at first login and use that same model for all subsequent requests from that user.
choices.explanation: This can fix a model per user, but does not account for requests of varying difficulty from the same user.

choices.text: Always run two models in parallel for every user request and use only the shorter answer.
choices.explanation: This runs both inference requests every time, and answer length does not indicate business quality.

source.label: Amazon Bedrockのインテリジェントプロンプトルーティング

learning.reason: Use routing based on each input's suitability among supported models in the same family.
learning.concept: Selecting a model for each request differs from serving the same model from another Region.

title: Distinguish Missing Retrieval from Missing Citations
prompt: Evaluate a RAG system that answers questions from policies. The reference data also includes the evidence statements needed for the answers. Match each metric to its purpose so that distinct failure modes are not confused.

choices.text: Citation coverage
choices.explanation: Evaluates whether any citations needed to support the answer are missing.

choices.text: Context coverage
choices.explanation: Evaluates how much of the required information shown in the reference data is present in the retrieved results.

choices.text: Citation precision
choices.explanation: Evaluates how many of the cited passages are correct citations.

source.label: BedrockのRAG評価指標

learning.reason: Assessing the scope of retrieved evidence, links to incorrect citations, and missing required citations are separate tasks.
learning.concept: Retrieving evidence and citing that evidence correctly are different stages.

prompts.text: Measure whether any of the reference evidence is missing from the search results.
Measure whether the cited passages actually support the claims.
Measure whether any claims in the answer lack a required citation.

title: Review generated SQL before execution
prompt: You want to obtain SQL for structured order data from a natural-language question about the number of orders. Execution must be limited to SQL approved by an internal review process. In Bedrock Knowledge Bases, how should generation and execution be separated?

choices.text: Create an answer with RetrieveAndGenerate, then check whether the executed SQL was appropriate.
choices.explanation: Data retrieval begins before the SQL can be reviewed.

choices.text: Convert the order table into document chunks and use vector-search scores to decide whether to approve the SQL.
choices.explanation: Relevance scoring is different from checking whether SQL meets the approval criteria.

choices.text: Add “use only approved SQL” to the question and execute the result automatically.
choices.explanation: An instruction can be provided before generation, but that does not mean the actual output has been reviewed.

choices.text: Use GenerateQuery to obtain SQL from natural language, and execute it only if it passes review.
choices.explanation: This lets you decide whether to proceed with the generated SQL before retrieving results.

source.label: 構造化データのクエリ生成

learning.reason: Retrieve and inspect only the generated SQL, then execute approved SQL in a separate step.
learning.concept: The API that generates SQL can be separated from the process that uses it to retrieve data.

title: Find matching product photos from a description
prompt: In a parts search service, a user enters “a bracket with two holes on the side,” and you want to list similar parts photos. The photos have no captions. How can you search for similar existing images without generating new ones?

choices.text: Convert the images and input text into multimodal embeddings, then search for image vectors that are close to the text vector.
choices.explanation: This lets you find existing photos based on the visual features described by the input text.

choices.text: Generate an image from the input text and return only the generated image as the search result.
choices.explanation: This can create an image matching the input's meaning, but it does not search the registered parts photos.

choices.text: Create text embeddings from the product photo filenames and exclude the visual content of the photos from the index.
choices.explanation: Without descriptions, filenames cannot represent photo content such as the number of holes.

choices.text: Extract text from the photos and search for matches with the input text.
choices.explanation: This can find markings, but it cannot match shapes that are not described in text.

source.label: Amazon Titan Multimodal Embeddings

learning.reason: Represent text and images in a space where they can be compared, then select existing images close to the query vector.
learning.concept: Embeddings for search serve a different purpose from generating new images or reading text within images.

title: Identify which stage produced a misclassification
prompt: A request is classified, and a draft is generated based on that classification. A single model invocation currently returns only the final result, so you cannot tell whether an incorrect draft resulted from a classification failure or a drafting failure. Choose an architecture that lets you test each stage separately before release.

choices.text: Keep the single invocation and infer the classification from part of the draft.
choices.explanation: An error in the final draft does not reveal the internal classification result with certainty.

choices.text: Extract and validate the classification result separately, then pass it to draft generation.
choices.explanation: You can compare the inputs and outputs of each stage and pinpoint where an error occurred.

choices.text: Use a model retrained for classification and drafting, and return only the draft.
choices.explanation: Even if quality changes, the stage where a failure occurred remains unobservable.

choices.text: Lower the model temperature and infer whether the classification is correct from how reproducible the draft is.
choices.explanation: The model can produce highly reproducible responses to the same misclassification.

source.label: Bedrockのプロンプト設計

learning.reason: Make the classification result explicit and validate it before using it to draft a response; this allows you to assess quality at each stage.
learning.concept: Separating tasks lets you score intermediate outputs or restrict them to an approved set of values.

title: Isolate the effect of adding examples
prompt: Using the same foundation model, compare a version with instructions only against a version that adds examples to the instructions. You want to determine whether adding examples improves the results. Which plan is appropriate?

choices.text: For the version with examples, use examples already included in the prompt as inputs; for the instructions-only version, use examples the model has not seen before.
choices.explanation: The evaluation conditions differ, so you cannot isolate the difference between the prompts.

choices.text: Use a low temperature for the instructions-only version and a high temperature for the version with examples, then compare them on the same inputs.
choices.explanation: Temperature also differs, so you cannot attribute the improvement solely to adding examples.

choices.text: Keep the model settings fixed and score both versions on the same queries that were not used in the examples.
choices.explanation: The model and evaluation conditions are held constant, so you can compare the effect of adding examples.

choices.text: Use a larger model only for the version with examples, then compare both versions on business data.
choices.explanation: You can compare the overall configurations, but you cannot isolate the effect of adding examples.

source.label: Prompt managementでの版の比較

learning.reason: Use the same evaluation examples and model settings for both versions, changing only the prompt structure to isolate the effect of adding examples.
learning.concept: Prompts and evaluation sets serve different purposes; examples used in the prompt should not be included in the evaluation results.

title: Evaluating Translations Beyond Word Order
prompt: Some translations preserve the meaning while differing from the reference in word order or word choice. Because word-sequence matching alone can score them poorly, you want a supplementary metric that captures semantic similarity to the reference. Which metric best fits this goal?

choices.text: Use BLEU alone to measure word-sequence overlap.
choices.explanation: BLEU can be used to evaluate translations, but it still depends on surface-level overlap, which is what you want to supplement here.

choices.text: Calculate the proportion of phrases in the reference that also appear in the candidate.
choices.explanation: This measures surface overlap and is unlikely to capture paraphrases with the same meaning.

choices.text: Measure the length ratio between the reference and the candidate.
choices.explanation: This shows length differences but does not determine whether the meanings match.

choices.text: Use BERTScore as a supplementary metric to compare translation similarity with context-aware embeddings.
choices.explanation: This supplements the evaluation of semantic similarity without relying only on identical words.

source.label: BERTScoreの一次研究

learning.reason: BERTScore compares translations using context-aware vector representations, adding a perspective that differs from surface-level overlap.
learning.concept: A score from an automatic metric alone cannot establish that a translation is error-free. For important material, also check terminology and numbers.

title: Validate an Automatically Optimized Prompt Before Release
prompt: Prompt optimization made the style of equipment maintenance logs easier to read, but some outputs confuse kilowatt-hours with megawatt-hours. Preserving the units accurately is mandatory, and you also want to improve readability. Which evaluation should you use to select the version for release?

choices.text: Score unit preservation and readability separately on the same independent validation examples, then select a version that meets both requirements.
choices.explanation: This lets you compare style improvements on the same data without overlooking degradation in a mandatory requirement.

choices.text: Release the version with the highest style score and use production complaints to find unit errors.
choices.explanation: This does not verify before release that the mandatory unit-preservation requirement is met.

choices.text: Score using validation examples that contain only megawatt-hours, and do not measure other units or style quality.
choices.explanation: This tests only one side of a common mix-up and cannot compare readability.

choices.text: Compare only whether the input and output contain the same number of unit strings, and use that as the release criterion.
choices.explanation: The counts can match even when units are swapped between different values, so this does not check which unit belongs to which number.

source.label: Bedrockのプロンプト最適化時の評価

learning.reason: Measure style and unit accuracy separately. Do not decide on release based only on an average score for either one.
learning.concept: Treat business-critical requirements as gates, and define how to measure them before comparing candidates.

title: Move the Same Business Instructions to Another Model
prompt: To improve response time, you are moving inquiry classification to a new model. Using the current prompt as is lowers the quality of both the output format and the classifications. Which approach revises the prompt while preserving the same business decisions without changing the model weights?

choices.text: Optimize the prompt only for the source model and do not evaluate it on the destination model.
choices.explanation: A prompt that works well with the source model will not necessarily maintain the same quality on a new model.

choices.text: Optimize the prompt for the destination model and compare its results against the existing pass/fail criteria.
choices.explanation: This adapts the prompt to the destination model's response tendencies without changing its weights, and checks performance against the same criteria as before.

choices.text: Replace the original evaluation labels to match the destination model.
choices.explanation: This may improve agreement between outputs and labels, but it does not preserve the business classification criteria.

choices.text: Raise only the character limit and judge classification quality by the length of the resulting output.
choices.explanation: A longer output is not necessarily classified correctly.

source.label: Amazon Bedrockのプロンプト移行と最適化

learning.reason: Adapt the prompt to the destination model, then recheck quality using the fixed evaluation data.
learning.concept: When the model changes, the same instructions can have different effects, so evaluate the prompt and model together.

sourceLabel: Amazon Bedrock prompt migration and optimization

title: Use Pre-Split Short Documents As They Are
prompt: The FAQ content has already been split into short files, each containing one question-and-answer pair. You want each pair to be returned as a single retrieval unit, and page-number citations are not needed. Which chunking strategy should you use during ingestion?

choices.text: Combine all FAQs into one file and treat the entire file as a single unit.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve a separate retrieval unit for each question-and-answer pair.

choices.text: Re-split each file into a small fixed number of tokens, even if a boundary falls within a question.
choices.explanation: The question and answer could be retrieved separately, which does not meet the requirement to return them as a pair.

choices.text: Keep the pre-created one-pair-per-file structure and select no chunking during ingestion.
choices.explanation: This preserves the original units, keeping each question and its answer in the same retrieval unit.

choices.text: Apply hierarchical chunking to every file without regard to the question-and-answer pairing in each file.
choices.explanation: If each pair is already split into its own file, further chunking during ingestion is unnecessary to preserve it.

source.label: Bedrock Knowledge Basesのチャンク分割

learning.reason: If each file is already the retrieval unit you need, choose the setting that does not split it further during ingestion.
learning.concept: When preserving pre-split content, also check constraints such as file size and the handling of page information.

title: Return Only Reviewed Text During Streaming
prompt: In an internal chat that displays generated text a little at a time, an output filter must not allow unevaluated text to be displayed first. A small delay is acceptable, but streaming must be retained. Which approach should you choose?

choices.text: Process the output stream synchronously and display the reviewed content incrementally.
choices.explanation: This allows the required checks to run before output is sent while preserving streaming.

choices.text: Prioritize time to first token and evaluate the output asynchronously.
choices.explanation: A portion that has already been sent could later be judged problematic.

choices.text: Check only the input synchronously and stream the output without checking it.
choices.explanation: Blocking unsafe input in advance does not check the generated text.

choices.text: Stream the output, then check the full text at the end and remove the portions already displayed.
choices.explanation: Removing text from the display does not change the fact that unevaluated content was delivered first.

source.label: Bedrockのストリーミング検査

learning.reason: Choose an approach that buffers the output and returns only the portions that pass inspection, in sequence.
learning.concept: Sending output immediately and evaluating it afterward can reduce latency, but unevaluated content may arrive first.

title: Compare Synthetic-Data Performance with Real Inputs
prompt: A rare defect in component images is uncommon in real images, so generated images were used to increase the number of training examples. Performance is good when evaluated only on synthetic images. Before release, choose two ways to check whether the model can handle defects found in the factory.

choices.text: Set aside real images that were used neither to generate synthetic data nor for training as an evaluation set.
choices.explanation: This lets you assess performance on real inputs separately from the effects of training.

choices.text: Use only new random seeds from the generator used for training to add synthetic images for the final acceptance decision.
choices.explanation: Biases from the same generator remain, and this does not directly evaluate performance on real defects.

choices.text: Mix synthetic examples and real images, then use only overall accuracy to decide whether to release.
choices.explanation: Results from the many synthetic examples can make errors on the few real images harder to see.

choices.text: Aggregate results by defect type on real images and compare them with the results obtained from synthetic data.
choices.explanation: This can reveal weaknesses for defects that matter in production and differences between real and synthetic images.

choices.text: Use an image-generation model to score only the visual quality of the generated images.
choices.explanation: Visual quality is separate from the classifier's ability to detect real defects.

source.label: 責任あるAIでの拡張・合成データの検証

learning.reason: A high score on data produced by the same generation method used for training does not guarantee good performance on real images.
learning.concept: Even when synthetic data is used for training, evaluate separately on the real-world distribution and check performance under important conditions.

sourceLabel: Validating augmented and synthetic data for responsible AI

title: Measure Differences in Selection Rates
prompt: A company already uses SageMaker Clarify. Its model predicts priority for training invitations and has similar accuracy in Region A and Region B. The sample size is sufficient for comparison, but the proportion of people selected by the model as invitation candidates differs. The current question is the difference in predicted positive rates between the regions. Which Clarify metric directly addresses this?

choices.text: Calculate Accuracy across all data.
choices.explanation: This shows agreement between predictions and actual labels, but it does not compare the predicted positive rate in each region.

choices.text: Calculate Difference in Positive Proportions in Predicted Labels.
choices.explanation: This metric measures the difference in predicted positive rates between the regions.

choices.text: Calculate Class Imbalance from the number of training records in each region.
choices.explanation: This shows differences in record counts between regions, but does not compare the model's selection rates.

choices.text: Recall Difference
choices.explanation: This compares which people with actual positive labels were selected; it differs from the predicted positive rate across everyone.

source.label: Clarifyの学習後のバイアス指標

learning.reason: The quantity of interest is the difference in the proportion of predicted positives in each region, not accuracy against actual labels.
learning.concept: Choose a fairness metric based on what you want to compare; no single value represents every form of unfairness.

title: Find Poor Outcomes Beyond Complaints
prompt: Reviewers evaluating generated guidance assess quality only from complaints submitted by users. They also want to catch errors affecting groups of users who may be less likely to submit complaints. The business team can sample usage scenarios and outcomes. Which method should they add?

choices.text: Assume that usage scenarios with few complaints have low error rates and narrow the review scope.
choices.explanation: Differences in how likely people are to report issues are treated as differences in outcome quality.

choices.text: Sample only responses that users rated highly and compare them with complaints.
choices.explanation: The bias toward users who are more likely to submit ratings remains.

choices.text: Sample by usage scenario and have people review the samples against established criteria, regardless of whether a complaint was submitted.
choices.explanation: This includes scenarios from people who do not submit ratings or complaints in human review.

choices.text: Collect only the number of responses during operation and divide the number of complaints by the number of responses.
choices.explanation: This measures the reporting rate but does not check for errors that go unreported.

source.label: 生成AI運用でのフィードバックの収集

learning.reason: Add human review based on samples less subject to reporting bias, alongside reports submitted voluntarily by users.
learning.concept: Voluntary reports alone can be biased by factors related to whether people choose to report.

sourceLabel: Collecting feedback during generative AI operations

title: Verify that guardrails work for each target language
prompt: You approved a guardrail using only Japanese and want to use it for chats in English and Spanish as well. Which TWO actions should you take before deployment to confirm that the filters work in the new languages and do not unnecessarily reject ordinary messages?

choices.text: Use the Japanese results as-is to determine whether the new languages pass.
choices.explanation: This does not evaluate language-specific phrasing or false positives.

choices.text: Confirm that the selected filters and configuration support the languages you plan to use.
choices.explanation: Support can vary depending on the configuration and filter type.

choices.text: For the new languages, score only short, fixed English messages instead of evaluating users’ messages.
choices.explanation: This does not test the target-language phrasing or measure variation within the same language.

choices.text: Create allowed and denied examples in each language and compare the results with the expected decisions.
choices.explanation: This checks both content that should be blocked and content that should be allowed.

choices.text: Display every term covered by privacy classification as a quotation and use the display count as a safety metric.
choices.explanation: This does not test the required filter behavior or inform decisions about what to display.

source.label: Bedrock Guardrailsの対応範囲

learning.reason: First confirm that the features you plan to use support each language, then measure their behavior with phrasing drawn from actual usage.
learning.concept: A standard validated in one language cannot necessarily be applied unchanged to another.

title: Do not mistake prediction explanations for causal evidence
prompt: In a model that predicts maintenance contract renewals, the feature for usage hours had a strong influence on many predictions. The sales team wants to tell customers, “Increasing usage hours will raise the renewal rate.” What can reasonably be concluded from the current feature-attribution results?

choices.text: For a feature with a large contribution, the effects of actions that change it have also been established.
choices.explanation: A feature’s contribution to predictions must be distinguished from a real-world causal relationship.

choices.text: Increasing usage hours raises the probability of renewal by a fixed percentage for every device.
choices.explanation: An average contribution does not establish the direction or magnitude of change for every customer.

choices.text: Removing usage hours as an input lets you predict how measured renewal rates will change.
choices.explanation: Removing an input may change the model’s output, but that does not prove that customer behavior will change.

choices.text: The model relies heavily on usage hours, but the effect of an intervention to change usage hours requires separate evaluation.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes what the prediction explanation established from the causal effect that has not yet been tested.

source.label: Clarifyの特徴量寄与の分析結果

learning.reason: A feature’s contribution to a model’s predictions does not prove that an intervention will change the outcome.
learning.concept: Feature attribution explains a model’s predictions. The effects of a business intervention require separate evaluation.

sourceLabel: Analysis results for feature attribution in Clarify

title: Minimize data used for AI evaluation
prompt: You are asking an external contractor to evaluate an AI model’s quality. The contractor does not need customer identifiers but does need attribute distributions and usage patterns. What is the most appropriate way to prepare the data?

choices.text: Encrypt the entire production dataset before sharing it.
choices.explanation: If the contractor can decrypt it, encryption does not prevent you from providing identifiers that are not needed.

choices.text: Share a dataset containing only the attributes needed for the evaluation, with direct identifiers removed.
choices.explanation: This limits the data to what the purpose requires and excludes unnecessary identifiers.

choices.text: Share the production data, including identifiers, as read-only.
choices.explanation: Read-only access does not minimize the data.

choices.text: Share every field on the understanding that it will be deleted after the evaluation.
choices.explanation: Deleting data afterward is no substitute for avoiding unnecessary collection in the first place.

source.label: AWS Machine Learning Lensのデータ最小化

learning.reason: For AI evaluation too, design the data handling so that it uses only the data needed for the purpose.
learning.concept: Data minimization.

sourceLabel: Data minimization in the AWS Machine Learning Lens

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Assess anonymization and re-identification risk
prompt: You removed names from a dataset for AI analysis, but there is concern that individuals could be identified from combinations of ZIP code, date of birth, and gender. What is the most appropriate conclusion?

choices.text: Once names are removed, the data should always be considered anonymized.
choices.explanation: This ignores the possibility of re-identification through quasi-identifiers.

choices.text: Compress the analysis data before storing it.
choices.explanation: Compression does not reduce re-identification risk.

choices.text: Do not treat the data as anonymized based only on removing direct identifiers; assess re-identification risk from combinations of quasi-identifiers.
choices.explanation: Even without names, combinations of other attributes may link records to individuals.

choices.text: Reorder the rows in the dataset.
choices.explanation: Reordering does not change whether combinations of attributes can identify someone.

source.label: NIST SP 800-188のデータ非識別化とガバナンス

learning.reason: An anonymization assessment must also consider combinations of attributes beyond direct identifiers.
learning.concept: Quasi-identifiers and re-identification risk.

sourceLabel: Data de-identification and governance in NIST SP 800-188

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Check the permitted use of data under the agreement
prompt: You want to repurpose a dataset obtained from a third party to evaluate a new generative AI feature. The agreement permits its use only for the existing demand forecasting purpose. What is the most appropriate action?

choices.text: Copy the data to a different bucket before using it.
choices.explanation: Changing the storage location does not change the permitted purpose under the agreement.

choices.text: Use the data without checking, as long as it is only in an evaluation environment.
choices.explanation: Even for evaluation, use outside the scope permitted by the agreement is not authorized.

choices.text: Encrypt the data so that the purpose restriction no longer applies.
choices.explanation: Encryption is a protection measure, not a substitute for the terms of use.

choices.text: Before repurposing the data, confirm that the new purpose is permitted under the agreement and, if necessary, update the agreement with the provider.
choices.explanation: Data use must comply with the purposes permitted by the agreement, in addition to being technically feasible.

source.label: AWS Machine Learning Lensの利用許諾の確認

learning.reason: Data governance requires checking technical feasibility separately from the contractual permission to use the data.
learning.concept: Data use terms and contractual compliance.

sourceLabel: AWS Machine Learning Lens: Verify Usage Rights

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Analyze data together without disclosing raw data
prompt: Two companies want to evaluate an AI initiative by counting overlapping customers without disclosing their customer data to each other. Which AWS service is most appropriate?

choices.text: Configure a collaborative analysis in AWS Clean Rooms.
choices.explanation: Clean Rooms lets participants perform collaborative analysis without sharing or revealing their underlying data.

choices.text: Make a full copy of the data in the other company’s S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the requirement to avoid disclosing raw data.

choices.text: Exchange encrypted CSV files by email.
choices.explanation: Encryption does not change the fact that the raw data is being handed to the other company.

choices.text: Have only one company calculate the result and report it verbally.
choices.explanation: This does not provide a collaboratively verifiable analysis design.

source.label: AWS Clean Rooms User Guide

learning.reason: Collaborative analysis can provide the aggregate needed for the purpose while avoiding disclosure of the underlying data.
learning.concept: Privacy-protecting collaborative analysis.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Choose a protection boundary for data in use
prompt: When processing sensitive AI features, code must run in a computing environment isolated even from the host administrator. Which AWS feature is most appropriate?

choices.text: Make the EC2 instance name private.
choices.explanation: Naming does not create an isolation boundary for data in use.

choices.text: Use AWS Nitro Enclaves to create an isolated compute environment.
choices.explanation: Nitro Enclaves provide a compute environment isolated from the parent instance and can be used to isolate sensitive data processing.

choices.text: Extend the retention period for CloudWatch metrics.
choices.explanation: Metric retention does not isolate the compute environment.

choices.text: Configure an S3 lifecycle rule.
choices.explanation: This manages stored data; it does not isolate processing while data is in use.

source.label: AWS Nitro Enclaves User Guide

learning.reason: Design an isolation boundary for data in use in addition to encryption at rest.
learning.concept: Confidential computing.

title: Only the prediction scores suddenly shift lower
prompt: The production input distribution is nearly the same as last month, but immediately after a model deployment, prediction scores suddenly drop across the board. The drop is reproducible for the same inputs. What information should be compared first?

choices.text: Retrain every model to match the input distribution from the past month, without comparing it with the latest version.
choices.explanation: The observed issue is a score difference before and after deployment. Starting with retraining would not isolate what changed.

choices.text: Compare the model versions, inference processing, and preprocessing before and after the change, then compare outputs at each stage using the same inputs.
choices.explanation: This can determine whether a deployment difference coinciding with the change caused scores to differ for identical inputs.

choices.text: Wait for the ground-truth labels to arrive and decide whether to change the threshold based only on aggregate accuracy.
choices.explanation: This may measure a change in evaluation results, but it does not explain why scores for the same inputs suddenly changed.

choices.text: Check whether the request volume changed and skip comparisons using the same inputs.
choices.explanation: This may reveal a change in usage volume, but it cannot explain a score change that also occurs for identical inputs.

source.label: AWS Well-Architectedの障害調査

learning.reason: When the inputs are identical, first trace differences in the runtime environment, versions, and transformations.
learning.concept: Production monitoring should correlate model versions and output distributions with input data.

title: Monitoring with Actuals Available One Month Later
prompt: A demand forecast returns a prediction at forecast time, but actual sales are finalized one month later. What record-keeping design is needed to match each forecast with its actual result by store, product, and day, and measure the error once the actuals are finalized?

choices.text: Store only the distribution of forecast scores for each day, then compare it with the distribution of actuals one month later.
choices.explanation: The distributions can be compared, but this does not provide the error for each individual forecast target.

choices.text: Store only finalized actuals, then recreate the forecasts at evaluation time using the latest model available then.
choices.explanation: If the model or reference data has changed, this cannot evaluate the forecasts that were actually delivered at the time.

choices.text: Store each forecast with a key that identifies its forecast time and target, then associate the finalized actual with the same key later.
choices.explanation: This makes it possible to calculate the error for each forecast against its corresponding finalized actual.

choices.text: Use proxy labels available before finalization for the final evaluation, without linking them to the actuals received later.
choices.explanation: This can show early trends, but it cannot measure error against finalized actuals.

source.label: SageMakerの正解データを用いたモデル品質監視

learning.reason: With delayed labels, forecasts and actuals must be joinable later.
learning.concept: Data quality monitoring and model quality monitoring using ground-truth labels take place at different times.

sourceLabel: SageMaker Model Quality Monitoring Using Ground Truth

title: What Cluster Numbers Mean
prompt: Unlabeled customer data was clustered, and the clusters were assigned the numbers 0, 1, and 2. Someone proposes treating cluster 2 as high-value customers. What should be checked before assigning business meaning?

choices.text: Treat the cluster numbers as a ranking of customer value and recommend the cluster with the highest number first.
choices.explanation: Cluster numbers may be assigned automatically and usually do not indicate a ranking of value.

choices.text: Use only the size of each cluster and designate the largest group as the most valuable customer segment.
choices.explanation: Size indicates the number of records, but it may not reflect purchasing behavior or customer value.

choices.text: Designate the cluster with the highest cohesion score as the most profitable group without examining business metrics.
choices.explanation: This score evaluates clustering structure; it does not measure business profitability.

choices.text: Examine each cluster’s usage frequency and purchasing patterns, then compare them with business metrics to interpret the numbers.
choices.explanation: The numbers are identifiers; interpret the clusters based on their characteristics and business evaluation.

source.label: AIF-C01 Domain 1 試験ガイド

learning.reason: Cluster numbers are identifiers; inspect each group’s characteristics before interpreting it for the business.
learning.concept: Results from unsupervised learning should be validated and interpreted in a business context before use.

title: Do Not Discard an Extreme Value Immediately
prompt: One transaction in the sales data is 100 times larger than usual. It has not yet been confirmed whether this is a data-entry error or a large contract. What is the most appropriate action before training?

choices.text: Check the original value and how the transaction occurred, then handle it according to whether it was an entry error or a genuine large transaction.
choices.explanation: Removing a genuine large transaction by mistake would reduce the number of training examples for a business that needs to account for large transactions.

choices.text: Immediately cap the value at a high percentile without checking whether it was entered incorrectly.
choices.explanation: This can limit the effect of an outlier, but it may also discard information about a valid sales amount.

choices.text: Train the model with robust statistics and skip the investigation into whether the original value is correct.
choices.explanation: This can make the model less dominated by one value, but it cannot determine whether the data is wrong.

choices.text: Augment the data with the extreme value as a rare large transaction so that the model gives it more weight.
choices.explanation: This does not establish whether the value is valid and distorts the transaction’s actual frequency.

source.label: SageMaker Canvas データ品質分析

learning.reason: Check the business meaning of an outlier before deciding how to handle it.
learning.concept: Do not confuse a data quality anomaly with a rare event that matters to the business.

title: A Baseline That Captures Seasonality
prompt: Demand for a product rises every Monday. You want to determine whether an advanced forecast that captures the day-of-week seasonality is valuable. Which baseline is appropriate for comparison?

choices.text: Use only the average across the entire period and exclude Mondays from the model evaluation.
choices.explanation: This does not let you assess the performance difference on days with seasonality.

choices.text: Prepare a forecast based on historical values for the same day of the week, then compare it with the advanced model over the same target period using the same error metric.
choices.explanation: Even a simple method can capture day-of-week seasonality, so improvements over that baseline can be measured.

choices.text: Score the advanced model by forecast error but compare the baseline only by processing speed.
choices.explanation: This does not compare the models on the same scale to determine whether the advanced model forecasts demand more accurately.

choices.text: Use the finalized sales for each test date as the baseline forecast.
choices.explanation: Those actuals are unavailable at forecast time, so using them as a comparison would overstate performance.

source.label: SageMaker Canvasの時系列予測

learning.reason: The value of a complex model can be judged only by comparing it with a seasonal baseline.
learning.concept: Model evaluation should include a simple method that is reasonable for the business as a comparison.

title: Limits of Recommendations for New Users
prompt: A video streaming service provides recommendations based on viewing history. It wants to show relevant suggestions to users who have not watched anything, starting with their first visit, but it cannot assume that a user has a viewing history. Which approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Copy an existing user's history unconditionally and treat it as the new user's own history.
choices.explanation: This attributes someone else's behavior to the user, so it cannot serve as evidence of that individual's preferences.

choices.text: Show no suggestions until the user has accumulated dozens of actual viewing events.
choices.explanation: This may preserve the accuracy of history-based recommendations, but it does not meet the requirement to show suggestions from the first visit.

choices.text: While no history is available, use popularity or selected genres; switch to history-based recommendations after the user's own behavior has accumulated.
choices.explanation: This makes recommendations possible from the first visit without relying on nonexistent history.

choices.text: Tune the hyperparameters of a history-based model and determine the user's preferences without providing any inputs other than history.
choices.explanation: Tuning parameters alone cannot fill the information gap when no history is available.

source.label: Amazon Personalizeの新規利用者と推薦

learning.reason: For a cold start with no history, use other available information or popular suggestions.
learning.concept: Recommendation quality depends on the availability of users, items, and interactions.

sourceLabel: New Users and Recommendations in Amazon Personalize

title: Effects of Extending the Forecast Horizon
prompt: A model that forecast only the next day's sales is being extended to produce daily forecasts up to 90 days ahead. The next day's price is known, but promotions two months from now have not been finalized. Which plan is appropriate for validating the results after this extension?

choices.text: If the next-day forecast performs well, apply that performance to forecasts 90 days ahead as well.
choices.explanation: Next-day accuracy does not show whether the model can handle day-to-day changes far into the future.

choices.text: For historical backtests, provide promotions that were known to be finalized but were still in the future at the time, and make good accuracy a pass condition.
choices.explanation: The evaluation would use information unavailable at forecast time and overstate operational accuracy.

choices.text: Aggregate all 90 days at once and evaluate only total sales, without checking daily forecast performance.
choices.explanation: Daily errors may be large even when the total is the same, making the results unsuitable for the decisions required.

choices.text: Run historical backtests at different forecast distances, matching what was knowable in advance about prices and promotions at each point.
choices.explanation: This measures uncertainty at longer horizons separately and avoids evaluating the model with future information that would not exist in production.

source.label: SageMaker Canvas 時系列予測

learning.reason: For longer forecast horizons, check both uncertainty and the availability of future information.
learning.concept: Time-series evaluation should reproduce the forecast horizon and information conditions that will be used in practice.

title: What to Do After a Monitoring Alert
prompt: After a data quality alert for inference, responders follow different investigation sequences, and action does not begin until the impact has spread. The cause of the anomaly is not known when the alert fires. What should be standardized?

choices.text: Document in a playbook the order for checking the input scope, impact, and recent changes, as well as who decides the next action.
choices.explanation: Even before the cause is known, responders can investigate the impact using the same criteria and choose a response.

choices.text: Automatically retrain the model whenever any alert occurs.
choices.explanation: If the anomaly is caused by something other than training, retraining is unnecessary and still will not identify the scope of the impact.

choices.text: Define only the model update procedure and exclude investigation of anomalies during operation.
choices.explanation: This can standardize known update work, but it does not improve the initial response when the cause is unknown.

choices.text: Send more alerts to the same responder, without defining how to begin the investigation or response.
choices.explanation: More notifications do not standardize the investigation sequence or identify who makes the decision.

source.label: AWS Well-Architectedの障害調査プレイブック

learning.reason: Connect alerts to an assigned responder, investigation, and recovery decision.
learning.concept: Monitoring should lead to operations guided by predefined response procedures, not stop at detection.

title: Carry a Reference Palette and Brushwork into a New Composition
prompt: A design team wants to create several concepts for a new venue. It wants to carry the palette and brushwork of an approved reference into the concepts, without carrying over the reference's subject or layout. Which method lets the team specify the new venue and composition in text?

choices.text: Use style transfer on the reference itself to preserve its composition, without adding a text prompt.
choices.explanation: This prioritizes preserving the input composition, so it does not meet the requirement to specify a new venue and layout.

choices.text: Extend the reference beyond its edges with outpainting, without changing the venue to be specified.
choices.explanation: Outpainting can add surrounding content, but it does not fulfill the requirement to create a new venue and composition.

choices.text: Provide the reference to Stable Image Style Guide and describe the new venue and composition in text.
choices.explanation: This uses the reference as a style guide while generating an image with different content specified in text.

choices.text: Use semantic search to find images with compositions similar to the reference, then use the closest existing image as is.
choices.explanation: Search returns existing images; it does not generate an image that combines the new venue with the reference's style.

source.label: Amazon BedrockのStability AI画像機能

learning.reason: Choose a method that preserves the reference style while generating new content.
learning.concept: The style reference and the content to create can be specified separately.

sourceLabel: Amazon Bedrock Stability AI Image Features

title: Why a brief signal may be missed
prompt: Nova 2 Lite is being used to summarize the broad progression of a long test video. You are now asked to always detect a test lamp that appears for much less than one second, including its timestamp. Which approach is appropriate with the current input and model?

choices.text: Re-encode the video at a higher frame rate so the model is guaranteed to read every saved frame.
choices.explanation: Increasing the input file's frame rate does not change how the model samples frames.

choices.text: Raise the output token limit so no input frames are missed.
choices.explanation: The length of the generated response does not guarantee how many frames are ingested.

choices.text: Pass the long video to the same model several times and conclude that all frames have been seen.
choices.explanation: Retrying with the same ingestion method is not evidence that every frame was evaluated.

choices.text: Treat this as a separate detection task, since the event may appear only in a frame the model did not select.
choices.explanation: Broad scene understanding and exhaustive detection of very brief events have different requirements.

source.label: Nova 2 Liteの動画フレームのサンプリング

learning.reason: A video-understanding model may not evaluate every frame individually, so it can miss brief events in the footage.
learning.concept: When every frame must be checked, analyze the pixels or logs in a separate process and use generative AI to explain the results if useful.

title: Attribute costs by application when using the same model
prompt: In the same AWS account, a sales-support application and an internal help application call the same Bedrock model with Converse. They want to keep the model unchanged and track usage costs by department on an ongoing basis. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Create an application inference profile for each application, enable cost allocation tags, and make calls through the profiles.
choices.explanation: This keeps the same model and allows tagged usage to be aggregated by application.

choices.text: Have both applications call the same model ID directly and include the department name in the prompt.
choices.explanation: Telling the model the department name does not add a tag to billing records.

choices.text: Lower the model's maximum output tokens and split the total cost evenly between the departments.
choices.explanation: This may reduce costs, but it does not represent each department's actual usage.

choices.text: Change a tag on a different model that neither application uses to separate the applications' charges.
choices.explanation: The tag is not associated with the resources actually called and cannot separate the applications' usage costs.

source.label: Bedrockのアプリケーション推論プロファイル

learning.reason: Use separate application profiles that reference the same model, then aggregate billing with cost allocation tags attached to the profiles.
learning.concept: Usage is included after cost allocation tags are activated; tags do not apply retroactively to past costs.

title: Handle regional peak load while keeping the same model
prompt: A conversational API has been validated for a specific foundation model, and it must handle peak load without changing models. Multiple AWS Regions are approved for processing, but inference must not be sent outside them. Which configuration should be considered for the supported model?

choices.text: Always switch to a global profile without checking the destinations it can use.
choices.explanation: Processing can be distributed, but this does not guarantee that inference stays within the approved scope.

choices.text: Use a cross-Region inference profile whose candidate destinations are confined to approved Regions.
choices.explanation: This can use the same supported model across multiple Regions while keeping the approved scope in view.

choices.text: Switch to a smaller, different model and process only in the same Region.
choices.explanation: This may meet the Region constraint, but it does not preserve the model that was evaluated.

choices.text: Keep the same model and lower the prompt temperature to increase the number of processing Regions.
choices.explanation: Sampling temperature does not control the destination Region.

source.label: Bedrockのクロスリージョン推論

learning.reason: A profile whose destinations have been confirmed to stay within the approved scope can use inference across Regions with the same model.
learning.concept: Do not rely only on a label indicating the same geographic scope; compare the Regions used by the profile with the organization's approved locations.

title: Determine whether input or output drove the cost increase
prompt: The number of inquiries and the model used have stayed nearly the same, but inference costs for document summarization have increased. The application has started handling longer documents, and responses may also have become longer. Select two metrics to use first to isolate the cost driver.

choices.text: The number of service errors from model invocations
choices.explanation: This can help investigate errors, but it does not show the input and output usage in this case.

choices.text: InputTokenCount for each time period
choices.explanation: This lets you compare the amount of input added to the model.

choices.text: Only the time until the first response is returned
choices.explanation: This shows response speed, but does not let you separately check input and output usage.

choices.text: The number of users registered in the application
choices.explanation: The number of people with access differs from the number of tokens actually consumed.

choices.text: OutputTokenCount for each time period
choices.explanation: This lets you compare whether the amount of generated output increased.

source.label: Bedrock推論のCloudWatchメトリクス

learning.reason: Comparing input and output token counts separately shows which side changed more.
learning.concept: Even when the number of calls is unchanged, token charges can change if the input or output size per call changes.

title: Combine separately directed scenes into one video
prompt: For a product video prototype, you want to show three scenes in sequence: a full view of the product, a close-up of it being operated, and an example of it in use. You need to specify the subject and camera movement separately for each scene, without joining generated clips in separate software. Which capability should you look for in a candidate video generation service?

choices.text: Enter a short prompt for only the first scene into the video generation model and omit details for the other two scenes.
choices.explanation: This produces one video, but does not specify the required sequence or individual camera movements.

choices.text: Generate three still images with an image generation model and record only their order in the filenames.
choices.explanation: This can indicate the order, but it does not generate video or camera movement.

choices.text: Run video generation three separate times and deliver the resulting clips as they are.
choices.explanation: You can specify each scene, but the result does not meet the requirement to produce one video.

choices.text: A storyboard that lets you specify the content and movement shot by shot within one video.
choices.explanation: You can specify the required details for each scene and build the structure of one video.

source.label: ショット別のストーリーボードの例（提供終了モデルの技術資料）

learning.reason: Video generation that accepts input for individual shots can produce one result while controlling the content of each scene.
learning.concept: You can design each shot separately, rather than creating a video from one prompt and one initial image.

sourceLabel: Example of a shot-by-shot storyboard (technical documentation for a discontinued model)

title: Investigate why a short answer uses up the token quota
prompt: In Bedrock text generation, responses are usually 300 tokens or fewer, but the maximum output is set to 8,000 every time. During periods when many short inputs arrive at once, the token quota is exhausted before the request-rate limit is reached. Without changing the model, which adjustment should you try first?

choices.text: Keep the maximum output at 8,000 even for short responses, and track only the number of requests.
choices.explanation: Counting calls alone does not address the effect of the token quota reserved when generation starts.

choices.text: Increase the input and send the same request using several different phrasings.
choices.explanation: This increases the input tokens for each call and can worsen the underlying cause of quota throttling.

choices.text: Check the generated lengths and lower the maximum output setting, leaving enough headroom to avoid truncating responses.
choices.explanation: This brings the reservation made at the start of each request closer to what is needed and can improve how many requests can start concurrently.

choices.text: Lower the output temperature without changing the maximum output setting.
choices.explanation: Changing sampling does not change the initial token reservation based on the specified maximum.

source.label: Bedrockのトークン割当計算

learning.reason: Because the specified maximum output is used in the allocation calculation when generation starts, revise it based on observed lengths while retaining sufficient headroom.
learning.concept: Distinguish the tokens actually generated and billed from the token quota held in advance to support concurrent requests.

title: Start reading before the response is complete
prompt: In an internal chat application that uses text generation, users cannot read anything until the entire response is complete. You want to keep the generation settings and model unchanged while displaying each generated part as it arrives. Which method should you choose for a supported model?

choices.text: Receive the response with ConverseStream and display text as each part arrives.
choices.explanation: Users can start reading the first content received without waiting for generation to finish.

choices.text: Use a batch inference job and retrieve the completed result from S3.
choices.explanation: This is suitable for large-scale background processing, but not for displaying generated content in the chat as it is produced.

choices.text: Keep using regular Converse, then display the text gradually after receiving the entire response.
choices.explanation: This changes how the response appears, but the first display still occurs only after the response is complete.

choices.text: Set a shorter maximum output and wait for the full response to complete.
choices.explanation: This may reduce the amount generated, but could truncate needed content and does not enable incremental display.

source.label: Bedrock ConverseとConverseStream

learning.reason: Streaming lets you receive portions of a generated response in sequence without waiting for completion.
learning.concept: Streaming can reduce time to first display, but it does not necessarily shorten the time required to generate the entire response.

title: Compare low-latency settings for the same model
prompt: You want to investigate slow chat responses without replacing a validated foundation model. Bedrock low-latency inference is available for the candidate model and Region, and your organization permits preview features in a test environment. What should you compare using the same evaluation inputs?

choices.text: Switch to a smaller model and measure response speed only.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the condition to keep the model unchanged, and it does not assess any quality differences caused by the change.

choices.text: Trim the same model's output downstream and treat the model call as having used low-latency mode.
choices.explanation: This is post-processing; it does not change the inference mode.

choices.text: Send only short evaluation texts to low-latency mode and long evaluation texts to standard mode.
choices.explanation: The inputs differ, so you cannot compare the effect of changing modes.

choices.text: Use standard and low-latency inference settings with the same model and evaluation inputs, then compare latency, quality, and cost.
choices.explanation: This evaluates the candidate modes without changing the model and checks whether they meet business requirements.

source.label: Bedrockの低遅延推論

learning.reason: Test standard and low-latency modes with the same model, then measure their actual latency, cost, and quality for the target application.
learning.concept: Availability is limited to supported models and Regions, so measure performance under the target workload instead of assuming low-latency mode is always faster.

title: Summarize an Existing Dashboard
prompt: The sales department uses a Quick Sight dashboard. Management wants an explanation of key trends and changes, but the team cannot build a separate data integration for generative AI or a custom web app. Which option uses the existing dashboard?

choices.text: Build a custom generative interface with Bedrock and load the dashboard’s underlying data separately.
choices.explanation: This can produce a summary, but it requires a separate data connection and application.

choices.text: Enable executive summaries in the Quick Sight dashboard.
choices.explanation: Users can review key points based on insights from the dashboard.

choices.text: Turn the dashboard screen into a static image and send only the image to the person in charge each day.
choices.explanation: This shares the display, but does not generate a summary of trends for management.

choices.text: Have users run ad hoc queries individually and output the values only in a table.
choices.explanation: This provides numbers, but does not meet the requirement to briefly explain key changes from the existing dashboard.

source.label: Quick Sightのエグゼクティブサマリー

learning.reason: A feature that summarizes insights from an existing dashboard avoids the need for a separate data pipeline.
learning.concept: Choose a feature that summarizes results from the BI system already in use, rather than generic question answering.

title: Provide a Detailed Diagram to a Model with Image Constraints
prompt: The answer must identify small equipment labels at multiple locations on a large factory floor plan. The image understanding model has a file-size limit, and simply shrinking the full image would make the text that needs to be identified illegible. Which processing method should be used?

choices.text: Substantially shrink the height and width of the full image and assume the small text will still be visible.
choices.explanation: The diagram can be sent all at once, but the resolution needed to read small equipment labels cannot be maintained.

choices.text: Crop only the center and have the model infer the equipment labels around the edges.
choices.explanation: The center can be examined in detail, but the input contains no evidence for the text around the edges.

choices.text: Split the image into sizes that preserve readable text and analyze the pieces, using region information to map each equipment label back to its original position.
choices.explanation: This keeps the input within the limit while allowing the necessary details and their locations to be evaluated.

choices.text: Send the entire image at its original size and shorten the generated text.
choices.explanation: Shortening the output does not resolve the input image constraint.

source.label: Amazon Novaの画像入力制約

learning.reason: Divide the image into tiles or other regions that fit the input constraint while preserving text size, then map the regions back to their original positions.
learning.concept: Simply making a single image smaller can remove details needed for inference.

title: Compare Documents and Questions Correctly with Cohere Embed
prompt: The same Cohere Embed v3 model is used for a search index and user questions. You discover that a classification input type was set for both documents and questions. When rebuilding the search setup, which combination is appropriate?

choices.text: Set classification for documents and clustering for questions.
choices.explanation: Neither setting is intended for search, and they do not match the roles of documents and questions.

choices.text: Set search_query for documents and search_document for questions.
choices.explanation: Even though these are search settings, the roles of indexed documents and search queries are reversed.

choices.text: Keep using the same classification input type for documents and questions, and only increase the number of search results.
choices.explanation: Increasing the number of retrieved results does not change vectors created with the wrong input type.

choices.text: Set search_document for indexed documents and search_query for user questions.
choices.explanation: This aligns both document ingestion and queries with the search roles expected by the model.

source.label: Cohere Embed v3の入力タイプ

learning.reason: For search, use the input type intended for each side: the indexed documents and the queries.
learning.concept: Even with the same embedding model, the intended input type differs for documents, queries, and classification.

title: Train a Model for a Task While Limiting GPU Budget
prompt: A team adapts the same large foundation model for each department using a small number of labeled examples. It is difficult to secure enough GPU memory to train all of the model’s parameters. Which method keeps the base weights shared and stores only the department-specific trained differences?

choices.text: Use LoRA to freeze the base weights and train low-rank adapters for each department.
choices.explanation: This limits the parameters being trained and stores each department’s differences separately from the base model.

choices.text: Fine-tune all parameters for each department and save the entire model.
choices.explanation: This can adapt the model for each department, but does not meet the training-memory and storage requirements.

choices.text: Further pretrain the same model separately for each department and combine the updated weights with the original weights.
choices.explanation: This updates many model weights, so it does not fit the requirement to keep only a small trained difference.

choices.text: Retrieve departmental examples at query time without training any weights or adapters.
choices.explanation: This can add information at inference time, but does not create department-specific trained differences.

source.label: SageMaker AIのLoRA

learning.reason: Keep the base model fixed and adjust only a small number of trainable parameters.
learning.concept: LoRA adapters are relatively small, but inference still requires a compatible base model.

title: Return an exact aggregate from table records
prompt: A business unit wants a query feature that returns “the number of returns by product category last month” across all orders in Redshift. It needs to aggregate every matching record, not estimate from sample or approximate values. Which design is most appropriate?

choices.text: Convert return records into short text chunks and estimate the total number of returns from the top 10 results by similarity score.
choices.explanation: This can find related examples, but it does not count every row.

choices.text: Use a knowledge base connected to structured data and aggregate in Redshift using the date range and category conditions.
choices.explanation: This selects matching data using structured conditions and calculates the count.

choices.text: Train a model on last month’s return report and do not load new monthly records.
choices.explanation: The model may learn patterns in previous data, but it cannot calculate the count for a new month.

choices.text: Return only the single order record with the highest score and treat its category as the result.
choices.explanation: A representative record can be shown, but it does not provide a category-level aggregate across the entire period.

source.label: Bedrock Knowledge Basesの構造化データ接続

learning.reason: Because the task is to count all records matching the conditions in the table, the calculation should be performed by a query in the structured data store.
learning.concept: An aggregate across all rows cannot be calculated from the contents of only the top documents retrieved by text search.

sourceLabel: Structured data connections for Bedrock Knowledge Bases

title: Shorten a prompt while preserving its decisions
prompt: An existing prompt for classifying return inquiries meets quality requirements, but it uses many input tokens each time. You want to reduce only the input tokens while preserving the policy’s applicability conditions and the response format. What should you do?

choices.text: Lower the maximum number of tokens in the generated response and leave the input prompt unchanged.
choices.explanation: This changes the output limit, but the input sent each time remains the same.

choices.text: Delete every sentence containing applicability conditions and publish as soon as the prompt is shorter.
choices.explanation: This reduces input, but omits mandatory business conditions and quality checks.

choices.text: Condense redundant wording, keep the applicability conditions explicit, and compare the shortened and original versions using the same representative cases.
choices.explanation: This reduces input while verifying that the required conditions and format have not regressed.

choices.text: Send the same prompt and remove only unnecessary sentences from the full response after generation.
choices.explanation: This can tidy the generated content, but does not reduce the input tokens sent to the model.

source.label: Bedrockのプロンプト短縮

learning.reason: Remove redundancy while preserving the meaning, then compare output quality before and after shortening.
learning.concept: Reducing the input budget and reducing the number of output characters are controlled by different settings.

title: Find rare failures with the same input
prompt: When each inquiry is tested once under the same conditions, the candidate models have nearly identical quality. The business uses nondeterministic sampling, so you also want the release decision to account for how often the same input rarely produces a failure. What should you plan?

choices.text: Reduce the representative inputs used for evaluation and evaluate each candidate once.
choices.explanation: This uses fewer inputs than the current plan and cannot measure variation for the same input.

choices.text: Generate multiple outputs for each input, but evaluate only the single highest-quality output.
choices.explanation: This measures whether a good output can be produced, but does not reveal how often a failure occurs in a single current use.
