choices.text: Use different temperatures and pass criteria for each candidate, then compare the highest average scores.
choices.explanation: The conditions are not aligned across models, making it difficult to tell whether differences in failure frequency come from configuration or model behavior.

choices.text: Run the same representative cases for each candidate under the same conditions and the same number of times, then compare the proportion that misses a required condition.
choices.explanation: This provides samples for comparing rare failure frequency even when model outputs vary.

source.label: AWSの生成出力の品質と信頼性の評価

learning.reason: A single response cannot capture variation, so evaluate representative inputs multiple times using the same settings.
learning.concept: To compare failure frequency, align the evaluation population and repetition count, as well as average quality.

sourceLabel: Evaluating the quality and reliability of generative output with AWS

title: Adjust retrieval count and generation limit independently
prompt: In policy search, retrieving more items makes it easier to find exception clauses. However, you want to keep answers within a fixed length that fits on screen. Select two ways to adjust the number of retrieved items and the generation length limit so changing one does not change the other.

choices.text: Adjust the number of results retrieved in the vector search settings.
choices.explanation: This setting changes the number of search candidates that may be passed to the model.

choices.text: Increase only the character limit for the query to return more search results.
choices.explanation: This allows a longer query, but does not change the maximum number of results returned.

choices.text: Lower the temperature at generation time and treat it as changing the maximum response length.
choices.explanation: Temperature controls sampling; it is not an output limit.

choices.text: Adjust the maximum number of output tokens in the generation settings.
choices.explanation: This sets the output limit and is separate from the number of retrieved items.

choices.text: Ingest only short documents and treat the response length as fixed as well.
choices.explanation: Shortening documents does not fix the generated output length.

source.label: Knowledge Basesの検索・生成設定

learning.reason: Handle retrieval through search settings and response length through generation settings so each can be evaluated independently.
learning.concept: The number of supporting items retrieved and the length of text generated by the model are adjusted separately.

sourceLabel: Retrieval and generation settings for Knowledge Bases

title: Scoring only facts the model knows
prompt: As a feature of a news-classification system, you want to check how well a foundation model can answer general geography questions. For this evaluation, do not connect a search service, and assess whether the model gives the expected facts rather than whether it stays faithful to reference material. Which plan is appropriate?

choices.text: Connect a search service and count only answers with citations as knowledge scores.
choices.explanation: This introduces the effect of evidence retrieved externally, so it does not measure the model’s own knowledge.

choices.text: Without connecting search, run a Factual Knowledge evaluation with a set of questions that have expected answers.
choices.explanation: This lets you compare under the same conditions whether the model includes the expected facts in its answers.

choices.text: Determine correctness by counting the words shared by the model’s response and the question.
choices.explanation: Even a response that merely repeats the question may share words without stating the correct facts.

choices.text: Look for information in the model’s response that is absent from a source passage and count it toward the knowledge score.
choices.explanation: This can evaluate whether a response stays within supplied material, but no material is provided here.

source.label: SageMakerのFactual Knowledge評価

learning.reason: Evaluate the model’s answers to factual questions with known answers, without using external search.
learning.concept: A high score on general factual knowledge does not guarantee correct answers about change history or private materials.

title: Matching Evaluation Inputs and Outputs to Tasks
prompt: Evaluate separately whether a shared foundation model is suitable for three use cases. Match each evaluation dataset to a Bedrock model evaluation task type.

choices.text: Question and answer
choices.explanation: Compares the quality of answers to specific questions.

choices.text: Classification
choices.explanation: Compares the model’s ability to return a prescribed category for each input.

choices.text: Text summarization
choices.explanation: Compares whether the model can read a source text and produce a shorter text that preserves its key points.

source.label: Amazon Bedrockのモデル評価タスク

learning.reason: Evaluation data should make it possible to compare the model’s outputs against what the task requires.
learning.concept: Even with the same source document, the evaluation method differs depending on whether the model should generate a shorter version, answer a question, or return a label.

prompts.text: A long incident report and a short reference summary of its key points.
A question to answer by reading a document and the expected answer.
The text of an inquiry and a predefined assignment category.

title: Order the steps for adding department-specific response classification
prompt: An organization’s classification accuracy is inadequate with prompts alone, so it will supervised-tune an approved, compatible foundation model. Company policy requires reviewing the training data before tuning, then comparing the tuned model with the original using evaluation examples not used for training before release. Put the steps in order.

choices.text: Run a supervised-tuning job on the approved base model using labeled training data.
choices.explanation: Use reviewed inputs and expected outputs to adapt the model to the task.

choices.text: Approve the tuned model that meets the comparison criteria as the model to use in the business application.
choices.explanation: The tuned model becomes an approved option only after its quality has been confirmed through an independent evaluation.

choices.text: Prepare classification inputs and expected labels, review the data, and split it into training data and a separate evaluation set.
choices.explanation: Before training begins, decide which examples to use for training and which to hold out for evaluation before release.

choices.text: Compare the tuned model with the original under the same criteria using unused evaluation examples.
choices.explanation: After tuning is complete, measure actual improvement on examples the models have not seen.

source.label: Bedrockのモデルカスタマイズジョブ

learning.reason: Prepare the input-to-expected-output pairs, tune the model, and evaluate the tuned model on independent examples before switching to it.
learning.concept: Agreement on training data alone is not evidence of business quality at release.

title: Stop subsequent text at a delimiter
prompt: You receive a summary whose length varies with the number of items from a compatible foundation model. When the required summary is complete, the model generates an agreed-upon, dedicated delimiter string and then starts adding extra explanation. Which setting lets your application receive the entire summary while stopping generation at the delimiter?

choices.text: Set the dedicated delimiter string as a stop sequence.
choices.explanation: The response can be configured to end when that string appears.

choices.text: Set the output-token limit to the length of the shortest summary.
choices.explanation: Longer summaries will be cut off, dropping required content before the delimiter is reached.

choices.text: Set a low temperature and assume that nothing will be generated after the delimiter.
choices.explanation: Temperature changes selection probabilities; it does not set a termination condition for a particular string.

choices.text: Reduce the number of candidate tokens during generation and automatically discard output after the delimiter.
choices.explanation: Even if the application hides unwanted text, generation continues.

source.label: Bedrockの推論時パラメーター

learning.reason: Setting the end marker as a stop sequence avoids truncating variable-length summaries based only on their length.
learning.concept: Use a unique delimiter so that an ordinary string produced by the task is not accidentally treated as a stop condition.

title: Preventing the same term from producing different aggregations
prompt: When asked about “shipped” in a structured knowledge base, the model sometimes filters by the delivery start date and sometimes by the shipment-completed status. The organization has defined the latter as the intended meaning, and the existing tables cannot be changed. Which setting would improve query generation quality?

choices.text: Explain the meaning of the status in the settings and provide representative questions with SQL examples that use the correct WHERE condition.
choices.explanation: This clarifies the aggregation condition associated with the term and teaches the mapping between intent and query.

choices.text: Only lower the output temperature, without providing the relationship between business terminology and status.
choices.explanation: This may reduce output variation, but it does not specify the meaning of the correct column and condition.

choices.text: Shorten and format the aggregated result in post-processing without changing how the generated SQL is determined.
choices.explanation: The display may look cleaner, but the values aggregated with the wrong condition will not be corrected.

choices.text: Leave the columns used by the current SQL undecided and use only a natural-language explanation as the output.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to aggregate actual data according to the organization’s definition.

source.label: 構造化ナレッジベースのクエリ生成設定

learning.reason: Explain which columns and conditions correspond to the business term, and provide the knowledge base’s query generation with examples that map known questions to correct SQL.
learning.concept: Business meanings that cannot be inferred from table names alone can be supplied through descriptions and known query examples.

sourceLabel: Structured knowledge base query generation settings

title: Keep an adapter aligned with the base version it was built for
prompt: A LoRA adapter was created for a specific version of a foundation model. When updating the inference platform, someone proposes attaching the adapter to a different base version with the same name. What should you verify to preserve the learned behavior?

choices.text: Assume the behavior will be preserved on any base as long as the file extension is the same.
choices.explanation: The file format alone does not establish compatibility with the parameter shapes or the base used during training.

choices.text: Check only that the preprocessing settings are the same, without checking differences in the base version or architecture.
choices.explanation: Matching preprocessing does not guarantee the parameter alignment on which the adapter operates.

choices.text: Verify compatibility with the version of the base model used during training, then rerun the business evaluation with that combination.
choices.explanation: This checks the alignment between the base and the adapter and verifies whether behavior and quality are actually preserved.

choices.text: Deploy the adapter alone as an independent foundation model so that choosing a base is unnecessary.
choices.explanation: The adapter contains only a set of differences; it does not replace all the parameters of the original model.

source.label: SageMaker AIのLoRA

learning.reason: An adapter contains parameter differences relative to its base, so it should be paired with a compatible base and validated.
learning.concept: Storing the files separately does not mean the same adapter can be used with any base.

title: Find cases where similar conditions produce different outcomes
prompt: An organization already using SageMaker Clarify is evaluating a training recommendation model. It wants to examine whether users in different groups who have similar relevant characteristics tend to receive different predictions, rather than looking only at the overall positive prediction rate for each group. Which metric fits this purpose?

choices.text: Counterfactual Fliptest
choices.explanation: It evaluates differences in predictions by comparing neighborhoods of similar observations across different groups.

choices.text: Difference in Positive Proportions in Predicted Labels
choices.explanation: It compares the overall proportion of positive predictions across groups and does not match individuals with similar characteristics.

choices.text: Class Imbalance
choices.explanation: It compares the number of observations for each group in the data and does not address differences in predictions.

choices.text: Recall Difference
choices.explanation: It compares, by group, the proportion of actually positive cases that were also predicted positive. This differs from measuring differences between neighborhoods.

source.label: ClarifyのCounterfactual Fliptest

learning.reason: Comparing nearby observations across groups examines differences in predictions from a perspective distinct from overall group proportions.
learning.concept: Differences between neighborhoods can prompt further investigation, but do not by themselves establish a causal relationship between group membership and outcomes.

title: When development and independent evaluation results disagree
prompt: The release criteria for an assistant model require it to respond correctly to harmless questions across multiple use cases. The development team’s tests pass, but examples created by an independent evaluation team fall below the criteria in a particular use case. How should this affect the release decision?

choices.text: Average the overall scores from the development and independent teams, and ignore the failure in the affected use case if the average passes.
choices.explanation: Information that the model falls below the criteria under a specific condition could be obscured by aggregation.

choices.text: Reproduce the failing examples using the same pass/fail criteria and investigate before release which use cases were inadequately covered by the internal evaluation.
choices.explanation: This helps determine whether the issue found in the independent evaluation occurs in the intended use case.

choices.text: Have the independent team use only the test data selected by the development team, then release if the results match.
choices.explanation: This can confirm reproducibility on the same data, but does not address the difference in use cases found by the independent team.

choices.text: Lower the criteria for the failing use case and release the model unchanged.
choices.explanation: This does not resolve why the evaluations disagree or what impact the issue may have on users.

source.label: 責任あるAIの独立した評価

learning.reason: Do not hide a disagreement by averaging scores. First investigate whether examples from both evaluations represent the intended use cases appropriately.
learning.concept: Evaluating important release criteria from another perspective can reveal gaps in the development team’s assumptions.

title: Removing an attribute does not prove that bias is gone
prompt: A model predicts priority for training invitations. The model’s input no longer includes users’ ages, but some features, including years since enrollment and parts of their usage history, are strongly correlated with age. What should be done before deployment?

choices.text: End the bias review as soon as age is removed from the model inputs.
choices.explanation: Patterns related to age may remain in strongly correlated features.

choices.text: Conclude that each group is affected the same way if the overall accuracy is unchanged from the previous version.
choices.explanation: The same overall accuracy can conceal changes for specific groups.

choices.text: Investigate how related features affect the model, evaluate results by group and business quality, and consider mitigation measures.
choices.explanation: This makes it possible to assess the effects of measures on both bias and predictive information.

choices.text: Remove every column correlated with age and deploy without changing data collection or evaluation.
choices.explanation: This could discard information needed for prediction and does not verify that bias has been eliminated.

source.label: 責任あるAIの意図しない偏りの緩和

learning.reason: Even when a direct attribute is removed, bias can remain in predictions through related features.
learning.concept: Where validation attributes are available, examine related features and group-level evaluations, and compare the effects on information needed by the business.

sourceLabel: Mitigating unintended bias in responsible AI

title: Evaluate both safe abstention and usefulness
prompt: A feature that drafts answers about policies must answer questions when the source material contains the information and abstain when it does not. Comparing candidates only by refusal rate does not show whether a high rate reflects safety or excessive refusals. Which evaluation is appropriate?

choices.text: Choose the candidate with the highest share of refusals across all inputs.
choices.explanation: This does not distinguish a candidate that also refuses answerable questions.

choices.text: Prepare only questions answered by the source material and compare the length of each candidate’s responses.
choices.explanation: This does not evaluate safe responses when information is absent, and response length does not guarantee that an answer is valid.

choices.text: Count only the number of search results and do not check whether the model actually abstained.
choices.explanation: This reveals how search behaves but does not evaluate the model’s response policy.

choices.text: Count inappropriate refusals on questions answered by the source material separately from unsupported answers on questions it does not answer.
choices.explanation: This evaluates both safe abstention and answering when useful.

source.label: Bedrockのモデル評価指標

learning.reason: Separate cases where the source material can answer a question from those where it cannot, then check whether abstaining is appropriate in each case.
learning.concept: Increasing the refusal rate alone can cause the model to stop answering questions it should answer.

title: Find out how often people follow AI recommendations
prompt: In an application system with human review, reviewers’ decisions almost always match the AI’s. To improve the system, you want to determine whether reviewers would reach the same conclusions independently from the source material or whether the AI display influences their decisions. Which evaluation method is most appropriate?

choices.text: In some evaluations, hide the AI recommendation, have the reviewer record an initial decision based only on the source material, and then compare it with the condition in which the recommendation is visible.
choices.explanation: The decision made without the recommendation provides a baseline for comparing the effect of displaying it.

choices.text: Show the recommendation to every reviewer first and compare the approval-button click rates.
choices.explanation: This measures agreement under the existing conditions but cannot isolate the effect of displaying the recommendation.

choices.text: Show the same recommendation to two reviewers first, and treat their conclusion as independent if both approve it.
choices.explanation: Both reviewers may be influenced by the recommendation.

choices.text: Compare the AI’s conclusions with those of a separate model, without collecting independent human decisions.
choices.explanation: This measures differences between AI systems but cannot show whether reviewers were influenced by the recommendation.

source.label: 責任あるAIの独立した評価

learning.reason: Record a reviewer’s initial decision when they have not seen the AI recommendation to isolate the effect of presenting it.
learning.concept: The share of cases in which a person approves on screen alone does not show whether they made an independent judgment.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Link data access requests to owner approval
prompt: An AI team wants to use another department’s data that it found in a catalog. The data owner must see the intended purpose and the reason for the request, and the data must be shared only with an approved project. When using Amazon DataZone, which procedure is appropriate? DataZone

choices.text: Grant read permissions to all projects as soon as the data is published in the catalog.
choices.explanation: This makes the data discoverable but does not require individual approval of its intended use.

choices.text: Submit a subscription request for the data, obtain the owner’s approval, and share it with the approved project.
choices.explanation: This separates data discovery from access and lets the owner manage access after reviewing the purpose.

choices.text: Grant the planned project access first and have the owner review the request reason monthly.
choices.explanation: This is a review after the fact, so it does not meet the requirement to share data after approval.

choices.text: Give the AI team catalog administration permissions so it can approve its own request.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to govern use through data-owner approval.

source.label: Amazon DataZoneのサブスクリプション申請の承認

learning.reason: Design data sharing to separate discoverability from owner approval based on the intended use.
learning.concept: Governance of data-use requests.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Restricting the output of a collaborative analysis
prompt: Two companies are conducting a collaborative analysis in AWS Clean Rooms. They want to receive aggregated values by category only when each category contains at least a specified number of unique customers. Which setting returns permitted aggregates without returning rows based on too few people?

choices.text: Encrypt the aggregated results, then return rows based on too few people to the permitted recipient.
choices.explanation: Encryption can protect data in transit and at rest, but it does not prevent the recipient from learning about a small-group aggregate.

choices.text: Restrict the columns used for aggregation, but set no output condition on the customer count in each category.
choices.explanation: Column restrictions alone may still allow results that do not meet a minimum group size.

choices.text: Set the minimum number of distinct values in the customer identifier column as an output constraint in the aggregation analysis rule.
choices.explanation: This can prevent results from being returned when the unique customer count represented by an aggregate row is below the threshold.

choices.text: Check only the total number of customers in the input data and impose no constraints on individual categories in the results.
choices.explanation: Even when the overall dataset is large, a single category may represent only a very small number of people.

source.label: AWS Clean Roomsの集計分析ルール

learning.reason: Controls should define the boundaries of permitted collaborative-analysis outputs as well as the data being shared.
learning.concept: Output controls for collaborative analysis.

sourceLabel: AWS Clean Rooms aggregation analysis rules

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Allowing selection only of approved software
prompt: You are procuring a learning-assistance tool from AWS Marketplace. Developers in the organization should be able to subscribe only to preapproved products, and new products should require an approval request to the procurement team. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Configure AWS Budgets to notify you of high usage charges after a product has been subscribed to.
choices.explanation: This can monitor costs, but it does not control subscriptions based on prior approval.

choices.text: Remove developers' permission to subscribe to all products, and have the procurement team subscribe to every product, including approved ones.
choices.explanation: This prevents unapproved subscriptions, but does not let developers start using approved products themselves.

choices.text: Ask to add an “Approved” billing tag and let developers choose products themselves.
choices.explanation: A tag can classify a product, but it cannot prevent a subscription to an unapproved product in advance.

choices.text: Use Private Marketplace to allow approved products and have the procurement team process additional requests.
choices.explanation: This lets the organization manage a product list that meets its requirements and prevent users from starting to use unapproved products.

source.label: AWS MarketplaceのPrivate Marketplace

learning.reason: External product procurement should be controlled with an allowlist, rather than relying on reminders to buyers.
learning.concept: Controlling the use of approved software.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Preventing changes to a containerized inference environment
prompt: In Amazon ECR, an inference pipeline references an approved release tag. If the tag already exists, a subsequent standard push must not be able to overwrite it with a different image. Which setting is appropriate?

choices.text: Enable tag immutability for the release tag.
choices.explanation: This can reject a standard push that assigns a different image to an existing tag.

choices.text: Enable enhanced image scanning and allow tag overwrites.
choices.explanation: This provides image findings, but does not prevent overwriting the same tag.

choices.text: Add an approved identifier as a tag to the image, but do not use immutability.
choices.explanation: This identifies the approved target, but the tag could later refer to a different image.

choices.text: Keep using the same tag and make the image size at approval time the only release condition.
choices.explanation: A different image could have the same size, and this setting would not reject an overwrite.

source.label: Amazon ECR image tag mutability

learning.reason: Keeping inference dependencies immutable preserves the correspondence between the approved image and the image that runs.
learning.concept: Supply chain integrity for AI containers.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Requiring two people to control key deletion
prompt: A KMS key for training data now requires an independent two-person process to reduce accidental deletion during the retention period. The person responsible must not be able to schedule deletion directly. Which design enforces approval?

choices.text: Give all key administrators permission to delete keys, then use CloudTrail notifications to inform approvers when an action occurs.
choices.explanation: This notifies approvers after a deletion action; it does not prevent the action before approval.

choices.text: Grant permission to schedule deletion only to a workflow that has passed independent approval, and remove direct deletion permission from the responsible person's role.
choices.explanation: This removes the path for the responsible person to bypass approval and perform the operation directly.

choices.text: Extend the deletion waiting period while still allowing the responsible person to act alone.
choices.explanation: This provides more time to cancel deletion, but does not require prior approval from another person.

choices.text: Duplicate the stored data and keep all current deletion permissions in place.
choices.explanation: The deletion process for an individual key remains unchanged, so this does not ensure a two-person review.

source.label: AWS KMSの削除権限の制御

learning.reason: The strength of an encryption boundary depends not only on encryption, but also on separation of duties in key management.
learning.concept: Least privilege and separation of duties in key management.

sourceLabel: Controlling AWS KMS key deletion permissions

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Managing the Expiration of Shared Data Access
prompt: Revoke a time-limited Amazon DataZone access approval when a collaborative project ends. During the approved period, the project copied files to an authorized working area. Which approach prevents the data from being used in the next project?

choices.text: Change the catalog display name and treat access and working copies as expired.
choices.explanation: Changing the display name does not revoke granted access rights or existing copies.

choices.text: Keep access to the source data and the working copies, and reject only new requests.
choices.explanation: Controlling future requests does not end use by the completed project.

choices.text: Revoke the subscription to the source data and handle copies already created in the working area according to the retention policy.
choices.explanation: Revocation stops future access to the source data, while copies in other storage locations can also be handled.

choices.text: Handle only the working-area copies and leave the subscription to the source data in place.
choices.explanation: The source-data authorization remains, so the data can be retrieved again.

source.label: Amazon DataZoneのサブスクリプション取消し

learning.reason: Data sharing governance includes managing the usage period and removing access after it expires, not just granting access.
learning.concept: Reviewing temporary data-use rights.

title: Training Data for Rare Failures
prompt: Operational records contain a large volume of normal-operation logs, but only a few examples of each known failure type to be classified. People can review the labels. To independently assess how well each failure type is identified in a future evaluation, which data-preparation step should be improved first?

choices.text: Duplicate the few existing examples and split the same records between training and evaluation.
choices.explanation: This increases the count, but evaluation records are the same as training examples, so performance on unseen data remains unknown.

choices.text: Collect additional examples of known failures, verify their labels, and secure independent examples for training and evaluation.
choices.explanation: This provides examples from which to learn the features of each class of interest and separate examples for independent assessment.

choices.text: Run anomaly detection using only normal-operation data and treat it as having directly learned every failure type.
choices.explanation: This may find signs that differ from normal operation, but it does not assess identification performance for each known failure label.

choices.text: Compare only overall accuracy across all records while keeping the number of known failure examples low.
choices.explanation: Performance on the much larger normal class can mask whether rare failures can be distinguished.

source.label: AIF-C01 Domain 1 試験ガイド

learning.reason: Increase labeled data for rare classes to improve the ability to train and evaluate the model.
learning.concept: The amount and quality of data for each class constrain what a classifier can learn.

title: Poor Performance During Training
prompt: A candidate model has high error on both the training and validation sets. No data errors have been found, and even after sufficient training, the model barely captures a nonlinear relationship between inputs and outputs. Which issue should be suspected first based on the evaluation?

choices.text: It is overfitting by memorizing the training examples.
choices.explanation: This is a possibility when training performance is good but performance on unseen data is poor; here, training performance is also poor.

choices.text: Data leakage is occurring because validation data is mixed into the training data.
choices.explanation: Duplication or leakage often makes evaluation performance look better, and does not directly explain why the model fails to capture the relationship even on training data.

choices.text: The model is underfitting because it cannot represent the relationships in the data.
choices.explanation: This matches a situation in which the model cannot capture complex patterns and error remains high on both training and validation data.

choices.text: The distribution of production inputs is changing over time.
choices.explanation: That could explain a difference during operation, but the model already fails to capture the relationship in the training data.

source.label: AIF-C01 Domain 1 試験ガイド

learning.reason: Poor performance even during training is a sign of underfitting.
learning.concept: Comparing training and validation performance patterns helps distinguish insufficient model capacity from overfitting.

title: Ordering When a Point Forecast Is Not Enough
prompt: The central forecast for next month's demand was 100 units. Because the cost of a stockout is high for this product, the order should also account for the upper end of expected demand. Which additional forecast value should be reviewed?

choices.text: Only a lower quantile.
choices.explanation: This can inform a downside scenario, but it does not help assess an upside in demand that could lead to a stockout.

choices.text: Only a simple average of the central forecasts for all stores.
choices.explanation: This may help compare overall levels, but it does not represent the upper-side uncertainty for this product.

choices.text: The number of features used by the model during training.
choices.explanation: This may indicate model size, but it does not represent how much demand could increase next month.

choices.text: An uncertainty-related forecast output, such as an upper demand quantile.
choices.explanation: This accounts for the possibility of higher demand in addition to the central value.

source.label: SageMaker Canvasの分位点予測

learning.reason: When stockout costs are high, account for the forecast range.
learning.concept: Distinguish the forecast value from uncertainty and connect it to the business's risk tolerance.

title: A New Category Appears Only in Production
prompt: A classifier trained on categorically encoded inputs receives a product category for the first time that was not present during training. You cannot assume the new category is equivalent to an existing one, and the meaning of the current input columns must not change. Which operational approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Keep the existing encoding rules and handle the unknown category as an explicitly defined unknown value or route it for review.
choices.explanation: This preserves the mapping between the current columns and the model and avoids passing an incorrect value for a new category.

choices.text: Rebuild the column assignments from the categories in each request without updating the model.
choices.explanation: The column order or meaning could change, causing the same number to represent a different category.

choices.text: Always replace the category with the existing category whose spelling is closest.
choices.explanation: String similarity does not guarantee classification meaning, and the business context does not allow assuming they are equivalent.

choices.text: Whenever a new category arrives, remove an existing feature column and run the current model with the remaining columns.
choices.explanation: This changes the feature structure and cannot preserve the same input meaning used during training.

source.label: SageMaker Data Wranglerのカテゴリ値の変換

learning.reason: Define explicit handling for unknown categories and route them for review when needed.
learning.concept: Production inputs can contain values absent from training, so the input contract needs exception handling.

sourceLabel: SageMaker Data Wrangler categorical value transformations

title: Reuse the Original Subject with a New Design Overlay
prompt: You want to place the subject of an already approved product photo into different promotional designs for each season. The product itself must not be redrawn, and you need to give the editor an image with a transparent background. Which image-processing operation is appropriate?

choices.text: Generate the product and a new background together from a reference photo.
choices.explanation: Because this recreates the whole image, it may not meet the requirement to use the approved subject as is.

choices.text: Mask the background, use inpainting to generate the promotional design, and create a single flattened image.
choices.explanation: This can generate a specific background, but the result will not have a transparent background that can be reused with other designs.

choices.text: Use Stable Image Remove Background to keep the subject and make the background transparent.
choices.explanation: This cuts out the existing subject so the editor can combine it with a different background.

choices.text: Outpaint beyond the original image and keep the subject centered.
choices.explanation: This can expand the frame, but it does not make the background transparent.

source.label: Amazon BedrockのStability AI画像機能

learning.reason: To reuse the original subject, remove the background while preserving transparency.
learning.concept: Creating an image with a transparent background is different from generating artwork to replace the background.

sourceLabel: Amazon Bedrock Stability AI image capabilities

title: Check the Input Budget for the Selected Model Before Sending
prompt: A service sends the same long inquiry to one of two selected foundation models. If the input exceeds the limit, users must be notified before generation is invoked. Even when the character count is the same, the models may process different numbers of tokens. Which design is appropriate?

choices.text: Assume that Japanese always has the same character-to-token ratio and apply one character limit to both models.
choices.explanation: Tokenization can vary across models and character types.

choices.text: Start generation first and notify users of an overage based on the returned usage.
choices.explanation: This reveals actual usage but does not meet the requirement to notify users before generation starts.

choices.text: Set only the output token limit and do not check the number of input tokens.
choices.explanation: An output limit does not establish whether the input fits within the allowed range.

choices.text: Pass the selected model and actual input to CountTokens, then compare the result with the model limit while allowing enough room for the input and response.
choices.explanation: This enables a decision before invoking generation based on the measurement for the selected model.

source.label: Bedrock CountTokensのモデル別計測

learning.reason: Estimate token usage before generation by specifying the actual model and input.
learning.concept: A shared character limit cannot account for differences in model tokenizers.

title: Launch an Internal Business App with Generative AI
prompt: The administration team wants an internal form where employees can submit requests, compare them with existing data, and update approval status. The environment can connect to existing data sources, and the team wants to avoid a dedicated web server or building the interface from scratch. Chat responses to users alone are not sufficient. What is appropriate?

choices.text: Use AWS App Studio to generate an application foundation, then configure the approval screens and connection to existing data.
choices.explanation: It can be used to build an application with business screens and persistent data without creating a separate web platform.

choices.text: Enter the request fields in a foundation model's test chat and do not save confirmed status.
choices.explanation: This lets users try prompts but does not provide a request form or update approval status.

choices.text: Create only a no-code public prototype and leave the approval status as a dummy value.
choices.explanation: A prototype is possible, but it cannot connect to existing internal data and update records.

choices.text: Deploy a document-search assistant and write every approval-status change into the documents used for search.
choices.explanation: It can answer questions from documents, but it is not a form with a procedure for updating status.

source.label: AWS App Studioの生成AIで業務アプリを作る機能

learning.reason: When an internal business app needs forms and data, choose a service that supports application configuration and data connections.
learning.concept: Generative AI chat responses and business screens that create or update records have different requirements.

sourceLabel: AWS App Studio capability for building business apps with generative AI

title: Share a recurring information workflow
prompt: Each week, a team member enters a product name and time period. In an environment where external connections are allowed, they want to run information gathering, issue organization, and report drafting in the same order. Which approach lets other team members reuse the process in an existing AWS Quick environment without developing a separate application?

choices.text: Open a different chat each week and have the team member enter every step manually.
choices.explanation: The work can still get done, but the process cannot be run consistently as a shared workflow.

choices.text: Define the inputs and each step in AWS Quick Flows, publish the flow to the team, and have users provide the values.
choices.explanation: The same multi-step process can be reused even when the product or time period changes.

choices.text: Generate only a KPI summary from an existing dashboard, and have the team member gather information and organize issues manually.
choices.explanation: A dashboard can be described, but the multi-step process cannot be standardized.

choices.text: Build a separate web application and reconnect all the steps in its backend.
choices.explanation: This allows flexible use of external services, but it does not meet the requirement to reuse the existing environment and avoid application development.

source.label: AWS Quick Flowsの作成

learning.reason: Use a reusable flow that accepts changing values as inputs and combines the standard steps.
learning.concept: Define a process that the whole team can review instead of relying on a one-off free-form chat.

title: Identify a configuration with costly rework despite the same rate
prompt: Compare two generative AI configurations that use the same model. Configuration A has a short output per run but often has to be regenerated because it fails the usage requirements. Configuration B costs more per run but is more likely to pass validation on the first try. Which metric compares the cost of obtaining an answer that can be used?

choices.text: Compare only the output token count of the first request.
choices.explanation: This does not capture the cost of repeated regeneration when outputs are short.

choices.text: Because both configurations use the same model, compare only the rate and treat their costs as equal.
choices.explanation: Even at the same rate, token consumption and the number of retries can differ.

choices.text: Sum the costs of all attempts and divide by the number of answers that meet the acceptance criteria.
choices.explanation: This compares the cost per usable answer, including regeneration.

choices.text: Compare only the cost of the first response that did not violate the constraints.
choices.explanation: Selecting only calls that meet quality requirements excludes the cost of failed calls.

source.label: AWSの完了タスク単位の生成AI費用評価

learning.reason: Divide total cost, including retries, by the number of results that were actually usable, rather than looking only at the price of individual calls.
learning.concept: A completion-based metric also captures the cost of increased rework.

sourceLabel: AWS generative AI cost evaluation per completed task

title: Compare the effects of image style instructions
prompt: You want to compare photorealistic and line-art prompts using the same image generation model. Because generated results vary, you first want to reduce variation due to randomness and compare results that differ only in the style description. Which comparison is appropriate for a supported model?

choices.text: Use the best result from all different seeds for the photorealistic style, but only one run for the line-art style.
choices.explanation: The examples are selected differently, so the effect of the style instruction cannot be compared.

choices.text: Change the style and resolution at the same time and determine which one changed the result.
choices.explanation: Multiple factors change, making it difficult to isolate the effect of one.

choices.text: Change both the style and generation seed, and attribute any difference to the style.
choices.explanation: Changing the initial sampling conditions can also affect the generated result.

choices.text: Use the same seed, resolution, number of generated images, and other settings, and change only the style description.
choices.explanation: This controls for differences in randomness and settings, making the effect of the style instruction easier to see.

source.label: Amazon BedrockのStability AI画像機能

learning.reason: Keep the seed and other parameters the same so that only the style instruction being compared changes.
learning.concept: Using the same seed controls a comparison condition; it does not mean that changing the prompt will produce the same image.

sourceLabel: Stability AI image capabilities in Amazon Bedrock

title: Trace dependencies spread across multiple documents
prompt: Product architecture diagrams, bills of materials, and supplier documents are stored separately. Users often ask questions such as, “Which products are affected by a change at supplier X?” and need to follow relationships from a supplier through a component to a product. Which candidate can help avoid limiting context to a single retrieved document?

choices.text: Convert each document into longer chunks and retrieve only the most similar document.
choices.explanation: This adds context within one document, but does not retrieve the links between suppliers, components, and products in separate documents.

choices.text: Register product names as stop sequences during generation.
choices.explanation: This controls the strings that end generation; it does not provide a way to follow relationships during retrieval.

choices.text: Search text only in supplier documents and have the generation model infer the product relationships.
choices.explanation: The supplier can be identified, but the evidence does not include the links between components and products.

choices.text: Consider GraphRAG using Neptune Analytics, and use relationships between elements from multiple documents during retrieval.
choices.explanation: Relationships can be followed across entities in separate documents, allowing relevant information to be provided for generation.

source.label: Amazon BedrockとNeptune Analyticsのグラフ検索

learning.reason: Represent relationships across documents as a graph and use multiple related elements as retrieval context.
learning.concept: Text similarity and links between separate elements are different signals.

sourceLabel: Graph search with Amazon Bedrock and Neptune Analytics

title: Use an Existing Search Index as Grounding for Generative AI
prompt: A company has an active Amazon Kendra GenAI index covering several document repositories. It wants to use Bedrock to generate answers for internal teams that share the same document access permissions, but it cannot copy the documents to another repository or operate a separate vector index. What should it configure?

choices.text: Connect the existing Kendra GenAI index to Bedrock Knowledge Bases and use it for retrieval.
choices.explanation: This retrieves grounding information from the active index for answer generation.

choices.text: Export all content from Kendra and build a separate vector index dedicated to Bedrock.
choices.explanation: This could support answer generation, but it requires copying the documents and operating another index.

choices.text: Train a foundation model only on Kendra search logs, without invoking the document index.
choices.explanation: Search-query patterns may be available, but the current internal documents would not be retrieved when answering.

choices.text: Do not use the existing internal documents; add a shared system instruction to every request.
choices.explanation: This can control response behavior, but it cannot provide facts tied to the internal documents.

source.label: Bedrockで既存のKendra GenAIインデックスを使う

learning.reason: If the existing GenAI index can be connected to a knowledge base, it can provide context for answers without creating another search index.
learning.concept: Check whether this configuration is supported for the existing index type and connection requirements.

sourceLabel: Use an existing Kendra GenAI index with Bedrock

title: Delete Derived Vectors for a Retired Document Source
prompt: A data source dedicated to old product manuals is being retired from Bedrock Knowledge Bases. The documents in S3 must be kept as evidence, but embeddings generated on the knowledge-base side must not remain in the index. For a compatible configuration, which deletion policy is appropriate?

choices.text: Set the policy to RETAIN and delete the data source.
choices.explanation: This policy keeps ingested data in the vector store after the source is detached, so it does not meet the requirement.

choices.text: Set the data deletion policy to DELETE and delete the data source.
choices.explanation: This policy deletes derived data ingested into the index. The requirement to retain the original S3 documents is separate.

choices.text: Delete the S3 documents and do not check what happens to the ingestion results.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement to retain the original documents and does not verify index deletion.

choices.text: Reject old product names at query time and leave the index unchanged.
choices.explanation: This may control some queries, but the derived vectors remain physically present.

source.label: Bedrockのデータソース削除

learning.reason: Delete the data source with a policy that includes deleting data from the index, then verify that no derived vectors remain.
learning.concept: Removing a data source from a knowledge base and deciding whether to retain its ingested data in the index are separate decisions.

title: Separate CSV Descriptions from Filter Attributes
prompt: Each row in a product CSV has one description, a category, and a stock status. Searches for paraphrases of the descriptions should use semantic search, while a specified category or stock status should be filtered by exact match. Which configuration should be used to ingest the CSV into a knowledge base?

choices.text: Use only the category as searchable content and do not ingest the descriptions.
choices.explanation: Product names and attributes might be searchable, but semantic search over the description content would not be possible.

choices.text: Treat the entire CSV as one document and use the category as a style instruction during generation.
choices.explanation: This does not filter results by comparing attributes at the row level.

choices.text: Treat the description as content, store the category and stock status as row metadata, and filter on them during retrieval.
choices.explanation: This supports semantic search over descriptions while applying exact conditions on separate attributes.

choices.text: Append the category and stock status to the description and rely only on similarity scores to determine exact matches.
choices.explanation: Semantic similarity is not the same as an exact match, so results with a different category could still be returned.

source.label: BedrockのCSVの列とメタデータ

learning.reason: Specify the description column as content and keep the category and stock status as metadata that can be used to filter rows.
learning.concept: Keep columns used for filtering as matchable attributes instead of merely concatenating them into the semantic-search text.

title: Get the Final Amount from the Existing Calculation Service
prompt: A quoting chatbot can organize the items provided verbally. Discount and tax calculations must use the results from an audited calculation service. From the generated model output through displaying the final amount, which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Put the calculation method in the prompt and use the amount estimated by the model as the final value.
choices.explanation: The calculation steps can be provided in text, but this does not use the audited service's result.

choices.text: Search past quotes and return the amount for a similar set of terms as the current quote.
choices.explanation: A past amount can be a reference, but it is not calculated using the current quote's discount and tax.

choices.text: Run the model at a low temperature and make its reproducible amount the authoritative result.
choices.explanation: Even if the result is more reproducible, this does not ensure that it was calculated by the required service.

choices.text: Have the application receive calculation arguments from the model, call the service, and display the value returned by the service in the final amount field.
choices.explanation: The model can handle the conversation and organize inputs, while the required service provides the authoritative value.

source.label: Bedrockのクライアント側ツール実行

learning.reason: Have the generative model organize the calculation arguments, and have the application obtain the final value from the calculation service.
learning.concept: Treat model-based input organization and business calculations that require accuracy as separate processes.

title: Prepare reference answers for evaluation
prompt: Even for the same policy, one candidate answer tends to omit important conditions. You want to compare candidates based on how well they satisfy the conditions in a reference answer, not on how natural their wording sounds. What evaluation data should you create?

choices.text: Associate each evaluation question with a reference answer that includes the policy conditions required to answer it.
choices.explanation: This lets you compare candidate responses against the same required conditions.

choices.text: Evaluate using only the questions and choose the response with the most natural wording.
choices.explanation: This can assess fluency, but it provides no information for checking whether conditions were omitted.

choices.text: Record only the expected length of both candidate answers.
choices.explanation: Answers of the same length can still differ in which required conditions they include.

choices.text: Record the model's answer afterward as that model's reference answer.
choices.explanation: If the model's own output omits a condition, that omission will also be missing from the reference, so it cannot be detected.

source.label: Bedrockの評価用プロンプトデータ

learning.reason: Provide a reference answer or other reference information containing the conditions to compare, and associate it with the question to evaluate both candidates.
learning.concept: Readability and coverage of the items an answer must address require different comparison materials.

title: Add a new internal announcement to the index without an intermediate file
prompt: Each time a notification app receives a new internal announcement, you want to add its content as a document. You use a Bedrock custom data source and cannot stage the announcement as a temporary S3 file or wait for the next batch synchronization. How should you ingest it?

choices.text: Collect notifications into a nightly batch, write them to S3 as files each night, and then synchronize.
choices.explanation: This allows ingestion, but it violates the requirement not to stage files in S3 or wait.

choices.text: Have the app ingest the announcement text directly into the custom data source as a document.
choices.explanation: This adds the document without first placing it in an external storage location.

choices.text: Add the announcement text only as a fixed instruction in the generation prompt.
choices.explanation: This can provide the information for a particular invocation, but it does not add a document to the search index.

choices.text: Retrain the foundation model on the announcement text each time a new announcement is published.
choices.explanation: Model tuning is a different process from adding an announcement as a search candidate.

source.label: Bedrockのナレッジベースへの直接取り込み

learning.reason: Use an ingestion operation that adds the announcement content directly to the custom data source.
learning.concept: Periodically synchronizing an existing external data source and directly ingesting app content as individual documents are different approaches.

sourceLabel: Direct ingestion into a Bedrock knowledge base

title: Design the search query and displayed answer separately
prompt: In a policy application, you want to resolve which program name “it” refers to in the conversation before searching, then display the final answer as a comparison table. When using Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, which settings should you configure for each task? Choose TWO.

choices.text: Specify how to use the conversation before searching in the setting responsible for orchestration.
choices.explanation: This corresponds to interpreting the conversation and using that interpretation to form the query for retrieval.

choices.text: Set the instruction to render the answer as a table in the maximum number of search results.
choices.explanation: This changes the number of results retrieved, but does not instruct generation to produce a comparison table.

choices.text: Resolve the program name after generation and assume that this will add more retrieved candidates.
choices.explanation: Retrieval has already finished, so resolving the pronoun afterward will not automatically add candidates.

choices.text: Configure the instruction to produce an evidence-based comparison table in the generation-side template.
choices.explanation: Separate from the search query format, this setting specifies the format for output based on retrieved documents.

choices.text: Put all inputs and documents related to the search date into a shared style setting.
choices.explanation: This mixes display guidance with search conditions and does not specify either requirement appropriately.

source.label: Bedrockの検索・生成のカスタマイズ

learning.reason: The construction of the query sent for retrieval and the process of generating an answer from evidence can be configured separately.
learning.concept: Changing the final answer format does not guarantee that the same documents were retrieved beforehand; add necessary search terms before retrieval.

sourceLabel: Customizing retrieval and generation with Bedrock

title: Keep retrieved evidence available with a custom template
prompt: After changing the generation template for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases to a custom format, the answer stopped using documents even though the retrieval service was finding relevant material. The retrieval settings were not changed. What should you check first in the template?

choices.text: Only double the maximum number of search results.
choices.explanation: This may increase the number of retrieved candidates, but the cause of the template not receiving them remains.

choices.text: Ask the same model to answer again and assume that similar wording means it used retrieval.
choices.explanation: This may check reproducibility, but it does not show whether the model referenced a particular retrieved document.

choices.text: Generate a longer answer without using the retrieved documents.
choices.explanation: This increases the output, but does not use the retrieved evidence as input.

choices.text: Check that the custom generation template still has a placeholder that expands to include the retrieved results.
choices.explanation: This verifies the prerequisite that the retrieved evidence is actually passed to generation.

source.label: Bedrockの取得資料を使う生成テンプレート

learning.reason: Check whether the generation template includes a location where retrieved results are inserted.
learning.concept: Successful retrieval and the generation model receiving those results as input are separate things.

sourceLabel: Generation templates that use retrieved Bedrock documents

title: Exclude only names that have not yet been announced
prompt: In a public FAQ, any answer containing an unannounced product code must be withheld. Questions about announced products in the same field, and ordinary words that resemble a code, should still be answered as usual. If the short list of pre-release codes is finalized, which guardrail is appropriate?

choices.text: Add the specified codes to a word filter to check for those exact terms.
choices.explanation: This targets only the terms of concern without prohibiting discussion of every similar topic.

choices.text: Set the entire related product area as a denied topic.
choices.explanation: This might block answers containing the codes, but it would also cover discussion of announced products.

choices.text: Raise the minimum relevance score for documents.
choices.explanation: An answer can be strongly grounded in relevant documents and still contain a prohibited code.

choices.text: Strengthen the output filter for safety categories.
choices.explanation: Changing detection levels for harmful topics does not check a list of pre-release product codes.

source.label: Bedrock Guardrailsの語句フィルター

learning.reason: When the target is a short, fixed list and discussion of similar topics should remain allowed, a filter that targets the specified terms is appropriate.
learning.concept: Controlling fixed terms and semantically detecting prohibited topics with varied wording serve different purposes.

title: Inspect an attached image even when the text is harmless
prompt: A product-advice chat processes images attached to otherwise normal inquiries. Because an image alone may violate the permitted-use policy, it must be inspected before it is passed to the model. Which feature in the corresponding Bedrock configuration should be used?

choices.text: Apply a text content filter to the question itself and leave the attached image unchecked.
choices.explanation: The image content attached to harmless text would not be inspected.

choices.text: Use a guardrail that inspects the image modality in the input content.
choices.explanation: This allows harmful content in an image to be evaluated when the attached image is processed.

choices.text: Record the image's origin in metadata without evaluating its contents.
choices.explanation: The origin could be tracked, but this would not determine whether the image content violates policy.

choices.text: Inspect only the model's response text and pass the input image through as is.
choices.explanation: Even if content appearing in the output can be blocked, the input image reaches the model first.

source.label: Bedrock Guardrailsの画像用コンテンツフィルター

learning.reason: The relevant inspection must run on the input image to detect harmful content represented in it.
learning.concept: A finding that the text input is safe does not establish that an attached image is safe.

title: Explain at different levels of detail to users and operators
prompt: A delivery forecast is being released. Users need to understand how to use the forecast and the limits of its accuracy, while operators need to trace the evaluation conditions and model version during audits. There is no need to share detailed internal architecture with general users. Which two approaches to documentation are appropriate?

choices.text: Briefly tell users how to use the forecast, its typical limitations, and where to direct questions about the results.
choices.explanation: Users can judge how to handle the output.

choices.text: Publish all the source code without explaining how users should interpret the forecast or contact anyone.
choices.explanation: The code alone does not explain the forecast's limitations or what to do when questions arise.

choices.text: Use only the user-facing evaluation score for internal audits, without recording test conditions or the model version.
choices.explanation: A summary of performance is available, but there is no way to confirm which version was evaluated under which conditions.

choices.text: Provide operators with documentation that lets them check the evaluation data conditions, model version, and known limitations.
choices.explanation: Auditors can trace and verify the assumptions and history behind a decision.

choices.text: Give both groups the same complete internal reasoning logs and treat documentation as unnecessary.
choices.explanation: The information is not organized for each audience's needs, and the scope of sharing is too broad.

source.label: Responsible AI Lensの透明性戦略

learning.reason: Even for the same system, users and auditors need different information and different levels of detail to make decisions.
learning.concept: Explain assumptions and limitations to users, and provide detailed reproducibility information to relevant stakeholders with access controls.

title: Mandatory release criteria take precedence over usability
prompt: Candidate A for a consultation guide was preferred because its answers were concise, but it failed a mandatory release criterion: personal information must not be displayed on screen. Candidate B meets the no-display requirement and the other mandatory criteria, though its wording is somewhat longer. What is the appropriate release decision at this point?

choices.text: Average the safety and preference scores for both candidates, and release A if it ranks higher.
choices.explanation: This would let a score for a different quality compensate for failure to meet a mandatory criterion.

choices.text: Release A to a small group of users and decide whether displaying personal information matters only after complaints arise.
choices.explanation: A limited release does not demonstrate compliance with a mandatory pre-release condition.

choices.text: Add a user-facing disclaimer to A’s output and skip the check.
choices.explanation: A disclaimer does not guarantee that personal information will not be displayed.

choices.text: Choose B, which meets the mandatory criteria, and correct A’s failure before reevaluating it.
choices.explanation: User preferences can be considered, but failure to meet a mandatory release criterion must not be accepted.

source.label: Responsible AI Lensの未達成の公開基準

learning.reason: Do not average away a mandatory safety criterion with preference or speed scores.
learning.concept: Release a configuration that meets the specified criteria, and investigate and reevaluate candidates that do not.

sourceLabel: Unmet release criteria in the Responsible AI Lens

title: Pause Finalization When the Verification System Is Unavailable
prompt: An admissions office AI can finalize an application status only when the credential number appears in the verification service’s records. The verification service timed out, but the model strongly predicts from past cases that the credential number is valid. What should the system do until the service is available again?

choices.text: State that verification is unavailable, hold finalization, and route the case for manual review.
choices.explanation: This avoids finalizing without verification while providing a way for processing to continue.

choices.text: Treat the strong prediction as evidence of validity, finalize the case, and review only mismatches after the service recovers.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the requirement to check the record before finalization.

choices.text: Treat the timeout the same as a negative verification response and finalize rejection for every case.
choices.explanation: This confuses an inability to verify with a verified negative result and would cause unnecessary rejections.

choices.text: Ask a fallback generative model to estimate validity too, and finalize if the two predictions match.
choices.explanation: Matching predictions still do not mean the verification service was successfully queried.

source.label: Generative AI Lensの障害時の代替動作

learning.reason: When required data cannot be obtained, do not substitute a confident estimate; hold the case or route it for human review.
learning.concept: A design that lets a person correct an already finalized action later differs from one that prevents the action until verification is complete.

sourceLabel: Generative AI Lens fallback behavior during service outages

title: Check Whether an Explanation Reflects the Actual Decision
prompt: A model automatically prioritizes transactions, and a separate generative model writes a rationale. The text reads naturally, but you want to check whether the stated reasons are related to the prioritization model’s behavior. Which check best serves this purpose?

choices.text: Measure only whether the explanation is brief and contains no prohibited phrases.
choices.explanation: This can assess readability requirements, but it does not check whether the reasons are accurate.

choices.text: For representative cases, compare the factors cited in the explanations with the actual basis or behavior of the decisions, and detect discrepancies.
choices.explanation: This can verify whether the explanations are factually faithful to the original model.

choices.text: Have another model score the grammar, and treat a high score as proof that the reasons are correct.
choices.explanation: Even grammatically correct text can cite features the decision did not use.

choices.text: Create a standard rationale for all cases and display the same text for every individual case.
choices.explanation: This makes the display consistent but does not represent the factors that differed across individual decisions.

source.label: Responsible AI Lensの説明可能性の測定

learning.reason: Explanation quality includes not only readability but also whether an explanation reflects the actual reasons behind a decision.
learning.concept: Even when generative AI makes a model’s explanation easier to read, it must still be checked against the original decision and its factors.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Prevent External Communication from Training Containers
prompt: A training job in SageMaker AI must be configured so that the training container cannot communicate with external services or directly receive the execution role’s credentials. The SageMaker service must continue to transfer approved S3 data. Which feature should you choose?

choices.text: Only encrypt the data’s S3 bucket with KMS.
choices.explanation: This protects data at rest but does not prevent external communication from the running container.

choices.text: Enable SageMaker network isolation for the training job.
choices.explanation: It restricts outbound communication and direct access to credentials from the container, while SageMaker handles data transfer.

choices.text: Use a subnet with outbound access and enable only VPC Flow Logs.
choices.explanation: This lets you observe traffic but does not prohibit direct connections from the container.

choices.text: Store model artifacts in a bucket with restricted access.
choices.explanation: This can restrict access to artifacts, but container communication and credential access are separate requirements.

source.label: SageMaker network isolation

learning.reason: The network boundary for a running container must be designed separately from protection for stored data.
learning.concept: Restricting outbound communication from AI workloads.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Continuously Scan Inference Image Vulnerabilities
prompt: You want to detect newly disclosed vulnerabilities in existing inference images stored in Amazon ECR without pushing the same tag again. Which feature and setting are appropriate?

choices.text: Scan images only when they are pushed, and exclude scanned images from rescanning.
choices.explanation: This finds issues present at registration but does not check for issues disclosed later.

choices.text: Make tags immutable and leave images unchanged after registering them.
choices.explanation: This can prevent tags from being overwritten, but it does not scan that image version for newly discovered vulnerabilities.

choices.text: Use ECR enhanced scanning integrated with Amazon Inspector, and set the target repositories to continuous scanning.
choices.explanation: This continuously scans the target images as new vulnerability information becomes available.

choices.text: Monitor CPU and memory in the runtime environment and treat only images with high values as problematic.
choices.explanation: This can monitor load but does not continuously scan for package vulnerabilities.

source.label: Amazon Inspector ECR scanning

learning.reason: Reassess images already supplied as new vulnerability information becomes available.
learning.concept: Continuous vulnerability management for AI containers.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Automatically Remediate Configuration Drift in an AI Environment
prompt: In an AI development environment, you want to continuously detect resources that lack required governance tags and invoke an approved tag-correction procedure for the applicable resource types. The procedure must cover both newly noncompliant resources and resources whose tags are removed later. Which capability should you use?

choices.text: Use only a policy that enforces tags when resources are created, without checking their configuration afterward.
choices.explanation: Controlling resource creation does not detect or remediate tags removed later.

choices.text: Record tag changes with CloudTrail, but do not remediate them.
choices.explanation: This provides an operation history, but no procedure to correct detected noncompliance.

choices.text: Enable cost allocation tags for billing and aggregate resources without tags under the same department.
choices.explanation: This setting classifies billing data; it does not correct resource tags.

choices.text: Associate an AWS Config detection rule with an approved remediation action implemented through Systems Manager Automation.
choices.explanation: You can inspect the current state and invoke a defined action for noncompliant resources.

source.label: AWS Config remediation

learning.reason: Configuration governance can automate not only detection but also approved corrective procedures.
learning.concept: Detecting and remediating configuration drift.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Centrally Manage Findings Across AI Accounts
prompt: A central reliability team wants to prioritize security findings detected across multiple accounts and in-scope Regions in the same organization. Keep each service's original detections operating as they do today, and provide a way to work with AWS findings from a single aggregation destination. Which approach should you use?

choices.text: Manage the in-scope accounts through a Security Hub CSPM administrator account, and configure an aggregation Region and its linked Regions.
choices.explanation: This aggregates findings from the in-scope environment centrally so you can prioritize them without opening multiple locations.

choices.text: Only enable CloudTrail in the target Regions for the management account.
choices.explanation: This records operations, but does not aggregate findings from each detection service as findings.

choices.text: Collect evidence only for selected controls with AWS Audit Manager and assume that all findings will also appear in the same view.
choices.explanation: Audit evidence is its focus; it differs from aggregating findings from multiple services for prioritization.

choices.text: Process findings independently in each account without making all findings available centrally.
choices.explanation: Local processing is possible, but central staff cannot prioritize findings across the organization.

source.label: Security Hub CSPMのクロスリージョン集約

learning.reason: Central visibility of detections enables cross-organization prioritization and response management.
learning.concept: Aggregating security findings.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Monitor AI Workloads on EKS at Runtime
prompt: You run inference containers on EKS. The images have been scanned before deployment, but you also want to detect unusual process and network activity in the containers during operation. Which capability should you add?

choices.text: Configure ECR push-time scanning again.
choices.explanation: This can inspect registered images, but not behavior that occurs while they are running.

choices.text: Use GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring for the target cluster.
choices.explanation: It can detect potential threats based on activity in running workloads.

choices.text: Continuously check the cluster configuration with AWS Config.
choices.explanation: This can detect configuration drift, but it does not detect process activity at runtime.

choices.text: Enable AWS WAF in front of the access path.
choices.explanation: It can control incoming web requests, but does not monitor runtime events inside containers.

source.label: GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring

learning.reason: Running AI workloads need runtime protection in addition to container image scanning.
learning.concept: Detecting threats at container runtime.

title: Two Departments Use Different Meanings for the Closed-Won Label
prompt: You want to predict contract signing across sales departments. When you examine the histories, one department uses “closed won” to mean a contract was signed, while the other uses it once an opportunity can be opened. Both histories retain the contract signing date. What should you do to create training data for the same classifier?

choices.text: Keep the current labels and make the proportions of positive and negative examples the same in each department.
choices.explanation: This aligns the proportions, but the meaning of a positive example still differs between departments.

choices.text: Train with the current labels and use a different inference decision threshold for each sales department.
choices.explanation: You can adjust the proportion of positive predictions, but the prediction target used for training remains inconsistent.

choices.text: Fix the prediction target as contract signing and recreate the training labels for both departments based on the recorded signing dates.
choices.explanation: This makes the same label represent the same outcome in both departments and produces consistent training data.

choices.text: Keep the current labels and add the sales department as a feature for the classifier.
choices.explanation: The classifier may learn departmental differences, but the opportunity-opened label still will not represent a signed contract.
