source.label: SageMaker AIの教師あり学習

learning.reason: The same label can represent the same outcome in both departments, producing consistent training data.
learning.concept: Even when label names match, check the business conditions that define a positive example.

title: Encode satisfaction levels without losing their order
prompt: You are building a simple model to predict whether a customer inquiry will recur. Survey satisfaction has three levels—low, medium, and high—and you can add just one input column for comparison. You want to pass the direction of increasing levels to an existing linear model as a single numeric feature. Which transformation meets the requirement?

choices.text: Assign 0, 1, and 2 in the character-code order of the category names.
choices.explanation: This produces one column, but the string ordering does not necessarily match the satisfaction ordering.

choices.text: Assign a separate column containing 0 or 1 to each of the three categories.
choices.explanation: This represents the categories without assuming a numeric relationship among them, but it does not encode the direction of the levels in a single column.

choices.text: Assign 0, 1, and 2 to the levels in order from most frequent to least frequent.
choices.explanation: Ordering by frequency confuses the most common level with the highest satisfaction level.

choices.text: Follow the business ordering and assign 0, 1, and 2 to low, medium, and high, respectively.
choices.explanation: This preserves the increasing direction in one column. Because the linear term assumes equal spacing between levels, validate that assumption.

source.label: scikit-learnの順序エンコーディング

learning.reason: This preserves the increasing direction of the levels in one column. Because the linear term assumes equal spacing between levels, validate that assumption.
learning.concept: When encoding an ordinal scale, reflect the business-defined order rather than the labels’ written order or their frequencies.

title: When future values are known without leaking the outcome
prompt: You are forecasting daily sales for the next month. The model can take additional features for the forecast period. The promotion start dates and details will be approved and finalized before forecasting, and records of past promotions are available. Along with historical results, which future information should you use?

choices.text: Use the promotion dates and types already confirmed when generating the forecast as features for each day in the forecast horizon.
choices.explanation: The model can learn how sales changed during past promotions, and the future values are available before forecasting with the same meaning.

choices.text: Use the actual number of coupons used on each promotion date as a feature for the forecast for that date.
choices.explanation: This relates to the promotion’s effect, but the actual coupon count is not known at forecast time.

choices.text: Calculate the realized sales increase for each promotion in the next month and use it as a feature for product-level forecasts.
choices.explanation: The sales increase includes outcomes from the forecast period and cannot be used in production.

choices.text: Use the final calendar, including future promotion changes, only during training, regardless of whether it is finalized at forecast time.
choices.explanation: Training would have access to more information than is available in production, so the model could not be evaluated under the same conditions it will face in operation.

source.label: SageMaker Canvasの時系列予測

learning.reason: The model can learn how sales changed during past promotions, and future values are available before forecasting with the same meaning.
learning.concept: Even when forecasting the future, planned values that are confirmed at inference time can be used as features.

title: Carry preferences into conversations on other days
prompt: An educational content recommendation assistant should use a learner’s preference for text over video, shared in a previous conversation, in a new conversation. It should retrieve only that learner’s preferences without sending the full history of past conversations to the model each time. Which design is appropriate?

choices.text: Retrieve the full previous conversation and prepend it to the prompt each time.
choices.explanation: This would tell the model about the preference, but it would violate the requirement not to send the full conversation each time.

choices.text: Use an AgentCore Memory long-term strategy that extracts user preferences, and retrieve the records for each learner.
choices.explanation: It can extract preferences from conversations and make them available in later sessions for the same learner.

choices.text: Retrieve short-term memory events using a newly issued session ID.
choices.explanation: The new session ID has no events containing preferences or questions from the previous conversation.

choices.text: Use a session summarization strategy and provide only a summary of the new session itself.
choices.explanation: The referenced scope does not include the previous session, so it cannot carry over the preference.

source.label: AgentCore Memoryの組み込み戦略

learning.reason: Preferences can be extracted from conversations and used in later sessions for the same learner.
learning.concept: Short-term memory, which maintains working context within a conversation, serves a different purpose from extracting preferences for use across sessions.

title: Make an existing inventory lookup available as a shared tool
prompt: An API Gateway REST API is available for inventory lookups. You want assistants that support MCP, built by different teams with different frameworks, to discover and call this operation in a common way. You do not want to modify the existing API or add conversion logic to each client. What should you choose?

choices.text: Add the REST API specification to Bedrock Knowledge Bases and have every client search it.
choices.explanation: Clients could search for argument descriptions, but that alone would not execute an operation that returns current inventory.

choices.text: Share the existing API’s OpenAPI document and have clients call it directly over HTTPS.
choices.explanation: Clients can refer to a shared specification, but this does not make the operation discoverable and directly callable as a tool by existing MCP clients.

choices.text: Register the REST API as a target in AgentCore Gateway and expose it as an MCP tool.
choices.explanation: The Gateway translates between MCP and the existing HTTP API.

choices.text: Register the REST API directly in each framework and align the invocation format team by team.
choices.explanation: The existing API can remain, but each framework’s definitions and conversion logic would need to be maintained.

source.label: API Gateway REST APIとAgentCore Gateway

learning.reason: The Gateway translates between MCP and the existing HTTP API.
learning.concept: MCP provides a common interface for compatible agents to discover and call operations in existing services.

sourceLabel: API Gateway REST APIs and AgentCore Gateway

title: Preserving a Review Path Defined by Policy
prompt: A shipping company is designing an application review process with Strands Agents. It routes reviews by package type and sends a request back for clarification if required approval details are missing. The policy fixes both the route and the maximum number of clarification cycles. Which design is appropriate if each reviewer’s work should use a model?

choices.text: Use a Swarm, letting each reviewer who reads the policy decide who should handle the request next and when to stop.
choices.explanation: This allows flexible handoffs, but transition decisions depend on the model’s interpretation.

choices.text: Use Agents as Tools, letting a supervisor model choose the reviewer and the number of clarification cycles.
choices.explanation: The supervisor can consolidate results, but the branching and stopping conditions are not fixed to follow the policy.

choices.text: Use a fixed Workflow that sends every request through all reviewers in the same order each time.
choices.explanation: The order stays consistent, but this cannot branch by package type or request clarification only when details are missing.

choices.text: Use a Graph with a node for each reviewer and define conditional transitions and a stopping condition for clarification cycles.
choices.explanation: The reviewers’ work can use models while the application controls which conditions move a request to the next reviewer.

source.label: Strands Agentsの複数エージェント構成

learning.reason: The reviewers’ work can use models while the application controls which conditions move a request to the next reviewer.
learning.concept: An application can control fixed transition conditions separately from the individual decisions delegated to reviewer agents.

title: Generating Multiple Furniture Designs from the Same Prompt
prompt: A furniture image-generation model was trained to infer the original features of an image after noise was added. At inference time, you want it to create several new designs from the same text without searching stored photographs. Which operation corresponds to this training method?

choices.text: Start with different initial noise and gradually remove noise while conditioning on the text.
choices.explanation: This uses the learned reverse process and can produce separate images from different initial noise.

choices.text: Vectorize the text and stored photographs, then return them in descending order of similarity.
choices.explanation: Retrieval finds similar existing designs; it does not create new ones.

choices.text: Predict image tokens one at a time from left to right, using each prior output as the next input.
choices.explanation: This is an example of an autoregressive approach, unlike the denoising training process described in the question.

choices.text: Train a generator and discriminator against each other to learn whether images are realistic.
choices.explanation: Adversarial training is a different generative modeling approach; it does not generate images through gradual denoising.

source.label: AWSの拡散モデルの解説

learning.reason: This uses the learned reverse process and can produce separate images from different initial noise.
learning.concept: Diffusion models distinguish the training process that adds noise from the generation process that removes it.

title: Evaluating a Question Phrasing That Appeared Only After Launch
prompt: A facility reservation assistant has been launched. Pre-launch evaluation using only formally worded questions scored well, but users often ask concise, elliptical questions such as “Is that place free next week?” What should the first step in continuous improvement be if the next revision must also preserve quality on formally phrased questions?

choices.text: Compare the revision with the previous version using only the total number of production questions and response time.
choices.explanation: This measures usage and speed, but not whether the assistant correctly understood elliptical questions.

choices.text: Add representative examples from actual elliptical questions to the evaluation set, keep the existing examples, and compare before and after the revision.
choices.explanation: This lets you reproduce the failure while checking for regressions on the previous inputs using the same process.

choices.text: Rewrite actual questions in formal language before adding them to the evaluation set.
choices.explanation: This removes the ellipsis that caused the failure, so the production issue cannot be reproduced.

choices.text: Replace the evaluation set with only elliptical questions to assess this issue.
choices.explanation: This can check the issue in scope, but it no longer tracks quality on formally worded inputs that the assistant handled before.

source.label: 生成AIのライフサイクル

learning.reason: This lets you reproduce the failure while checking for regressions on the previous inputs using the same process.
learning.concept: When production reveals a change in input patterns, include it in the next evaluation while retaining existing cases.

title: Rerunning Only Failed Rows in a Nightly Batch
prompt: An overnight product-description batch ran on Amazon Bedrock. The job is Completed, but some result rows contain generation errors. The successful descriptions have been reviewed and must be preserved; only the failed products should be processed again. Which method is appropriate?

choices.text: Treat Completed as success for every row and make up the missing results in the next full refresh.
choices.explanation: Even if the job as a whole is complete, individual result rows can fail. Successful content would also be regenerated.

choices.text: Look only for input files with no output file, then rerun every product in those files.
choices.explanation: This does not handle cases where successful and failed rows are in the same output file.

choices.text: Check each row’s error in the S3 output JSONL and match it to the original input using recordId.
choices.explanation: This associates errors with products so you can extract only the failed products’ inputs.

choices.text: Check errorRecordCount in the manifest and rerun that many inputs from the end of the input file.
choices.explanation: This gives the failure count, but failed records are not necessarily grouped at the end.

source.label: Amazon Bedrockのバッチ推論結果

learning.reason: This associates errors with products so you can extract only the failed products’ inputs.
learning.concept: For batch inference, check success and failure at the record level independently of the overall job status.

title: Agree on refund conditions and design before implementation
prompt: An exam registration service wants the business and development teams to agree on refund-processing exceptions before implementation. The team wants generative AI to assist with implementation while leaving repository artifacts that let them review acceptance criteria, design, and implementation tasks separately. Which approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Use Kiro chat to generate code and record the exception conditions later in code comments.
choices.explanation: This can assist with implementation, but it does not let the team review the requirements and design separately before implementation.

choices.text: Document shared terminology in Kiro Steering, then provide the exception-handling specification and tasks in chat as needed.
choices.explanation: This can keep terminology consistent, but it leaves no artifacts documenting the agreed specifications and tasks for each feature.

choices.text: Use Kiro Hooks to generate tests when code changes, and make those tests the sole record of the requirements.
choices.explanation: Tests help verify behavior, but this does not meet the requirement to approve acceptance criteria and design before implementation.

choices.text: Document requirements, design, and tasks in Kiro Specs, then have the team review them before implementation.
choices.explanation: This lets the team review conditions and design before implementation and link the agreed points to tasks.

source.label: Kiroの仕様駆動ワークフロー

learning.reason: This lets the team review conditions and design before implementation and link the agreed points to tasks.
learning.concept: With specification-driven development assistance, requirements, design, and implementation tasks are recorded in stages in a form that can be reviewed.

title: Isolate in-progress execution state from concurrent users
prompt: An image-editing assistant lets users request several revisions to the same work while viewing the output. Temporary files from an in-progress edit must be available to the next invocation for that work, while remaining isolated from other users' work. The team does not want to operate its own execution servers. Which architecture is appropriate?

choices.text: Use AgentCore Runtime to create a separate session for each work item, and invoke the same work item with the same session ID.
choices.explanation: Temporary execution state can be reused within a session and isolated from other sessions.

choices.text: Have everyone use one Runtime session and put the work item name at the start of each prompt.
choices.explanation: The model receives the work item name, but this does not create an isolation boundary for execution state or files.

choices.text: Save editing instructions in AgentCore Memory and create a different Runtime session for each invocation.
choices.explanation: The conversation instructions can be retrieved, but temporary files in the previous execution environment are not carried over.

choices.text: Give tools on AgentCore Gateway a different name for each work item, then route them to the same Runtime session.
choices.explanation: Changing tool names does not isolate the temporary state at the destination.

source.label: AgentCore Runtimeの分離されたセッション

learning.reason: Temporary execution state can be reused within a session and isolated from other sessions.
learning.concept: Temporary files and execution-process state for a conversation need an isolation boundary distinct from conversation records stored in memory.

title: Keep speaker-attributed utterances in the source and translated text
prompt: A single recording channel contains speech from several people. For auditing, the service must store a speaker-attributed transcript in the original language and a translation for each utterance. Audio responses and summaries are not needed. Which components should be combined?

choices.text: Convert the audio into speech in another language, then transcribe only the translated audio with speaker attribution.
choices.explanation: This produces a translation, but it does not preserve a record that associates the original-language utterances with their speakers.

choices.text: Use Amazon Transcribe to obtain a speaker-attributed transcript in the original language, then translate the utterance text with Amazon Translate.
choices.explanation: This preserves the association between speakers and utterances and produces a translation for each utterance.

choices.text: Create a transcript without speaker attribution, then translate the entire transcript as a whole.
choices.explanation: This provides source and translated text, but does not record which speaker said each utterance.

choices.text: Summarize the speaker-attributed transcript and store only each speaker's summary and its translation.
choices.explanation: This preserves key points, but not the original utterances and their translations required for auditing.

source.label: Amazon Transcribeの話者分離

learning.reason: This preserves the association between speakers and utterances and produces a translation for each utterance.
learning.concept: Identifying speakers in a single audio channel and translating utterance text are separate functions.

title: Sequence the adoption of an existing foundation model
prompt: A municipality is planning to provide assistance with summarizing application letters. It cannot afford to train a model from scratch, so it will use an existing model and adjust it only if needed. Arrange the work in dependency order, including evaluation before and after launch.

choices.text: Launch a configuration that meets the criteria, then identify improvements from user feedback and failure cases.
choices.explanation: After launch, the team can observe actual usage and apply what it learns to the next round of improvements and evaluation.

choices.text: Prepare examples of application letters and acceptance criteria, then compare existing foundation models against those criteria.
choices.explanation: Preparing the use case and selection criteria first makes it possible to determine whether an existing model meets the requirements.

choices.text: Adjust the selected model if needed, then evaluate the configuration intended for actual delivery using pre-launch examples.
choices.explanation: After selecting the base model, evaluate whether the configuration, including any adjustments, meets the acceptance criteria.

source.label: 生成AIのライフサイクル

learning.reason: Preparing the use case and selection criteria first makes it possible to determine whether an existing model meets the requirements.
learning.concept: Model evaluation supports both pre-deployment selection and ongoing improvement after launch.

title: Create video footage without changing approved captions
prompt: A production company is using video generation AI to create new background footage for an advertisement. The required captions have already been proofread and must not change by even one character when published. The editing team must also be able to adjust the captions’ position and font. Which production workflow is appropriate?

choices.text: Put the proofread captions in quotation marks in the prompt and generate them as text within the footage.
choices.explanation: The model may convey the text, but there is no guarantee it will render the exact characters.

choices.text: Provide an image containing the proofread captions as the first frame, then generate a video with the captions included throughout.
choices.explanation: The image can specify the starting frame, but it does not guarantee that the text will remain unchanged in later frames or be independently editable.

choices.text: Inspect the finished video with text recognition and regenerate it with the same prompt until the captions match.
choices.explanation: Inspection can detect mismatches, but it does not make caption position and font independently editable as a separate layer.

choices.text: Generate footage without captions, then overlay the proofread text on a separate layer in video editing software.
choices.explanation: This keeps the fixed text and its display settings separate from the video generation.

source.label: 生成動画における文字描写の制限の例（提供終了モデルのサービスカード）

learning.reason: This keeps the fixed text and its display settings separate from the video generation.
learning.concept: When captions must match character for character, composite them deterministically over the generated footage.

sourceLabel: Example of limitations in rendering text in generated video (service card for a discontinued model)

title: Use vector search and existing operational tables in the same SQL query
prompt: A team is adding semantic search for parts descriptions. Parts inventory and procurement availability are in an existing supported version of Aurora PostgreSQL, and the results must be joined with the inventory table in the same SQL query. The team cannot operate a separate search service or maintain a duplicate inventory. Where should it store the vectors?

choices.text: Enable pgvector in the existing Aurora PostgreSQL database and store the embeddings associated with each part.
choices.explanation: On a supported cluster, vector search and relational filtering or joins can be handled in SQL.

choices.text: Store the embeddings in OpenSearch Serverless, then pass search candidates to Aurora to join with the inventory table.
choices.explanation: Semantic search is possible, but this requires operating a separate search service and splitting search and the join into separate queries.

choices.text: Store vectors with inventory metadata in S3 Vectors and query only that service.
choices.explanation: Even if filtering is possible, this duplicates the existing inventory and does not provide a join in the same SQL query.

choices.text: Register parts as nodes in Neptune Analytics and add relationships to inventory.
choices.explanation: This can support relationship traversal, but it does not join inventory and embeddings inside the existing PostgreSQL database.

source.label: Aurora PostgreSQLをベクトルストアにする

learning.reason: On a supported cluster, vector search and relational filtering or joins can be handled in SQL.
learning.concept: When vector search and existing relational joins must run in one SQL query, one option is to store the vectors in the same supported database.

sourceLabel: Using Aurora PostgreSQL as a vector store

title: An unwanted pattern keeps appearing in the background
prompt: A team is generating a product-photo background with a Stable Image model in Bedrock. The wall color and lighting are as intended, but an unwanted grid pattern appears in part of the image. The team is using a model that lets it preserve desired features and specify unwanted features separately. What should it change first?

choices.text: Keep the positive prompt and increase prompt adherence.
choices.explanation: Adherence applies to the prompt as a whole; it does not exclude one specific feature.

choices.text: Keep the desired wall features in the positive prompt and specify the grid pattern in negative_prompt.
choices.explanation: The model can receive a separate input for the unwanted grid pattern while retaining the desired appearance.

choices.text: Move the wall color to the beginning of the positive prompt and say nothing about the grid pattern.
choices.explanation: This can emphasize the wall color, but it does not explicitly tell the model to suppress the unwanted element.

choices.text: Describe the grid pattern with equal emphasis in both the positive prompt and negative_prompt.
choices.explanation: This gives conflicting instructions about the same feature, so it does not distinguish what is desired from what should be avoided.

source.label: Amazon BedrockのStability AI画像機能

learning.reason: Use the image model’s negative prompt to specify unwanted features separately.
learning.concept: Specify desired features and features to avoid separately.

sourceLabel: Stability AI image capabilities in Amazon Bedrock

title: Stop early when training loss keeps falling
prompt: A team is fine-tuning a foundation model with supervised learning. Loss on the training data keeps decreasing, but loss on validation data representative of the target workload worsened after an initial improvement. For a compatible Amazon Bedrock model, the team wants to automatically stop a long run when validation quality no longer continues to improve. Which setting should it use?

choices.text: Lower only the learning rate and run every epoch each time.
choices.explanation: This reduces the size of updates, but it does not configure early stopping based on worsening validation results.

choices.text: Add the validation data to the training data and decide when to stop based only on the training-loss trend.
choices.explanation: The validation data would no longer be measured independently, so the team could not determine when performance on unseen examples had degraded.

choices.text: Configure early stopping with a minimum improvement in validation loss and a patience limit for when improvement stops.
choices.explanation: This uses validation data held out before publication to determine whether improvement continues, and can stop the run after a set number of rounds without improvement.

choices.text: Increase the number of epochs and compute until training loss is minimized.
choices.explanation: A better fit to training data does not necessarily improve generalization to validation data.

source.label: Bedrockカスタムモデルのハイパーパラメーター

learning.reason: This uses validation data held out before publication to determine whether improvement continues, and can stop the run after a set number of rounds without improvement.
learning.concept: Early stopping is based on improvement on validation data, which is distinct from fit to training data.

title: Checking whether automated grading aligns with business reviewers
prompt: A company is introducing an LLM judge to evaluate the rationale for classifying contract clauses. It wants to confirm that a candidate judge can assess exception clauses according to internal standards and reduce manual work where appropriate. Which check is the most direct?

choices.text: Have the same judge score the same outputs several times, and consider it successful if the scores agree.
choices.explanation: This checks repeatability, but it will not reveal a judge that consistently scores incorrectly.

choices.text: Conclude that exception clauses are judged correctly if the two candidate judges have a high agreement rate.
choices.explanation: This measures agreement between models, but cannot reveal whether both have misunderstood the same business standard.

choices.text: Calculate how often the output's technical terms match those in a reference answer, and use that rate as the judge's validity measure.
choices.explanation: This measures terminology similarity, but not whether experts and the judge agree on how to interpret exception clauses.

choices.text: Have experts and the judge evaluate a held-out set containing both typical and exceptional cases using the same criteria, then compare their judgments, rationales, and patterns of disagreement.
choices.explanation: This shows how closely the judge aligns with human judgment in the target business task and where its scoring is weak.

source.label: モデルによる評価指標の検証

learning.reason: This shows how closely the judge aligns with human judgment in the target business task and where its scoring is weak.
learning.concept: Measure the repeatability of automated grading separately from its validity against business grading criteria.

title: When an evaluator tends to select answers from its own family
prompt: Compare two foundation models. Even when the answer order is reversed, the grading model favors the writing style of the same model family as itself. In human evaluation of test responses, there is no tendency for that writing style to be superior. Which approach can reduce the bias identified here while continuing automated evaluation?

choices.text: Choose an evaluator from a model family different from both candidates, and validate its agreement with human grading.
choices.explanation: This reduces the path through which the evaluator favors the same family as the candidates and allows the alternative to be assessed against human standards.

choices.text: Keep the current grading model and randomly determine only the answer order each time.
choices.explanation: This can distribute position effects, but it does not directly address the family preference that persists after the order is changed.

choices.text: Apply a uniform adjustment, determined by answer length, to the scores assigned by the current grading model.
choices.explanation: This could be considered for length bias, but there is no evidence that answer length is causing the issue in this case.

choices.text: Have each candidate model self-grade its own answer and compare only the scores.
choices.explanation: Scoring standards would differ by evaluator, and the relationship in which the evaluator and evaluated model are the same would remain.

source.label: 生成出力の品質評価と採点モデルの偏り

learning.reason: This reduces the path through which the evaluator favors the same family as the candidates and allows the alternative to be assessed against human standards.
learning.concept: Bias caused by answer position and bias in which an evaluator favors answers from its own family require different countermeasures.

sourceLabel: Quality evaluation of generated outputs and bias in grading models

title: Showing retrieved candidates in a review interface without generating an answer
prompt: A quality team is building a review interface for investigating policies. It wants to list excerpts from documents that may be relevant to a user's question, along with their sources and relevance scores, so reviewers can select primary sources. The team wants to use an existing Bedrock Knowledge Base without having a model generate a summary or answer. Which call is appropriate?

choices.text: Call an embedding model directly to vectorize the question, and display its response as a source list.
choices.explanation: This retrieves a numerical representation, but does not return Knowledge Base search results, document locations, or relevance scores.

choices.text: Call Retrieve and use the returned chunk content, location, and score in the list.
choices.explanation: This retrieves search results without a generation step, and the results include sources and relevance scores.

choices.text: Call RetrieveAndGenerate and hide the generated text in the interface, displaying only citations.
choices.explanation: Hiding the display does not prevent answer generation, and the citations cover only the material used for the answer.

choices.text: Use the document ingestion job to get a list of items to update and the number processed.
choices.explanation: This provides ingestion status, but does not return excerpts ranked for relevance to a question.

source.label: Knowledge Baseからの検索結果の取得

learning.reason: This retrieves search results without a generation step, and the results include sources and relevance scores.
learning.concept: Retrieval and generation in RAG are separate operations, and an interface can use retrieval alone.

sourceLabel: Retrieving search results from a Knowledge Base

title: Investigating prompt versions whose behavior changed despite identical wording
prompt: The quality of contract summaries changed after a prompt update. The template wording appears to be the same. Amazon Bedrock Prompt management retains the old and new versions. You want to check for changes to the model or inference settings and compare the answers from each version using the same document. What should you do?

choices.text: Duplicate the current draft into two variants and replace only one variant's variable with the old document.
choices.explanation: This tests a difference in inputs and does not check differences in the configurations of the two saved versions.

choices.text: Have business reviewers compare outputs generated by the old and new versions, then infer the inference settings from the writing style.
choices.explanation: This may reveal a quality difference, but output tendencies alone cannot identify which settings changed.

choices.text: Open the saved old and new versions in Compare to compare their definitions, then run both with the same test variables.
choices.explanation: This lets you examine the version definitions, including the template, alongside answers to the same input.

choices.text: Copy the template wording from both versions and run them in a playground with the same default settings.
choices.explanation: This compares the effect of the wording, but does not reproduce the model or settings specific to each saved version.

source.label: Bedrock Prompt managementの版比較

learning.reason: This lets you examine the version definitions, including the template, alongside answers to the same input.
learning.concept: Saved prompt versions include configuration beyond their instructions, and their behavior can be compared using the same input.

sourceLabel: Comparing Amazon Bedrock Prompt management versions

title: Required fields are missing at the end of long responses
prompt: A foundation model generates inspection reports. Long inputs fit within the model's input window, and omissions are concentrated at the end of the output. Every problematic response uses tokens up to the configured output limit, and the stop reason indicates that the length limit was reached. What should you consider first to preserve every report field?

choices.text: Keep the generation limit unchanged and use a configuration with a larger model input window.
choices.explanation: The input fits within the window, and the output limit is what was reached. Increasing only the input window does not address the cause.

choices.text: Keep the generation limit unchanged and cache the instructions at the beginning of the prompt.
choices.explanation: This may affect processing repeated input or its cost, but it does not increase the number of tokens the model can generate.

choices.text: Instruct the model to emit a report delimiter early and add it as a stop sequence.
choices.explanation: The delimiter can end generation, but it would stop a report earlier when you need its remaining fields.

choices.text: Raise the supported generation limit, then check required-field output and cost on the same report cases.
choices.explanation: This responds to the observed stop reason by allowing more generation, while letting you check quality and token cost.

source.label: Bedrockでのモデルの停止理由と生成上限

learning.reason: This responds to the observed stop reason by allowing more generation, while letting you check quality and token cost.
learning.concept: The number of tokens a model can accept as input and its maximum output length are separate constraints.

sourceLabel: Bedrock stop reasons and generation limits

title: Split procedure documents at topic changes
prompt: You are searching procedure documents with inconsistent formats in a custom Bedrock Knowledge Base. The current fixed-size chunking sometimes splits a topic in the middle and sometimes includes a short, separate topic in the same chunk. You want to use changes in meaning as chunk boundaries and also set a maximum chunk length. What should you try?

choices.text: Configure semantic chunking and specify the maximum number of tokens.
choices.explanation: This uses semantic groupings to chunk the content while keeping chunks within the configured maximum length.

choices.text: Keep fixed-size chunking and increase only the overlap with adjacent chunks.
choices.explanation: Some boundary content can appear in both chunks, but this does not determine boundaries based on topic changes.

choices.text: Use hierarchical parent-child chunking and always return the broader parent context when a child chunk matches.
choices.explanation: This provides more surrounding context, but it does not configure chunk boundaries based on changes in topic meaning.

choices.text: Disable chunking so that each document remains one unit.
choices.explanation: This avoids splitting a document, but does not meet the requirement to separate distinct topics within it and set a maximum length.

source.label: Knowledge Basesのチャンク分割方式

learning.reason: This uses semantic groupings to chunk the content while keeping chunks within the configured maximum length.
learning.concept: Semantic chunking and methods for returning a wider range of context around a search match are separate design choices.

title: Measure whether specialization harms a general-purpose task
prompt: Your organization uses one foundation model to generate equipment reports and summarize HR documents. You are considering switching to a model that has undergone supervised fine-tuning only for equipment reports. The existing HR summaries must not lose quality. How should you compare the models before deployment?

choices.text: Score the equipment training data again and treat a lower training loss as evidence that HR quality has been maintained.
choices.explanation: A measure of adaptation to equipment reports does not indicate quality on HR documents, which were outside the scope of fine-tuning.

choices.text: Score the original and fine-tuned models separately, under the same conditions, on both unseen equipment reports and HR documents.
choices.explanation: This lets you test improvement on the target task and any degradation in summaries outside the fine-tuning scope.

choices.text: Give HR documents to the original model and equipment reports to the fine-tuned model, then compare the scores across domains.
choices.explanation: Because the models receive different content, you cannot tell whether a score difference results from the model change.

choices.text: Combine cases from both domains and decide whether to switch based only on the overall average score.
choices.explanation: A large improvement on equipment reports could offset a decline in HR summaries and hide a violation of the quality requirement.

source.label: SageMaker AIで調整済みモデルと元モデルを比較する

learning.reason: This lets you test improvement on the target task and any degradation in summaries outside the fine-tuning scope.
learning.concept: When evaluating fine-tuning, measure adaptation to the target task separately from quality on existing tasks.

sourceLabel: Comparing fine-tuned and original models in SageMaker AI

title: Find unevaluated cases behind the average score
prompt: You evaluated two foundation models on the same 200 document summaries. One has a higher average score, but the number of responses shown is lower than for the other model. You want to identify inputs missing from the comparison and determine their effect on the evaluation, without filling in cases that received no response. What should you check first?

choices.text: Randomly select the same number of successful cases from each model and recalculate only the averages.
choices.explanation: This equalizes the counts, but still does not reveal which of the same inputs received no response.

choices.text: Raise the output limit only for the model with the higher average score and rerun the evaluation with different inputs.
choices.explanation: This does not identify which inputs were missing from the current comparison, and it changes the conditions for the two models.

choices.text: Compare the Amazon S3 details with the submitted inputs, identify cases without responses or with errors, and report the counts for each model.
choices.explanation: This can reveal whether the averages were calculated only from successful responses and shows the comparison's sample size for each model.

choices.text: Rank the models using their averages as they are, and assume the lower response count is unrelated to summary quality after inference.
choices.explanation: If responses are missing disproportionately for difficult inputs, the averages may not be comparable.

source.label: Bedrock自動評価の応答件数と出力結果

learning.reason: This can reveal whether the averages were calculated only from successful responses and shows the comparison's sample size for each model.
learning.concept: Review an automated evaluation's average scores together with coverage: which inputs received a response.

sourceLabel: Bedrock automatic evaluation response counts and outputs

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Referencing the Same Business Term Across Different Data Assets
prompt: You catalog data for AI in Amazon DataZone. You want to associate the approved definition of “Valid Order” with multiple data assets so users can refer to the same meaning. You do not want to modify or duplicate the source data. Which approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Copy the approved definition into a separate description field for each asset.
choices.explanation: This communicates the meaning, but each copy must be updated when the definition changes, so it does not provide one shared approved definition.

choices.text: Add a column representing the term to the source table and write the definition version into every row.
choices.explanation: This modifies the source data and does not provide a way to reference a common term definition in the catalog.

choices.text: Require users to enter the term definition in each access request and have the data asset owner review it for each request.
choices.explanation: The owner can review requests, but this does not manage the relationship between multiple catalog assets and a common definition.

choices.text: Register the term and its definition in a business glossary, then associate the same term with the target data assets.
choices.explanation: Multiple assets can then reference the same organizational definition.

source.label: Amazon DataZoneのビジネス用語集

learning.reason: Multiple assets can reference the same organizational definition.
learning.concept: When users need to reference shared vocabulary from catalog data assets, manage associations with terms instead of copying descriptions into each asset.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Using Governed Classification Tags Across Multiple Accounts
prompt: You have separate AWS accounts for AI training and inference environments. When tagging supported resources with data classifications, you want the organization to standardize the capitalization of existing keys and the allowlist of values. The purpose is to make the notation of attached tags consistent. Which option should you use?

choices.text: Define key capitalization and an allowlist of values in an AWS Organizations tag policy, and configure enforcement for supported resources.
choices.explanation: This lets the organization share tag standards and prevent noncompliant operations for supported resources.

choices.text: Activate the key as a cost allocation tag in AWS Billing and use it for monthly aggregation.
choices.explanation: This can classify costs, but it does not control the capitalization or permitted values of keys attached to resources.

choices.text: Create a Resource Group for each classification value and group resources whose existing tags match.
choices.explanation: This can group resources by their current tags, but it does not define a standard for new tag entries.

choices.text: Add an IAM access condition that uses the classification tag and restrict access to the group.
choices.explanation: This can authorize access based on existing tags, but it does not define tag notation or allowed values across the organization.

source.label: AWS Organizationsのタグポリシー

learning.reason: This lets the organization share tag standards and prevent noncompliant operations for supported resources.
learning.concept: Authorization and cost classification based on attached tags serve different purposes from standardizing the tags themselves.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Letting Teams Create Approved AI Environments Themselves
prompt: The AI team needs a standard environment for each project that includes a VPC, encrypted storage, and roles. The central administration team manages the versions of reviewed templates and launch permissions, while developers create environments themselves without administrator permissions. Which approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Distribute existing CloudFormation stacks to all teams and limit creation for each department to the central administration team.
choices.explanation: This can standardize configurations, but it does not meet the requirement for each team to provision environments as needed through self-service.

choices.text: Register reviewed templates as AWS Service Catalog products in a portfolio and grant the target teams permission to use them.
choices.explanation: The central team can manage product versions and users while enabling self-service with constraints such as a launch role.

choices.text: Share the templates in an internal Git repository and give each developer permission to create all of the configured resources directly.
choices.explanation: This shares templates, but developers are not limited to launching products defined from approved templates.

choices.text: Use AWS Config to detect configurations that do not match the standard environment and notify the central administration team.
choices.explanation: This can detect issues after creation, but it does not let target teams choose and launch a reviewed version.

source.label: AWS Service Catalogの概要

learning.reason: The central team can manage product versions and users while enabling self-service with constraints such as a launch role.
learning.concept: For self-service infrastructure provisioning, reviewed templates can be offered as products with approved launch permissions.

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Reviewing a Cloud Provider’s Audit Materials
prompt: You are adopting AWS AI services for a regulated business. You can already collect internal access logs. During adoption review, you want to determine whether candidate services and Regions are in scope by consulting third-party audit reports and contractual documents published by AWS. Which service should you consult first?

choices.text: Use AWS Config to record and export resource configurations in candidate Regions.
choices.explanation: This records customer-side settings and does not show the scope of the cloud provider’s audit materials.

choices.text: Inspect AWS Organizations activity and list the accounts that used the candidate services.
choices.explanation: Knowing which accounts used a service does not establish whether the service or Region is covered by an audit.

choices.text: Use AWS Artifact to obtain the relevant audit reports and contractual documents and check their scope.
choices.explanation: You can access AWS reports and agreements and check which services, among other things, are covered by a report.

choices.text: Start an assessment in AWS Audit Manager and collect evidence from your AWS accounts.
choices.explanation: This can collect evidence about controls in your own environment, but the goal here is to obtain third-party reports from AWS as the provider.

source.label: AWS Artifactのレポートと契約

learning.reason: You can access AWS reports and agreements and check which services, among other things, are covered by a report.
learning.concept: Distinguish the scope you can verify in provider audit materials from evidence of application controls that you collect yourself.

title: Improve recognition of a small set of product names in transcripts
prompt: Call transcripts are generally accurate, but the names of only five new products are replaced with common words. You can provide a list of the product names and their desired written forms, but you do not have a large collection of materials for teaching industry-wide context. Which change should you try first with Amazon Transcribe?

choices.text: After transcription, replace every commonly misrecognized word with a product name.
choices.explanation: This would also replace cases where that common word was actually spoken, and it would not improve recognition from the audio.

choices.text: Increase the maximum number of speakers for speaker separation and assign a separate label to the speaker associated with the incorrect word.
choices.explanation: This could improve speaker distinction, but it does not change the clues used to recognize a word as a product name.

choices.text: Define the product names as a custom vocabulary, specify the desired written forms, and apply it to the relevant job.
choices.explanation: This adds information to help recognize and render a limited set of proper nouns without requiring a large training corpus.

choices.text: Train a custom language model using only a list of product names so it learns word choices across entire utterances.
choices.explanation: A custom language model can suit broader industry-context learning, but with only a few names, a custom vocabulary is more direct.

source.label: Transcribeのカスタム語彙と言語モデル

learning.reason: This adds information to help recognize and render a limited set of proper nouns without requiring a large training corpus.
learning.concept: Choose between helping the system recognize and render a few words and learning language patterns across an industry based on the goal and amount of data.

sourceLabel: Transcribe custom vocabularies and language models

title: Keep a trademark in HTML unchanged
prompt: You are using Amazon Translate to translate HTML product descriptions into another language. The body text should be translated, but the registered trademark must remain exactly as it appears in the source string. You can modify the HTML before translation. Which feature should you use to exclude only the trademark from translation?

choices.text: Change the custom translation style to formal and stop product names from being translated.
choices.explanation: A style setting does not exclude a specific HTML element from translation.

choices.text: Set the do-not-translate attribute on the HTML element containing the trademark, then translate the HTML.
choices.explanation: This excludes the trademark from translation while allowing the surrounding text to be translated.

choices.text: Add the same string to a custom terminology list and assume it will always pass through unchanged in every context.
choices.explanation: A terminology list guides word choice; it does not guarantee an exact match in every context.

choices.text: Wrap the trademark in a bold HTML element and assume content inside emphasis elements is not translated.
choices.explanation: Bold formatting only specifies emphasis; it does not suppress translation.

source.label: Amazon Translateの翻訳対象外タグ

learning.reason: This excludes the trademark from translation while allowing the surrounding text to be translated.
learning.concept: Recommending a translation and specifying that part of HTML must not be translated are separate features.

sourceLabel: Amazon Translate tags for content not to translate

title: Extract line items with standard fields from receipts in different formats
prompt: Extract the merchant name, total amount, tax amount, and the products and quantities on purchase line items from receipt images. The receipts have different layouts at different stores. You want to use standard receipt-specific fields without configuring positions or border coordinates for each store. Which operation should you call?

choices.text: Use Amazon Textract AnalyzeExpense to retrieve summary fields and line items.
choices.explanation: It returns standardized receipt attributes and line-item details in the same analysis result.

choices.text: Use Amazon Textract DetectDocumentText and pass through every text line as is.
choices.explanation: It can read the text, but it does not classify types of amounts and purchase items into standard fields.

choices.text: Use Amazon Textract AnalyzeDocument to extract only tables, and always treat the top-left table cell as the merchant name.
choices.explanation: This can retrieve table structure, but the receipts do not guarantee that merchant names and totals appear at the same coordinates across different layouts.

choices.text: Use an Amazon Textract query to ask only for the total, then reconstruct the other payment fields and line items from that value.
choices.explanation: An individual question can retrieve a value, but the total alone does not reveal the tax amount or quantities for each line item.

source.label: Textractの領収書・請求書応答

learning.reason: It returns standardized receipt attributes and line-item details in the same analysis result.
learning.concept: Reading text with OCR is different from extracting fields and line items with receipt-specific meaning.

title: Route detailed moderation labels to the same reviewer
prompt: You assign Amazon Rekognition moderation labels to posted images. The review team wants to retain details for individual labels, but route cases by grouping them at one level above in the AWS label hierarchy. What should you use to classify the labels without inferring a category from their names?

choices.text: Route labels with the same confidence level to the same reviewer.
choices.explanation: Confidence indicates how certain a detection is; it does not represent parent-child relationships in the label hierarchy.

choices.text: Truncate the string of a specific label to its first word and treat that string as the parent label.
choices.explanation: There is no contract that label names use structured prefixes to specify categories, so this cannot accurately reproduce the hierarchy.

choices.text: Save only the first label returned and use its name as the parent category for every candidate.
choices.explanation: If the results contain multiple distinct categories, this loses each label's actual parent.

choices.text: Save the returned label name and parent-label information, and route the case to the reviewer for the corresponding parent label.
choices.explanation: This preserves the detailed label while allowing you to use the higher-level category included in the detection result.

source.label: Rekognitionのモデレーションラベル情報

learning.reason: This preserves the detailed label while allowing you to use the higher-level category included in the detection result.
learning.concept: When using moderation labels, distinguish confidence scores from parent-child relationships in the label hierarchy.

title: Share a consistent pronunciation for proper nouns across announcements
prompt: A department uses Amazon Polly to read hundreds of announcements. The pronunciation of proper nouns must be consistent. The content and punctuation of each announcement have already been approved, so you want to manage pronunciations in one place without editing each announcement. What should you use?

choices.text: Set the same speech rate for every announcement.
choices.explanation: You can adjust the speaking rate, but it does not specify how proper nouns are pronounced.

choices.text: Switch all announcements to a different voice and replace any mispronounced words in the text.
choices.explanation: Using the same voice does not create a pronunciation dictionary, and this approach still requires changes to the announcement text.

choices.text: Define the proper nouns and their pronunciations in a pronunciation lexicon, then specify the same lexicon in the corresponding synthesis requests.
choices.explanation: Many read-aloud requests can refer to one lexicon, so the announcement text does not need to be edited.

choices.text: Embed a pronunciation for each proper noun in the SSML for every announcement and maintain the same information in each file.
choices.explanation: This can specify a pronunciation, but it does not meet the requirement to maintain the pronunciation settings in one shared lexicon.

source.label: Amazon Pollyの発音辞書

learning.reason: Many read-aloud requests can refer to one lexicon, so the announcement text does not need to be edited.
learning.concept: A one-time pronunciation specification and pronunciation management reused across multiple synthesis requests serve different needs.

title: Mask personal information that does not follow a fixed format before sharing
prompt: A team uses English customer inquiry emails to study product trends. The content of each inquiry should be retained, but names, addresses, and phone numbers mixed into free-form text must be masked before the research team reads it. The team wants to avoid removing every proper noun commonly used in the industry. Which analysis should it use?

choices.text: Use Amazon Comprehend to classify sentiment and withhold only emails classified as negative.
choices.explanation: Personal information can appear regardless of sentiment. Control based on the type of information is needed.

choices.text: Use Amazon Comprehend PII detection to find specified types of personal information and mask the matching spans.
choices.explanation: This can process the selected types of personal information while preserving the general meaning of the text.

choices.text: Use Amazon Comprehend general entity detection and remove all entities, including names and locations.
choices.explanation: This would also remove ordinary organization names and place names, and it would not ensure that every phone number, for example, is treated as personal information.

choices.text: Use Amazon Comprehend to extract key phrases and share only the beginning of the text.
choices.explanation: The shortened text could still contain personal information, so this does not mask it before sharing.

source.label: Comprehendの個人情報検出とマスキング

learning.reason: This can process the selected types of personal information while preserving the general meaning of the text.
learning.concept: Before sharing free-form text, distinguish general entities from personal information that must be protected.

title: Ask again for a date that is valid in format but unavailable for booking
prompt: You are collecting a booking date with Amazon Lex V2. The date format can be recognized, but users may also enter dates in the past or department-specific closure dates. If the date is invalid, do not invoke the booking process; ask for the date again. Which design is appropriate?

choices.text: Validate the date slot against business rules in a dialog Lambda function and elicit the slot again if it is invalid.
choices.explanation: This applies business rules even to a date that is syntactically valid, so booking can occur only after the input passes validation.

choices.text: Switch to a built-in date slot and treat successful recognition alone as proof that the date is valid for booking.
choices.explanation: A date may be interpreted successfully even if it falls on a department-specific closure date.

choices.text: Add more user utterance examples for the booking date and use only the intent recognition score to determine whether it is valid.
choices.explanation: This may provide more information for recognizing the booking intent, but it does not ensure that the collected date is valid.

choices.text: Run the booking process once all slots are filled, then tell the user in the completion message to choose a different date.
choices.explanation: This does not stop an invalid value before the booking is made.

source.label: Lex V2のスロットの検証

learning.reason: This applies business rules even to a date that is syntactically valid, so booking can occur only after the input passes validation.
learning.concept: Recognizing a slot value and confirming that it is valid for a business operation are separate checks.

title: Select relevant tools without sending all tool definitions every time
prompt: A support assistant can use about 120 MCP tools registered with AgentCore Gateway. Only a few capabilities are relevant to an individual request, but including every definition in the input each time leaves less context available for the response. How can you narrow the definitions sent to the model while preserving the configured authorization?

choices.text: Always send only the tool used previously, and do not search for candidates when the inquiry changes.
choices.explanation: This shortens the input, but the assistant cannot use a needed operation when the user's request changes.

choices.text: Pass the user's request to Gateway tool search and send only the definitions for relevant candidates to the model.
choices.explanation: This keeps the set of executable tools available while reducing the definitions included in the input for each request.

choices.text: Include all tool definitions in a cached prompt each time to make the tool-selection process faster.
choices.explanation: This may reduce the overhead of repeated processing, but it does not change the length of all definitions visible to the model at inference time.

choices.text: Lower the maximum response token count while sending the same-length tool list in the input.
choices.explanation: This only reduces the space available for the response; it does not narrow the input tool list.

source.label: AgentCore Gatewayのツールのセマンティック検索

learning.reason: This keeps the set of executable tools available while reducing the definitions included in the input for each request.
learning.concept: Authorization for tools and selection of the candidates shown to the model for each task are separate concerns.

sourceLabel: Semantic search for tools in AgentCore Gateway

title: Find requests that independent assistants can handle
prompt: Two departments operate independent agents. They want to do more than call a single function between departments: they need to discover programmatically what work the other agent can handle and hand off work using an existing standard messaging protocol. The other agent supports A2A. Which design is appropriate?

choices.text: Use an Agent Card to discover the other agent’s capabilities, then request work through A2A messages.
choices.explanation: This uses a mechanism for publishing and discovering agent capabilities and a communication contract for agents.

choices.text: Add the other agent’s specification to a knowledge base and generate response text on its behalf.
choices.explanation: The specification can be searched, but the other agent does not execute its own processing.

choices.text: Save the other agent’s decisions in conversational memory and infer the next request from past results.
choices.explanation: Past results can be referenced, but this does not discover or invoke work the other agent currently offers.

choices.text: Combine both departments’ execution environments into one function and hard-code the other agent’s capabilities in both.
choices.explanation: A fixed implementation can be called, but it does not meet the requirement for independent agents to publish and discover capabilities through a standard contract.

source.label: AgentCore RuntimeでA2Aサーバーを動かす

learning.reason: This uses a mechanism for publishing and discovering agent capabilities and a communication contract for agents.
learning.concept: A2A supports publishing and discovering agent capabilities and exchanging messages between agents.

sourceLabel: Run an A2A server with AgentCore Runtime

title: Run two independent estimates at the same time
prompt: A procurement assistant asks separate specialists for shipping and packaging estimates based on the same product list. Neither specialist uses the other’s result, but both results are required for the final total. In what order should the work run to reduce wait time without producing duplicate estimates?

choices.text: Finish whichever estimate is faster first, then run the slower one and calculate the total.
choices.explanation: This produces the correct result, but the wait times for independent tasks are added together because they run sequentially.

choices.text: Ask both specialists for the same shipping estimate and use whichever result finishes first.
choices.explanation: Even if speculative execution reduces latency, it does not provide the required packaging estimate.

choices.text: Present a total using only whichever estimate finishes first, and save the other one to a log.
choices.explanation: The first response arrives sooner, but one of the estimates required for the total is missing from the amount shown to the user.

choices.text: Start the shipping and packaging estimates at the same time, wait for both results, and then calculate the total.
choices.explanation: This overlaps independent tasks and ensures both required results are available before calculating the total.

source.label: エージェントの処理順と並列実行

learning.reason: This overlaps independent tasks and ensures both required results are available before calculating the total.
learning.concept: Run independent tasks in parallel, then gather their results immediately before the dependent aggregation step.

sourceLabel: Agent task sequencing and parallel execution

title: Preserve recent details and earlier decisions in a long conversation
prompt: In a travel-planning conversation, you want to retain recent, specific constraints as they were stated while also remembering the budget decided at the start. As the conversation grows, sending the full text of every past turn is causing input-limit and cost problems. How should the context be assembled?

choices.text: Send only a fixed number of recent turns and discard decisions from older turns each time.
choices.explanation: Recent details are retained, but constraints decided earlier are lost.

choices.text: Keep the full history and shorten the current question each time before adding it.
choices.explanation: This may save a little space, but it does not limit the growing volume of old history.

choices.text: Replace older turns with a summary of decisions and include a fixed number of the most recent turns verbatim.
choices.explanation: This retains older decisions such as the budget while preserving the details needed from recent exchanges.

choices.text: Keep only the first few turns verbatim and delete all other conversation except the current question.
choices.explanation: The initial budget remains, but information needed to interpret a question in light of recent conversation is missing.

source.label: 文脈ウィンドウと履歴の最適化

learning.reason: This retains older decisions such as the budget while preserving the details needed from recent exchanges.
learning.concept: The input space used for conversation history can be managed by combining summaries of older information with the verbatim recent conversation.

title: Record only the audio guidance actually delivered at a service desk
prompt: Amazon Nova 2 Sonic is used for voice guidance. If a user starts speaking mid-response, the latter part of the text prepared by the model is not spoken. The interaction record must contain what the model actually said, not the text it planned to say. Which output should be used?

choices.text: Record the assistant’s initial provisional text unchanged, even after audio output.
choices.explanation: It can include planned text, so the record may contain a later portion that was never spoken.

choices.text: Retrieve the speech-recognition result for the user’s audio and record it as the assistant’s response.
choices.explanation: This records what the user said, not the response spoken by the assistant.

choices.text: Join the assistant’s tool calls and responses, and use that string as the record of the voice guidance.
choices.explanation: This can show what information was consulted, but it does not indicate how much was spoken aloud.

choices.text: Record the transcript of the audio sent as the assistant’s FINAL output.
choices.explanation: The final transcript corresponds to the response actually spoken, including when playback is interrupted.

source.label: Nova 2 Sonicの出力イベント

learning.reason: The final transcript corresponds to the response actually spoken, including when playback is interrupted.
learning.concept: Use planned text and the final audio transcript for different purposes.

title: Track video analysis requests through completion
prompt: A training department uses Amazon Bedrock Data Automation to analyze recordings in S3. Even after closing the screen, staff must be able to check the status of the same request later and retrieve its analysis results. What should be recorded when the request is accepted and then used to prevent duplicate processing?

choices.text: Save the S3 key of the input file, and start a new analysis and look for the results each time the screen is opened.
choices.explanation: The S3 key identifies the input, but it does not associate it with an execution that has already started, so this can cause duplicate processing.

choices.text: Treat the request as complete as soon as the start API succeeds, and read the expected results without checking the status.
choices.explanation: For an asynchronous process, successful acceptance does not mean the analysis is complete. Check separately whether results were generated or the process failed.

choices.text: Save the invocation ARN returned upon acceptance and associate it with the request, then use that ARN to check the status and output location.
choices.explanation: This identifies the individual asynchronous execution and lets you track its results, so reopening the screen does not require starting another analysis.

choices.text: Save only the destination bucket name and always display the latest results in that bucket.
choices.explanation: When multiple videos are processed, this cannot distinguish one request's results from another's.

source.label: Data Automationの非同期呼び出し

learning.reason: This identifies the individual asynchronous execution and lets you track its results, so reopening the screen does not require starting another analysis.
learning.concept: To associate an asynchronous request with its output, retain an identifier for the execution itself, not just the file.

title: Account for costs during periods with no exam usage
prompt: The prototype used an on-demand model in Bedrock. Another candidate is selected from Bedrock Marketplace and deployed to a dedicated SageMaker AI instance. The endpoint remains running even during periods when evaluators hardly use it. How should you compare the costs?

choices.text: Even if the dedicated endpoint exists, count instance runtime only for the time users have the screen open.
choices.explanation: The period when the endpoint is retained does not necessarily match the period when users interact with it.

choices.text: In addition to the listed model's pricing terms, account for the cost of the selected SageMaker AI instance type and number of instances, as well as their runtime.
choices.explanation: This comparison accounts for a configuration where Marketplace usage terms and the deployment infrastructure incur separate costs.

choices.text: For both models, calculate the cost in the same way using only the per-token prices for input and output.
choices.explanation: This overlooks the cost of running the dedicated instance.

choices.text: Compare only the Marketplace listed price and treat the deployment instance as included in that price.
choices.explanation: SageMaker AI infrastructure costs apply in addition to the listed model pricing.

source.label: Bedrock Marketplaceのサブスクリプションと基盤費用

learning.reason: This comparison accounts for a configuration where Marketplace usage terms and the deployment infrastructure incur separate costs.
learning.concept: Estimate model inference charges separately from the cost of the compute capacity that hosts the model.

sourceLabel: Bedrock Marketplace subscription and infrastructure costs

title: Provide task-specific information to the same model
prompt: A single model is used to draft short customer notices and internal operating procedures. With shared input that combines both tasks, internal terminology that customers do not need becomes more prominent in customer notices, while internal procedures lack specific reference information. How can this be improved without retraining the model?

choices.text: Set a lower temperature for customer notices, but use the same instructions and references as for internal procedures.
choices.explanation: This may reduce output variability, but it does not change the scope of the information being referenced.

choices.text: Choose reference materials, instructions, and examples for each use case, and assemble only the context needed for that request.
choices.explanation: Even with the same model, the input can reflect each task's distinct purpose and materials.

choices.text: Attach the same set of materials every time, and reduce the maximum output tokens only for customer notices.
choices.explanation: Shorter output does not make the input terminology and references appropriate for each use case.

choices.text: Keep the shared input fixed and increase the number of search results for every document.
choices.explanation: Providing more candidates does not ensure that only the materials needed for each task are supplied.

source.label: 生成AIのコンテキストエンジニアリング

learning.reason: Even with the same model, the input can reflect each task's distinct purpose and materials.
learning.concept: Context design starts by dynamically selecting reference materials, instructions, and examples suited to the task.

title: Carry a rough sketch's composition into the finished image
prompt: A communications team is creating illustration concepts for an exhibition hall based on a floor plan. A hand-drawn sketch shows the positions and outlines of objects, while text specifies the finished image's texture and lighting. The goal is not to expand beyond the sketch. Which generation method is appropriate?

choices.text: Provide the sketch and descriptive text to an image generation feature that uses the sketch as a structural guide.
choices.explanation: The feature can use the drawing's shapes as a guide while following the text instructions for texture and lighting.

choices.text: Use only style reference to extract colors and brushwork from a reference image, without supplying the sketch's composition.
choices.explanation: This can create visual consistency, but it does not provide input to preserve the positions and outlines of objects.

choices.text: Use outpainting to extend the sketch's edges, without editing what is inside the existing lines.
choices.explanation: This suits expanding an area, but does not turn the sketch's content into a finished illustration.

choices.text: Remove the sketch's background to make it transparent, and use that transparent image as the finished product.
choices.explanation: Removing the background does not generate a finished image with the specified lighting and texture.

source.label: Stable ImageのSketch制御

learning.reason: The feature can use the drawing's shapes as a guide while following the text instructions for texture and lighting.
learning.concept: When using image references, distinguish constraints on composition from references to style, such as colors and brushwork.

title: Apply the Same Transformation to Multiple Java Repositories
prompt: A development team is migrating multiple Java applications to the same target JDK. They do not need to migrate an intermediary service or virtual machines; they want to update the code and libraries using the same transformation definition and review the results. Which option uses an AWS-managed transformation definition?

choices.text: Use AWS Transform for server migration and assume that duplicating the runtime environment will also rewrite the code for the new JDK.
choices.explanation: Migrating a deployment target is separate from updating source code and dependency libraries for a new runtime.

choices.text: Change only the JDK used by the build environment and leave code changes that break compatibility unaddressed.
choices.explanation: This can help verify behavior, but it does not meet the requirement to use a managed transformation to address errors and update dependencies.

choices.text: Get suggestions for code snippets from an IDE chat for each repository without sharing a project-wide transformation definition.
choices.explanation: This can help with individual changes, but it does not apply the same managed transformation across multiple repositories.

choices.text: Use the AWS Transform custom managed transformation for Java runtime updates.
choices.explanation: It provides a reusable transformation that targets JDK updates and related dependency changes.

source.label: AWS Transformの管理済み変換

learning.reason: A reusable transformation targets JDK updates and related dependency changes.
learning.concept: When the migration concerns application code and dependency libraries, choose code modernization rather than host migration.

title: Understand Console Resources and Costs
prompt: An operator is in the AWS Management Console. They want to ask natural-language questions about AWS resources and costs within their permissions, and understand the meaning of common errors shown in the console. They do not want to build a customer-facing chat application or an internal document index. Which option is appropriate?

choices.text: Connect AWS Quick to a custom dataset, build a new cost dashboard, and then ask questions.
choices.explanation: It can explain ingested metrics, but this does not meet the requirement to handle console resources and errors without building a new solution.

choices.text: Develop an organization-specific assistant and tools for billing data with Bedrock.
choices.explanation: This could provide the required features, but it does not meet the condition of not setting up a new chat application or data connection.

choices.text: Use AWS assistant to ask questions in the console about AWS resources, costs, and displayed errors.
