choices.explanation: It can provide guidance using console context and the permissions already granted.

choices.text: Use only AWS Cost Explorer to review costs, then diagnose general console errors from the cost charts in the same view.
choices.explanation: It is suitable for cost analysis, but does not provide natural-language guidance about general errors or resource operations.

source.label: AWS assistantのコンソール支援

learning.reason: It can provide guidance using console context and the permissions already granted.
learning.concept: Built-in console assistance and a dedicated assistant built by ingesting business data have different setup requirements.

title: Suggest Responses to an Agent During a Call
prompt: A contact center wants to identify the intent of customer calls and chats during the conversation and quickly show agents suggested responses, next steps, and relevant materials. Agents continue the call while selecting the guidance to relay to the customer. Which architecture is appropriate?

choices.text: A self-service bot that uses only fixed utterances in Amazon Lex
choices.explanation: It can support a self-service conversation flow, but it does not meet the requirement to provide agents with real-time generative AI suggestions.

choices.text: Real-time agent assistance with Amazon Q in Connect
choices.explanation: Correct. Amazon Q in Connect detects intent during calls and chats and provides agents with generated responses, suggested actions, and relevant materials.

choices.text: Search an internal portal with Amazon Q Business
choices.explanation: It can help search internal content, but it does not provide real-time suggestions to agents based on contact center conversations.

choices.text: Use Amazon Transcribe only to transcribe calls
choices.explanation: Transcription is available, but the requirement to show agents suggested responses and next actions remains unmet.

source.label: Create an agent assist intent from a Connect Customer instance

learning.reason: Amazon Q in Connect provides real-time generative AI assistance to agents by understanding conversations and helping resolve them.
learning.concept: Even within the same customer support domain, self-service automation and assistance for human agents are distinct use cases.

sourceLabel: Create an agent assist intent from a Connect Customer instance

title: Ingest Contracts with No Standard Fields in a Defined Format
prompt: Extract “renewal notice deadline” and “department permitted to grant an exception” from contracts. The format varies by contract, and the values appear in different sections of the text. You want the Bedrock Data Automation output to include two defined keys. Which setting should you choose?

choices.text: Use a blueprint that defines the two business fields for custom output.
choices.explanation: This lets you specify nonstandard business fields and return the extraction results in the defined structure.

choices.text: Enable the standard document summary and assume that the two values will always appear in the first two lines of the summary.
choices.explanation: A summary can be generated, but it does not guarantee a result with the required fields.

choices.text: Get OCR for the entire page from the standard output and rename only the keys in that output.
choices.explanation: Renaming keys in page-level text recognition results does not identify the target values in their respective sections.

choices.text: Leave the field names out of the blueprint and have the output keys generated anew from each contract as it is processed.
choices.explanation: This may adapt to each input, but it does not guarantee the two fixed keys expected by downstream consumers.

source.label: Bedrock Data Automationの標準出力とカスタム出力

learning.reason: This lets you specify nonstandard business fields and return the extraction results in the defined structure.
learning.concept: Use generic extraction or summaries for the fields they return, and define custom business fields when the consuming system requires them.

sourceLabel: Bedrock Data Automation Standard and Custom Outputs

title: Use only the results needed from standard video output
prompt: A training video processing project needs to pass only a summary of the entire video downstream. Cut-level details and scene-level output are not needed. Which configuration uses Bedrock Data Automation while reducing the effort of post-processing every output each time?

choices.text: Enable all video outputs and discard the results that are not needed each time in post-processing.
choices.explanation: This provides a summary, but still requires a step to handle and remove unneeded outputs.

choices.text: Define “summary” in a custom document blueprint and disable standard video output.
choices.explanation: Business-field extraction from documents and the output configuration for understanding and summarizing an entire video are different.

choices.text: Enable only cut-level detail output and treat the description of the first cut as a summary of the entire video.
choices.explanation: A description of one part of the video does not include what happens afterward.

choices.text: Configure a summary of the entire video in standard video output and disable the other options that are not needed.
choices.explanation: Selecting the needed summary reduces the effort of filtering out extra output in downstream processing.

source.label: Bedrock Data Automationのプロジェクト設定

learning.reason: Selecting the needed summary reduces the effort of filtering out extra output in downstream processing.
learning.concept: Choose outputs to match the modality and use case, without adding work to process unneeded supplementary information.

title: Choose the right-sized model for short-text classification
prompt: The same classification task was evaluated with Amazon Nova Micro, Lite, and Pro. All three met the accuracy requirement for classifying short Japanese text. Inputs and outputs are text only, and the next step prioritizes low latency and price among the candidates. Additional modalities and complex reasoning are not needed. Which candidate should be preferred?

choices.text: Use Amazon Nova Pro, designed for more complex tasks, for every input and disregard any accuracy difference.
choices.explanation: Spending more on difficult tasks can be appropriate, but here all candidates meet the required accuracy and cost and latency are the priorities.

choices.text: Send every input to all three models and use the result once at least two return the same classification.
choices.explanation: This adds redundancy to predictions, but a single model already meets the quality requirement, and this approach increases input and processing.

choices.text: Prefer Amazon Nova Micro, which is optimized for text-only workloads, speed, and low cost.
choices.explanation: Its required quality has been confirmed, and it fits the goal of reducing latency and cost without needing additional modalities.

choices.text: Prefer Amazon Nova Lite, which can also accept images and video, and switch to it because of the unused modalities.
choices.explanation: It could be a candidate if additional modalities were needed, but this selection does not use that capability.

source.label: Amazon Novaのモデルの比較

learning.reason: Its required quality has been confirmed, and it fits the goal of reducing latency and cost without needing additional modalities.
learning.concept: When all candidates meet the minimum quality threshold, choose based on latency and cost for the actual requirements.

title: Add per-chunk applicability metadata to a single manual
prompt: Repair procedures with different applicability conditions for each model appear in separate sections of one PDF. The existing parsing and chunking in Bedrock Knowledge Bases correctly ingest the content. You want to filter by the applicable model for each section at retrieval time, without splitting the PDF again. Where should you add the model information?

choices.text: In a post-chunking Lambda transformation for the data source, add the applicable model for each body section as metadata on its chunk.
choices.explanation: This retains the existing chunking while allowing chunks from the same PDF to have different retrieval attributes.

choices.text: Place a document-level metadata file alongside the PDF and list all models in an array.
choices.explanation: This identifies the models covered by the document, but does not preserve the mapping between a specific chunk and its model.

choices.text: Add the user's model to the generation prompt and do not set a model condition during retrieval.
choices.explanation: This tells generation which model applies, but does not meet the requirement to select only chunks for that model during retrieval.

choices.text: Increase the number of retrieval results and combine results belonging to the same document.
choices.explanation: This broadens retrieval but does not make section-level model attributes available to retrieval.

source.label: Knowledge Basesのカスタム取り込み変換

learning.reason: This retains the existing chunking while allowing chunks from the same PDF to have different retrieval attributes.
learning.concept: Set metadata at the document or chunk level according to the granularity at which the condition varies.

title: Ask the user for a missing required value
prompt: An existing user contacts an Amazon Bedrock Agents Classic agent about a delivery. The lookup function requires a unique tracking number, but the user may provide only a destination address. The system has no function for identifying a tracking number from an address. How should the agent ask a follow-up question only when the number is unknown?

choices.text: Configure the lookup action to omit the tracking number and send only the destination address for every lookup.
choices.explanation: The required data cannot be looked up because no function can derive a number from the destination address.

choices.text: Enable only confirmation before execution for the lookup action and make the tracking number optional.
choices.explanation: This can show the user what will be confirmed, but it is not designed to collect a missing required parameter.

choices.text: Store the tracking number from the previous inquiry in long-term memory and reuse it when none is provided.
choices.explanation: There is no basis for assuming that the previous tracking number belongs to this delivery, so the correct item cannot be looked up reliably.

choices.text: Configure an AMAZON.UserInput action group separately from the lookup action group, which requires the tracking number.
choices.explanation: The normal lookup receives the required value, and a separately configured user-input action group can ask for it when it is missing.

source.label: Bedrock Agentsのユーザーへの追加質問

learning.reason: When a required value is missing, the agent can ask for it and perform the lookup after receiving it.
learning.concept: Collecting a required value for a tool and confirming whether an operation may proceed with collected values are separate mechanisms.

title: Learning editors’ preferences from multiple good answers
prompt: A foundation model is used for internal writing assistance, and several drafts can be valid responses to the same request. Editors can compare two drafts and repeatedly choose the one that best balances politeness and concision. What format should you collect for model tuning based on human preferences?

choices.text: Store only the character count of the selected draft and rate every shorter answer more highly.
choices.explanation: This captures only one aspect of concision and does not represent the editor’s judgment about politeness.

choices.text: Record two drafts for different requests and always prefer the draft edited most recently.
choices.explanation: The requests differ, and editing order is confounded with preference, so the responses cannot be compared for the same input.

choices.text: Store the selected and unselected drafts together with the request they answer.
choices.explanation: This captures a relative preference for the same input and lets human judgment guide training without assuming there is only one correct wording.

choices.text: Keep only the adopted draft paired with the request, and discard the alternative that was compared.
choices.explanation: This can provide a supervised training example, but it loses the preference information about which of the two drafts was chosen.

source.label: AWSの生成AIライフサイクルにおける選好データ

learning.reason: This allows relative preferences for the same input to be compared and uses human judgment without assuming there is only one correct wording.
learning.concept: Preference data preserves evaluations of candidate responses to the same input.

sourceLabel: Preference data in the AWS generative AI lifecycle

title: Exclude unapproved text from logs used for distillation
prompt: You are preparing to distill a high-performance model into a smaller model. Bedrock inference logs contain approved guidance and experimental text, and request metadata distinguishes them. The teacher is the same model that produced the logs. How can you use previously approved responses with their corresponding inputs without recreating those responses?

choices.text: Replace the teacher responses in the production logs with student responses, and keep all logged inputs.
choices.explanation: This does not serve the purpose of transferring the established teacher behavior, and it mixes in experimental tasks that were not approved.

choices.text: Filter the inference logs by metadata and configure the job to read the approved input and existing response pairs.
choices.explanation: When the log-producing model is also the teacher, the job can use the inputs and responses that pass the filter without generating the responses again.

choices.text: Use all logs, then exclude only evaluation cases that produce unapproved text after training.
choices.explanation: Excluding cases from scoring does not remove the effects of training on undesirable responses.

choices.text: Pass the approved requests as inputs only and do not use their existing responses.
choices.explanation: This could be used to have the teacher generate new responses, but it does not reuse the specific responses that were already approved.

source.label: Bedrockモデル蒸留の推論ログと既存応答

learning.reason: You can select which tasks and outputs remain in the training examples, avoiding unintentionally passing along an experimental, undesirable style.
learning.concept: Distillation involves choosing not only the teacher model, but also the tasks and reference outputs you want it to reproduce.

sourceLabel: Bedrock inference logs and existing responses for model distillation

title: The same input times out only with a first-use schema
prompt: An order-confirmation system uses Bedrock structured outputs. Only the first request after a JSON Schema update reaches the existing timeout; subsequent requests with the same schema and input succeed quickly. How can you reduce latency immediately after release while continuing to produce schema-conforming output in production?

choices.text: Before release, send a test request using the schema that will be used, and configure the system to allow for the initial compilation time when no cache is available.
choices.explanation: The first request can be slower because the schema grammar needs to be prepared. You can plan for this initial processing while keeping the existing configuration.

choices.text: Change the schema values or shape on every request and validate the new structures concurrently.
choices.explanation: This creates more schemas and makes it harder to reuse the compiled result for the same schema.

choices.text: Cache only the prompt text and generate a different schema name and field definition for every request.
choices.explanation: Reusing text is different from reusing the grammar for structured output.

choices.text: Stop using schemas and put output examples in the prompt instead.
choices.explanation: This avoids compilation, but does not meet the requirement to maintain schema-conforming output.

source.label: Bedrockの構造化出力とスキーマの初回処理

learning.reason: The first request can be slower because the schema grammar needs to be prepared. You can plan for this initial processing while keeping the existing configuration.
learning.concept: When assessing initial latency for structured output, distinguish first-time schema compilation from the time taken by subsequent inference.

sourceLabel: Bedrock structured outputs and first-time schema processing

title: Measure retrieval quality while reducing vector storage
prompt: A department evaluated product-document retrieval using Titan Text Embeddings V2 with 1,024 dimensions. As the document count grows, the department wants to limit vector storage. Which approach can keep all products searchable and allow it to reassess whether critical retrieval misses increase?

choices.text: Change only query embeddings to 256 dimensions and search the 1,024-dimensional document index.
choices.explanation: This does not change storage requirements, and vectors with different dimensions cannot be searched against the same index.

choices.text: Keep the current dimensions and reduce the number of results returned per search from 10 to 3.
choices.explanation: This reduces the amount returned per request but does not change the size of vectors stored in the full index.

choices.text: Truncate each 1,024-dimensional output to its first 256 values after generation, and skip quality checks.
choices.explanation: Simple truncation is not the same as configuring the model to return a supported output dimension, and it provides no way to assess quality.

choices.text: Specify a lower supported dimension, create an index using embeddings at that dimension for both documents and queries, and measure recall with representative queries.
choices.explanation: This reduces storage per vector. The effect on retrieval quality can be measured using the target data.

source.label: Titan Text Embeddings V2の出力次元

learning.reason: This reduces storage per vector. The effect on retrieval quality can be measured using the target data.
learning.concept: Embedding dimensions affect storage and representational capacity; acceptable retrieval quality should be measured on real data.

sourceLabel: Titan Text Embeddings V2 output dimensions

title: Show the correct manual page using existing retrieval metadata
prompt: An existing custom Bedrock Knowledge Base uses OpenSearch Serverless and splits PDFs into chunks. When displaying search results, you want to show the source PDF and page number. Which approach does this without re-ingesting the content or asking the model to guess the number during generation?

choices.text: Have the LLM read the retrieved chunk and infer the page number from its wording and document structure.
choices.explanation: The page number may not be uniquely identifiable from the text alone, so this cannot reliably direct users to the exact page.

choices.text: Divide the estimated number of tokens preceding the returned fragment by the average page length and display the result.
choices.explanation: Page length varies with the amount of text, tables, and images, so this is not a substitute for the actual recorded page number.

choices.text: Use the retrieved result's file location and the document page-number metadata generated by Bedrock.
choices.explanation: In a configuration that splits PDFs and uses OpenSearch Serverless, the page can be obtained from x-amz-bedrock-kb-document-page-number.

choices.text: Display the result's retrieval rank as the page number.
choices.explanation: Search results ranked by relevance do not necessarily follow the PDF's page order.

source.label: Knowledge Basesの検索結果のメタデータ

learning.reason: In the supported configuration, retrieved PDF results include page numbers, so the source location can be shown without rebuilding the Knowledge Base.
learning.concept: Use location metadata from the retrieved source to show evidence, rather than relying on retrieval rank or generated descriptions.

sourceLabel: Metadata in Knowledge Bases search results

title: Route requests directly when one specialist is enough
prompt: An existing Bedrock Agents Classic setup has an inventory specialist and a returns specialist. Every inquiry can be handled end to end by exactly one of them, and there is no need to combine information from multiple collaborators into an answer. Which design keeps a shared entry point while letting the selected specialist return the final answer?

choices.text: Put examples of the existing specialists' outputs in a supervisor agent's prompt and have the supervisor always answer.
choices.explanation: This simplifies the setup, but it does not meet the requirement that the actual specialist carry out its process and return the answer.

choices.text: Use Supervisor with routing to route each request to the relevant collaborator agent.
choices.explanation: The shared entry point can delegate to the appropriate specialist, which can then return the answer.

choices.text: Use Supervisor to collect answers from multiple collaborator agents and have the supervisor produce the final answer.
choices.explanation: This can coordinate information from multiple collaborators, but it does not fit a request that one specialist handles end to end and answers directly.

choices.text: Call both collaborator agents for every inquiry and use whichever answer arrives first.
choices.explanation: The faster agent is not necessarily the specialist for that subject, and this also creates unnecessary inquiries.

source.label: Bedrock Agentsの複数エージェントの設定

learning.reason: The shared entry point delegates to the relevant specialist, which can then return the answer.
learning.concept: Choose direct routing when one specialist can handle the request; use aggregation when results from multiple specialists must be combined.

sourceLabel: Configuring multi-agent collaboration in Bedrock Agents

title: Determine whether a model may have memorized a public benchmark
prompt: You are tuning a foundation model to summarize documents for an internal product. A candidate was trained on data of unknown provenance and scored highly only on a public benchmark. You want to measure improvement on new documents from production without relying on reproducing examples the model may already know. Which should you use for the final evaluation?

choices.text: Hold out new, production-like documents and their expected summaries that were not used for training, freeze the model, and compare it with the previous model on the same inputs.
choices.explanation: This avoids relying on fit to known public benchmark examples and checks performance on the new documents you actually want to compare.

choices.text: Reorder the public benchmark and change its item IDs, then evaluate again on the same examples.
choices.explanation: The source text and expected results remain the same, so this does not address the possibility that the examples were in the training data.

choices.text: Keep the public benchmark result, add production examples to the training data, and then score the model on those same production examples.
choices.explanation: Although these examples resemble production data, the model was trained on them, so this cannot show improvement on unseen examples.

choices.text: Have people rescore the candidate's answers on the same public data and select the candidate whose scores best agree with the human ratings.
choices.explanation: This may improve the judging method, but it does not resolve whether the examples themselves were in the training data.

source.label: 公開条件に対応する評価データの選び方

learning.reason: This avoids relying on fit to known public benchmark examples and checks performance on new documents you actually want to compare.
learning.concept: Changing the split mechanically is not enough; verify that evaluation examples were not visible during training.

sourceLabel: Choosing evaluation data for the disclosure conditions

title: Scores cannot be compared in the evaluation UI even though explanations appear
prompt: For a Bedrock model evaluation, you created a custom metric based on internal criteria for judging descriptions of indoor facilities. The judge model's responses include explanations, but scores are written in free-form text, so the evaluation UI does not aggregate them correctly. What should you fix while keeping the existing metric criteria?

choices.text: Add instructions to the target model's prompt to produce the scoring result too, and leave the evaluator's free-form output unchanged.
choices.explanation: This changes the wrong prompt; the evaluator's results would still be difficult to aggregate.

choices.text: Only lower the evaluator's temperature and keep its explanations in the same free-form format.
choices.explanation: Reducing variation does not make the scores structured so the service can parse them.

choices.text: Use only a built-in general text-quality metric and remove the custom metric based on internal criteria.
choices.explanation: The scores could be aggregated, but the metric would no longer assess the criteria required for this business task.

choices.text: Specify in the scoring instructions the evaluation result format and score scale that Bedrock can recognize.
choices.explanation: The service can extract and aggregate scores and explanations from the evaluator's output while preserving the evaluation criteria.

source.label: モデル評価でのカスタム指標の出力形式

learning.reason: The service can extract and aggregate scores and explanations from the evaluator's output while preserving the evaluation criteria.
learning.concept: Specify both the evaluator's judgment criteria and the score-output contract that the evaluation system must read.

sourceLabel: Output formats for custom metrics in model evaluation

title: Add examples where the same wording represents different intake categories
prompt: Classify inquiries as either “billing inquiry” or “billing correction.” In the existing examples, “I want to check the details” is an inquiry, but even when a correction request immediately follows the same phrase, the classification tends to favor inquiry. The classification specification is fixed: “If there is a specific correction request, classify it as a correction.” How can you improve this without additional training?

choices.text: Add a rule that always classifies the phrase “I want to check the details” as a correction.
choices.explanation: This would change some errors, but inquiries that only ask for confirmation would be incorrectly classified as corrections.

choices.text: Shorten the option names and instruct the model to produce the two options with equal probability.
choices.explanation: Changing the wording and output proportions does not explain which conditions distinguish the categories.

choices.text: State the priority conditions for both labels and add paired examples showing that the same wording receives different labels depending on whether a correction is requested.
choices.explanation: Showing the boundary condition in both the instructions and examples can weaken the association with a frequently occurring phrase alone.

choices.text: Add only typical examples the model already classifies correctly, so the number of inquiry and correction examples is equal.
choices.explanation: Balancing the number of examples does not show the shared wording that causes the error or the boundary for classification.

source.label: Bedrockのプロンプト設計とラベル定義

learning.reason: Showing the boundary condition in both the instructions and examples can weaken the association with a frequently occurring phrase alone.
learning.concept: When the missing piece is a label boundary, state the condition that determines the difference and illustrate it with examples.

sourceLabel: Bedrock prompt design and label definitions

title: Use a customized model for low initial production traffic
prompt: You trained a supported Amazon Bedrock custom model and obtained its custom model ARN. Initial usage is uncertain, and you will not purchase fixed inference capacity. Which configuration lets you use the customization for synchronous inference instead of the foundation model you have been using?

choices.text: Pass the ARN of the completed customization job as the inference model identifier without creating a deployment.
choices.explanation: A training job identifier is not an on-demand inference target.

choices.text: Deploy the custom model for on-demand inference and specify the returned deployment ARN when making inference requests.
choices.explanation: This lets you invoke the customized model without purchasing reserved capacity, instead of using the uncustomized model.

choices.text: Use the ID of the uncustomized foundation model and put the customization job name in a request tag.
choices.explanation: A tag provides identifying information; it does not switch the model weights used for inference.

choices.text: Purchase Provisioned Throughput for the custom model and specify the ARN for that capacity.
choices.explanation: Although this can invoke a supported model, it does not satisfy the requirement to avoid purchasing fixed capacity.

source.label: Bedrockのカスタムモデルのオンデマンド展開

learning.reason: This lets you invoke the customized model without purchasing reserved capacity, instead of using the uncustomized model.
learning.concept: The completed customized model and the inference deployment called by an application are separate resources.

title: Measure cases where only the value passed to the correct tool is wrong
prompt: A reservation-change agent calls the correct reservation-change tool, but sometimes passes a date from an earlier interaction instead of the date specified by the user. Its final response reads naturally, and it rarely chooses the wrong tool. Which evaluation is most direct?

choices.text: Measure tool parameter accuracy to determine whether the arguments in tool calls match the conditions in the conversation.
choices.explanation: Even when the function name is correct, this can check whether the date supplied at runtime matches the user's request.

choices.text: Measure only the proportion of cases where the agent selects a tool name that matches the user's intent.
choices.explanation: The tool name is correct in this failure mode, so this would miss the incorrect value.

choices.text: Evaluate whether the final response to the user is readable and treat the operation as correct if it passes.
choices.explanation: The quality of the prose does not show which value was actually passed.

choices.text: Measure the average tool execution time and treat only short inputs as correct.
choices.explanation: Execution time is a performance metric and does not directly indicate whether the date is correct.

source.label: AgentCoreの組み込み評価指標

learning.reason: Even when the function name is correct, this can check whether the date supplied at runtime matches the user's request.
learning.concept: Tool selection accuracy and the accuracy of the arguments passed to the selected tool can be measured independently.

title: Check a required process order even when the final result is correct
prompt: A quoting assistant must follow the order “inventory lookup → price lookup,” but it may use read-only helper tools in between. You want to detect before release an implementation that looks up the price first, even if the final amount is correct. How should you configure AgentCore Evaluations for a fixed scenario?

choices.text: Treat the run as successful if both required tools are present, regardless of order.
choices.explanation: This would also pass cases in which the tools are called in reverse order.

choices.text: Use an exact match requiring the two tools to appear consecutively, and fail runs with any additional read-only calls.
choices.explanation: This checks the order but also rejects valid cases that use permitted helper tools.

choices.text: Compare the reference amount with the final response and treat every execution order as successful if they match.
choices.explanation: Even if the final result is the same, this cannot detect violations of the required process order.

choices.text: Specify the two expected tools in order and evaluate an order match that permits other calls in between.
choices.explanation: This checks whether the two required tools were called in the required order without penalizing permitted helper operations.

source.label: AgentCoreの期待するツール実行順序

learning.reason: This checks whether the two required tools were called in the required order without penalizing permitted helper operations.
learning.concept: For business steps not represented in the final output, define and check the expected order against the call history.

title: How the number of training epochs affects training cost
prompt: In a Bedrock trial using the same model and training data, the previous run used 2 epochs. There is a proposal to increase this to 4 epochs without checking the budget. Early stopping is not configured, and the processing within each epoch is the same. Which view of the training token volume is correct?

choices.text: Increasing the number of epochs also doubles the inference input context limit for a single invocation.
choices.explanation: Inference capacity and the number of training passes are separate settings.

choices.text: If the learning rate stays the same, data processing after the first epoch is not billable, even with 4 epochs.
choices.explanation: The learning rate controls the size of updates; it does not eliminate data processing in subsequent epochs.

choices.text: The data is processed twice as many times, from 2 passes to 4, so the training token volume processed is approximately doubled even with the same data.
choices.explanation: The entire training dataset is processed in each epoch. The number of epochs affects customization cost.

choices.text: Because the files take up the same storage space, the volume of training tokens processed does not change.
choices.explanation: The amount of data stored differs from the total amount processed during repeated training passes.

source.label: Bedrockのエポックと学習処理量

learning.reason: The entire training dataset is processed in each epoch. The number of epochs affects customization cost.
learning.concept: More customization passes can increase compute without changing the stored size of the data.

title: Evaluating a consultation in which later questions change based on responses
prompt: A booking-assistance agent is being improved. If the customer's initial preference is fully booked, the agent suggests another date, so the customer's subsequent responses vary according to the model's reply. Rather than checking correctness in one fixed exchange, you want to provide the same user profile and goal and verify whether the goal can be achieved through a multi-turn conversation. Which evaluation scenario should you prepare?

choices.text: Measure the latest response time for actual inquiries and consider the user's goal achieved if the response becomes faster.
choices.explanation: This can measure speed, but it cannot determine whether the user was able to select an alternative reservation.

choices.text: Use a simulation that defines the user's background and goal, conduct the conversation, and evaluate whether the goal is achieved.
choices.explanation: This can verify whether the user's goal was reached while changing subsequent utterances according to the responses.

choices.text: Replay predetermined user utterances in the same order and proceed regardless of the agent's responses.
choices.explanation: This is suitable for regression checks along a fixed path, but it cannot test branches based on responses.

choices.text: Evaluate only the initial responses for fully booked and available cases independently, and consider a reservation possible if both are correct.
choices.explanation: This can verify the first response, but not whether a conversation for reconsidering alternative options is completed.

source.label: AgentCore評価のユーザーシミュレーション

learning.reason: This can verify whether the user's goal was reached while changing subsequent utterances according to the responses.
learning.concept: For tasks where subsequent conversational input is unknown, a user can be simulated with fixed starting conditions and a goal.

title: Enabling investigation of a challenged decision
prompt: A user challenges a published application guidance response, saying, “I submitted the same documents but received a different decision last time.” A reviewer needs to compare the guidance provided at the time with the policy, model, and input transformations used, and correct the guidance if needed. User data may be retained only within the prescribed limits. What should be prepared?

choices.text: Reassess the case using the current model and policy, and use only the latest result as evidence for the challenge.
choices.explanation: This verifies the current guidance but cannot investigate why the decision changed under an earlier version.

choices.text: Keep only the model's daily accuracy and the number of inquiries, without linking records to individual decisions.
choices.explanation: This tracks operational trends but cannot reconstruct the specific decision being challenged.

choices.text: Tell users the model name and publish only the latest model card whenever it changes.
choices.explanation: This explains the system but does not let a reviewer investigate the version or basis used for the specific decision.

choices.text: Link each decision to its challenge using identifiers, and let authorized reviewers access the version, input processing, rationale, and minimum necessary result from that time.
choices.explanation: This lets reviewers compare the conditions at the time with the guidance actually provided and specifically reassess the challenged case.

source.label: 推論と利用者からのフィードバックを関連付ける

learning.reason: This lets reviewers compare the conditions at the time with the guidance actually provided and specifically reassess the challenged case.
learning.concept: A challenge requires information that can trace the decision, version, and rationale from that time so it can be individually reassessed.

sourceLabel: Linking inference records with user feedback

title: Deciding whether a small group's results meet the release threshold
prompt: The release criteria for a document intake model require a minimum level of statistical confidence in the accuracy for each target group. Overall performance is high, but the model has only been correct on 3 out of 3 cases in a small group. Which procedure should be used to decide whether to release it?

choices.text: Average the group scores with equal weights and release the model if the overall result exceeds the threshold.
choices.explanation: This can adjust the overall evaluation but does not verify that each group meets the required confidence condition.

choices.text: Duplicate the existing 3 cases repeatedly in the evaluation file to increase the apparent sample size.
choices.explanation: Repeating the same results does not add new independent evidence.

choices.text: Examine the sample size and uncertainty for each group, add representative real examples if needed, and reevaluate the release criteria.
choices.explanation: Do not infer high confidence from a few successes alone; obtain the evidence needed for the specified decision.

choices.text: Because all 3 cases were correct, treat the observed 100% as definitive and release the model.
choices.explanation: Even with a good observed result, the small sample size means there is substantial uncertainty about true performance.

source.label: 公開条件に対する評価データの標本数

learning.reason: Do not infer high confidence from a few successes alone; obtain the evidence needed for the specified decision.
learning.concept: A subgroup's point estimate and the number of independent samples supporting that estimate both inform a release decision.

sourceLabel: Evaluation sample size for release criteria

title: Compare the rate of eligible applicants missed
prompt: The same model routes applications from two regions. In each region, staff confirmed that 80 applications were genuinely eligible. The model identified 72 in Region A and 60 in Region B as eligible. The proportion of all applications predicted to be eligible was the same in both regions, but you want to check whether the model misses eligible applicants at different rates by region. Which metric should you compare?

choices.text: Compare the proportion of all applications in each region that were predicted to be eligible.
choices.explanation: Even when the overall predicted proportions are the same, the proportions of genuinely eligible applicants identified by the model can differ.

choices.text: Compare the proportion of applications predicted to be eligible in each region that were genuinely eligible.
choices.explanation: A difference in precision evaluates how many applicants were incorrectly predicted to be eligible. Missed eligible applicants are not included in this denominator.

choices.text: Compare recall among applications that were genuinely eligible: 90% in Region A and 75% in Region B.
choices.explanation: Using the number of genuinely eligible applications in each region as the denominator measures differences in missed eligible applicants.

choices.text: Check only the combined recall of 82.5% across eligible applications in both regions.
choices.explanation: The combined recall can be calculated, but the aggregate value alone does not show the difference in misses between regions.

source.label: AWSの地域・グループ別の再現率差の解説

learning.reason: Use recall, with genuinely eligible applicants as the denominator, to measure whether the rate of missed eligible applicants differs by region.
learning.concept: Parity in the proportion predicted to be eligible is a different fairness metric from parity in the rate of identifying people who are genuinely eligible.

sourceLabel: AWS guidance on recall differences by region and group

title: Report what watermark detection can establish about audio
prompt: Amazon Nova 2 Sonic is used to provide audio guidance to users. When investigating audio of unknown origin, you are considering whether its transcript alone can show whether a person or AI created the audio. What is the appropriate approach?

choices.text: Check for the relevant model watermark in the audio itself, and avoid drawing a firm conclusion about its origin if the result is negative.
choices.explanation: A watermark in the model's audio is not included in the transcript, and detection applies only to the relevant watermark.

choices.text: If the accompanying transcript has no watermark, conclude that a person spoke the words.
choices.explanation: A transcript from Nova 2 Sonic does not contain the watermark embedded in generated audio.

choices.text: If a watermark is detected, treat the audio's content as accurate and skip content review.
choices.explanation: A watermark is a clue about provenance; it does not guarantee that the spoken content is accurate.

choices.text: Assume the watermark detection result is always consistent, even if the audio has been modified.
choices.explanation: Compression or other processing can weaken a watermark, so detection is uncertain.

source.label: Bedrockの透かしと検出の限界

learning.reason: A watermark in the model's audio is not included in the transcript, and detection applies only to the relevant watermark.
learning.concept: A watermark is a clue about provenance; its presence or absence alone cannot establish authorship, accuracy, or whether the audio was edited.

title: Link records across a safety-scoring rubric revision
prompt: The model in production has not changed, but a quarterly review made the safety rubric stricter for “assertive answers.” Scores fell under the new rubric. The audit must distinguish a change in the rules from a change in the model's actual quality. What should be retained and compared?

choices.text: Compare scores assigned under the latest rubric directly with scores assigned under the previous rubric.
choices.explanation: The scoring conditions differ, so the scores may have changed even if the output quality did not.

choices.text: Normalize scores to a mean of zero for each round and remove the rubric version.
choices.explanation: This may make the scores look aligned, but it prevents tracking what was tightened and breaks the link to the published safety criteria.

choices.text: Keep only the scoring model version, and do not record edits to the safety judgment instructions between rounds.
choices.explanation: Even with the same scoring model, changes to its instructions can change the meaning of the scores.

choices.text: Version the rubric and data, and, when needed, score the same outputs under both the old and new rubrics.
choices.explanation: Holding the outputs fixed makes it possible to identify the score difference caused by changing only the evaluation rules.

source.label: 生成出力の評価基準と採点の版管理

learning.reason: Holding the outputs fixed makes it possible to identify the score difference caused by changing only the evaluation rules.
learning.concept: Safety evaluations require the evaluation model, data, and judgment criteria to be managed so they can be compared.

sourceLabel: Versioning evaluation criteria and scores for generative outputs

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Set an organization-wide permission ceiling on the data owner's side
prompt: An organization member account contains S3 data for AI training. You want permissions to that data to remain ineffective unless the principal is approved as an exception, even if an individual bucket policy mistakenly allows an external principal. Which feature can the data-owning organization apply organization-wide?

choices.text: Use a permissions boundary for users in the organization and assume the same ceiling applies to external principals.
choices.explanation: A boundary applies to the permissions of the IAM principal to which it is attached. It cannot be attached to principals outside the organization.

choices.text: Review all bucket allow policies together once a month and correct any mistakes when found.
choices.explanation: This is a retrospective review, not a preventive control that makes external access ineffective as soon as an individual policy is misconfigured.

choices.text: Apply a Resource Control Policy (RCP) to place a ceiling on external principals' access to the S3 resources in scope.
choices.explanation: An RCP applies in resource-side permission evaluation, so its higher-level restriction applies even when an individual policy allows access.

choices.text: Use only a Service Control Policy (SCP) for organization principals to restrict access to the target buckets by principals outside the organization.
choices.explanation: An SCP controls the permission ceiling for principals in the organization; it does not constrain external principals on the resource side.

source.label: AWS OrganizationsのRCPとリソースの権限

learning.reason: An RCP applies in resource-side permission evaluation, so its higher-level restriction applies even when an individual policy allows access.
learning.concept: An SCP sets a permissions ceiling on the principal side, while an RCP sets one on supported resources.

sourceLabel: AWS Organizations RCPs and resource permissions

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Attach a human-approved evaluation report to the applicable audit control
prompt: You are verifying production approval for a model in AWS Audit Manager. AWS usage records have already been collected automatically, and an independent evaluator’s approved risk assessment PDF is stored in S3. You want auditors to review it alongside the automatically collected evidence as documentation for the same control. What should you do?

choices.text: Copy the file to a separate S3 prefix as an uncategorized attachment, without recording its association with the evaluation item.
choices.explanation: The file can be stored, but auditors cannot trace it as evidence for the applicable control.

choices.text: Ingest the evaluation PDF from S3 as manual evidence for the applicable control.
choices.explanation: Review materials that cannot be collected automatically from AWS services can be linked directly to the control being assessed.

choices.text: Collect only the access records for the evaluation PDF with CloudTrail, without attaching the PDF to the control.
choices.explanation: You can confirm that someone read the file, but the document showing the approval is not linked to the control.

choices.text: Collect new automated evidence in Audit Manager using only AWS Config, then reconstruct the PDF’s contents from that evidence.
choices.explanation: Configuration assessments and internal evaluation reports are different; Config cannot collect the approval result.

source.label: AWS Audit Managerで手動の証跡を追加する

learning.reason: Review materials that cannot be collected automatically from AWS services can be linked directly to the control being assessed.
learning.concept: Bring together AWS evidence that can be collected automatically and organizational evaluation and approval materials that must be attached individually, at the control level.

sourceLabel: Adding manual evidence in AWS Audit Manager

category: AIのセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Require consistent governance information for each catalog asset
prompt: AI training data published in Amazon DataZone must include the owning department, a contact, and terms of use. Important information is often omitted when it is entered freely in a descriptive text field, and you cannot change the source data’s columns. Which approach lets you use the same fields for the applicable asset type?

choices.text: Define required fields in a metadata form and use it with the applicable data asset type.
choices.explanation: This provides the same fields in the asset catalog and lets you make each field mandatory.

choices.text: Add the meanings of owning department and contact to the business glossary, and leave each asset’s entries in an optional description field.
choices.explanation: You can standardize definitions, but you cannot make each asset’s contact or terms of use mandatory fields.

choices.text: Collect owner information only through the subscription request form, leaving the original asset metadata empty.
choices.explanation: This collects information at request time, but does not ensure that governance information is present for each asset.

choices.text: Add owning department, contact, and terms-of-use columns to each source data record.
choices.explanation: This structures the information, but violates the constraint that the source data’s columns cannot be changed.

source.label: DataZoneのメタデータフォームの必須項目

learning.reason: This provides the same fields in the asset catalog and lets you make each field mandatory.
learning.concept: Use different features to standardize the meaning of terms and to require values for each asset.

sourceLabel: Required fields in DataZone metadata forms
